sops.title: Host Stand Opening SOP
sops.frequency: Before every opening period and again before any major shift change or high-volume reservation block.
sops.role: The opening host completes the setup. The manager on duty verifies readiness before the first guest is seated.
sops.purpose: To prepare the host stand, entrance, reservation tools, seating plan, and guest-arrival area before the restaurant opens.
steps: Clock in and review the manager communication log, reservation notes, events, promotions, and expected business level.
Inspect the entrance, lobby, door glass, floor, mats, signage, lighting, and guest path; correct or report problems.
Clean and organize the host stand. Remove outdated papers, menus, signs, and personal items.
Power on and test the phone, reservation system, waitlist system, pagers, tablets, radios, and charging equipment.
Count and organize menus, children's menus, drink menus, and other approved materials.
Review the floor plan, server sections, closed sections, reserved tables, large-party setups, and accessibility seating options.
Confirm which tables are clean, stable, correctly set, and approved for seating.
Review expected reservations and note birthdays, special requests, mobility needs, or manager follow-up.
Confirm the approved opening greeting, wait-time communication process, and manager escalation method.
Notify the manager when the host stand and guest-arrival area are ready for opening.
sops.checks:
□ Entrance and host stand are clean, organized, and guest-ready.
□ Reservation and waitlist technology is working.
□ Current floor plan and server sections are available.
□ Menus and guest materials are current and sufficient.
□ Accessibility routes and seating options are known.
□ Opening host can explain escalation and seating-decision authority.
sops.correction:
• Opening without reviewing reservations or section changes.
• Leaving outdated signs, menus, or handwritten notes visible to guests.
• Failing to test phones, pagers, or reservation equipment.
• Seating before tables, paths, or accessibility needs are verified.
• Not informing the manager about equipment, cleanliness, or staffing problems.
sops.records:
• Current floor plan and server section map
• Reservation and waitlist system
• Menus, children's menus, accessibility information, and promotional materials
• Charged phone, radio, tablet, pager, or other communication device
• Clean host stand supplies and manager notes

sops.title: Host Stand Closing SOP
sops.frequency: At the end of the final seating period or when the manager releases the host position.
sops.role: The closing host completes the process. The closing manager verifies equipment, records, lost items, and final building condition.
sops.purpose: To close, clean, secure, document, and prepare the host stand and guest-arrival area for the next operating period.
steps: Confirm with the manager that seating is closed or that the host position may be released.
Review the remaining guest count, open tables, late reservations, waiting parties, and expected pickups.
Finish greeting, departure recognition, phone coverage, and guest assistance until reassigned.
Close the waitlist and reservation day according to the approved system process.
Document no-shows, late cancellations, special requests, and manager follow-up items.
Collect menus, wipe approved surfaces, organize supplies, and remove trash from the host area.
Inspect the lobby, entry path, door area, and seating equipment; clean or report anything unfinished.
Process found property according to the lost-and-found SOP.
Charge, secure, or power down phones, tablets, pagers, radios, and other equipment.
Give the manager a final handoff and obtain closing verification before leaving.
sops.checks:
□ No waiting guests, reservations, or late arrivals are unaccounted for.
□ Guest and employee information is secured.
□ Equipment is charged, powered down, or stored correctly.
□ Host stand, lobby, and entry area are clean.
□ Lost property and unresolved issues are documented.
□ Manager receives a complete closing handoff.
sops.correction:
• Closing the stand while guests still need assistance.
• Leaving reservation information or guest phone numbers visible.
• Failing to charge or secure host equipment.
• Discarding found property or failing to log it.
• Leaving the manager without information about no-shows, complaints, or late parties.
sops.records:
• Closing checklist
• Reservation and waitlist system
• Lost-and-found container or log
• Cleaning supplies approved for the host area
• Charging cords, key storage, and manager communication log

sops.title: Guest Greeting and Acknowledgment SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest enters, approaches the host stand, calls for arrival assistance, or appears uncertain about where to go.
sops.role: The host leads the greeting. Every employee shares responsibility for immediate acknowledgment when the host is occupied.
sops.purpose: To make every arriving guest feel noticed, welcomed, and professionally guided from the moment they enter.
steps: Stop nonessential conversation and make eye contact with the arriving guest.
Offer the approved greeting and welcome the party to the restaurant.
Ask how many guests are in the party and whether they have a reservation.
Confirm the reservation name, party size, or walk-in status without announcing private information loudly.
Ask whether the party has accessibility, child-seating, high-chair, booster, or other seating needs.
Check table availability, reservation timing, server rotation, and manager restrictions.
If immediate seating is available, explain the next step and escort the party.
If a wait is necessary, quote the approved wait time and explain how updates will be provided.
If delayed by another task, acknowledge the guest and state that someone will assist them shortly.
Thank the guest for arriving and maintain professional attention until the handoff is complete.
sops.checks:
□ Employee acknowledges arriving guests promptly.
□ Approved greeting is used naturally and professionally.
□ Reservation and party information is confirmed accurately.
□ Accessibility and seating needs are asked respectfully.
□ Wait or seating next steps are clear.
□ Employee knows when to involve the manager.
sops.correction:
• Ignoring guests while finishing a personal conversation or looking at a screen.
• Pointing toward a table instead of guiding the guest.
• Using casual, dismissive, or overly familiar language.
• Announcing guest names, phone numbers, or special requests loudly.
• Giving an unrealistic wait time to avoid a difficult conversation.

• Current floor plan and table-status information
• Manager communication method

sops.title: Seating Rotation SOP
sops.frequency: During all seating periods, especially rushes, shift changes, reservation blocks, and large-party arrivals.
sops.role: The host follows the approved rotation. The manager authorizes major rotation changes, section closures, large-party placement, or intentional double-seating.
sops.purpose: To seat guests fairly and efficiently while balancing server workload, reservations, table availability, and guest needs.
steps: Review active server sections and confirm which servers are ready to receive tables.
Identify closed tables, reserved tables, large-party setups, accessibility seating, and temporary restrictions.
Use the approved rotation to select the next eligible section.
Confirm the selected table is clean, set, safe, and appropriate for the party size.
Consider the server's current workload, recent seating, and ability to provide timely service.
Seat the party and update the chart, system, or rotation tracker immediately.
Communicate special requests, accessibility needs, children, celebrations, or time-sensitive concerns to the server.
When guests request a specific table or server, adjust the rotation fairly and document the change.
Do not double-seat or overload a section without approval unless immediate action is required for guest safety or service recovery.
Notify the manager when seating flow, kitchen capacity, or server workload requires a larger adjustment.
sops.checks:
□ Host understands active sections and rotation order.
□ Table status is updated immediately after seating.
□ Guest and accessibility needs are considered.
□ Server workload is monitored.
□ Rotation changes are fair and communicated.
□ Host asks the manager for help before service is damaged.
sops.correction:
• Skipping servers without a documented reason.
• Repeatedly double-seating one section.
• Seating dirty or unapproved tables.
• Failing to update the seating chart.
• Ignoring kitchen capacity, large parties, or reservation commitments.

• Waitlist and table-status system
• Manager seating notes

sops.title: Waitlist Management SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever immediate seating is unavailable or when the manager activates a waitlist.
sops.role: The host maintains accurate entries and updates. The manager controls major quote changes, seating pauses, and guest-recovery decisions.
sops.purpose: To organize waiting parties, provide honest time expectations, protect guest information, and seat parties in a fair and controlled order.
steps: Confirm the party size, preferred name, contact method, seating needs, and whether all party members must be present.
Check current table status, reservation commitments, server capacity, kitchen conditions, and manager quote guidance.
Provide the approved estimated wait time and explain that timing may change.
Enter the party accurately into the waitlist and repeat the information for confirmation.
Explain where the party may wait, how notification will occur, and the grace period after notification.
Update table status and wait estimates as parties are seated, tables are reset, or service conditions change.
Provide reasonable updates to waiting guests, especially when the estimate changes materially.
Notify parties using the approved method and record the notification time.
If the party does not respond, follow the grace-period and second-contact process before removal.
Escalate disputes, long delays, accessibility concerns, or service-recovery needs to the manager.
sops.checks:
□ Entries include correct party size and contact information.
□ Wait quotes reflect current operations.
□ Guests receive clear notification and grace-period instructions.
□ Waitlist order and exceptions follow policy.
□ Updates are communicated when conditions change.
□ Private guest information is not exposed.
sops.correction:
• Giving an exact promise instead of an estimate.
• Adding the wrong party size or phone number.
• Removing parties too quickly.
• Failing to update guests when the wait increases.
• Allowing friends, regulars, or demanding guests to bypass policy without manager approval.

• Approved waitlist system
• Current floor plan and table status
• Guest notification device or method
• Reservation schedule
• Manager escalation process

sops.title: Reservation Handling SOP
sops.frequency: When a reservation is requested, confirmed, modified, canceled, checked in, or marked as a no- show.
sops.role: The employee entering the reservation verifies all details. The manager approves exceptions, large parties, deposits, special seating promises, or capacity overrides.
sops.purpose: To accept, confirm, update, seat, and document reservations accurately while protecting restaurant capacity and guest expectations.
steps: Ask for the reservation date, preferred time, party size, guest name, and contact information.
Check availability, pacing rules, special events, section restrictions, and large-party limits.
Explain available times and any deposit, cancellation, arrival, seating, or time-limit policy.
Enter the reservation and repeat the date, time, party size, name, and contact information for confirmation.
Record accessibility needs, allergies, high chairs, celebrations, mobility concerns, or other relevant notes.
Do not promise a specific table or area without manager authorization.
For changes, verify the guest identity and update every affected field.
Send or provide the approved confirmation and arrival instructions.
At check-in, confirm the name and party status, then update the reservation system.
Document cancellations, no-shows, late arrivals, and manager-approved exceptions.
sops.checks:
□ Reservation details are complete and repeated back.
□ Capacity and pacing rules are followed.
□ Special needs and important notes are visible to the correct team.
□ Unauthorized promises are not made.
□ Changes and cancellations are recorded immediately.
□ Guest information is protected.
sops.correction:
• Entering the wrong date, time, or party size.
• Promising a specific table without approval.
• Failing to document accessibility or allergy information.
• Overbooking without manager direction.
• Discussing guest contact or payment information where others can hear.
sops.records:
• Reservation system or approved reservation book
• Capacity and floor-plan rules
• Large-party and deposit policies
• Special-event schedule
• Manager contact method

sourceSections.purpose: To accept, confirm, update, seat, and document reservations accurately while protecting restaurant capacity and guest expectations.
sourceSections.appliesTo: Hosts, reservation agents, managers, and employees authorized to create or change reservations.
sourceSections.responsibility: The employee entering the reservation verifies all details. The manager approves exceptions, large parties, deposits, special seating promises, or capacity overrides.
sourceSections.whenUsed: When a reservation is requested, confirmed, modified, canceled, checked in, or marked as a no- show.
sourceSections.materials:
• Reservation system or approved reservation book
• Capacity and floor-plan rules
• Large-party and deposit policies
• Special-event schedule
• Manager contact method
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• No seating location, table number, exact timing, or special request is guaranteed unless authorized.
• Guest names, phone numbers, payment details, and notes are protected.
• Changes are documented immediately.
• Large parties, accessibility needs, allergies, celebrations, and time constraints are clearly noted and communicated.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Ask for the reservation date, preferred time, party size, guest name, and contact information.
2. Check availability, pacing rules, special events, section restrictions, and large-party limits.
3. Explain available times and any deposit, cancellation, arrival, seating, or time-limit policy.
4. Enter the reservation and repeat the date, time, party size, name, and contact information for confirmation.
5. Record accessibility needs, allergies, high chairs, celebrations, mobility concerns, or other relevant notes.
6. Do not promise a specific table or area without manager authorization.
7. For changes, verify the guest identity and update every affected field.
8. Send or provide the approved confirmation and arrival instructions.
9. At check-in, confirm the name and party status, then update the reservation system.
10. Document cancellations, no-shows, late arrivals, and manager-approved exceptions.
sourceSections.managerVerification:
□ Reservation details are complete and repeated back.
□ Capacity and pacing rules are followed.
□ Special needs and important notes are visible to the correct team.
□ Unauthorized promises are not made.
□ Changes and cancellations are recorded immediately.
□ Guest information is protected.
sourceSections.commonMistakes:
• Entering the wrong date, time, or party size.
• Promising a specific table without approval.
• Failing to document accessibility or allergy information.
• Overbooking without manager direction.
• Discussing guest contact or payment information where others can hear.

sops.title: Phone Answering SOP
sops.frequency: During all posted phone-answering hours and whenever the restaurant line rings while staff are present.
sops.role: The assigned employee answers and routes calls. The manager handles complaints, sensitive employee matters, media calls, emergencies, and policy exceptions.
sops.purpose: To answer restaurant calls promptly, professionally, accurately, and consistently while protecting guest information and avoiding operational disruption.
steps: Answer within the restaurant's approved ring standard whenever possible.
Use the approved greeting and speak clearly at a professional volume.
Ask how you may help and listen without interrupting.
Confirm the purpose of the call before transferring or placing the caller on hold.
Ask permission before placing the caller on hold and return within the approved time.
Provide only current, approved information about hours, location, menu, reservations, events, and policies.
For messages, record the caller name, number, reason, time, urgency, and intended recipient.
Do not provide employee schedules, personal contact information, guest information, or internal security details.
Escalate complaints, legal threats, media requests, emergencies, suspicious calls, and sensitive employee matters to the manager.
Close the call by confirming the next step and thanking the caller.
sops.checks:
□ Employee uses the approved greeting.
□ Calls are answered or returned within the standard.
□ Hold and transfer procedures are professional.
□ Messages are complete and legible.
□ Confidential information is protected.
□ Employee recognizes calls requiring manager escalation.
sops.correction:
• Answering with only "hello" or using an unprofessional tone.
• Leaving callers on hold without returning.
• Giving outdated hours or policy information.
• Sharing employee schedules or personal information.
• Arguing with a caller instead of escalating.
sops.records:
• Working phone and charger
• Approved greeting
• Current hours, directions, menu, reservation, and to-go information
• Message form or system
• Manager contact method

sops.title: Guest Seating and Escort SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a party is seated in the dining room, bar, patio, private room, or other approved area.
sops.role: The seating employee verifies the table and escorts the party. The manager resolves unsafe seating, accessibility, section, or guest-request conflicts.
sops.purpose: To escort guests safely and professionally from the host stand to an approved, ready table while communicating essential information to the service team.
steps: Confirm the selected table is clean, fully set, stable, and approved for the party size.
Gather the correct number and type of menus or guest materials.
Invite the party to follow and identify the area where they are being seated.
Choose the safest, clearest path and walk at a comfortable pace.
Monitor that children, older guests, and guests with mobility needs remain with the party.
Assist with chairs, high chairs, boosters, or accessibility arrangements according to policy.
Present the table and allow guests to settle before distributing menus.
Confirm that the seating arrangement is acceptable without pressuring the guest.
Inform the server or section team that the party is seated and communicate important notes.
Update the seating system or chart immediately.
sops.checks:
□ Table and path are checked before escorting.
□ Guest pace and accessibility needs are respected.
□ Menus and seating equipment are correct.
□ Host remains with the party until seated.
□ Server is informed promptly.
□ Seating chart is updated immediately.
sops.correction:
• Pointing to a table instead of escorting.
• Walking too quickly or leaving part of the party behind.
• Seating at an unclean or unstable table.
• Blocking walkways with high chairs or mobility devices.
• Failing to tell the server that the table has been seated.
sops.records:
• Menus and approved guest materials
• Current table and section status
• Accessibility route knowledge
• High chairs, boosters, or other approved seating equipment

sops.title: Accessibility Seating and Accommodation SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest requests an accommodation or an access need becomes apparent during arrival, seating, or service.
sops.role: The host offers available options. The manager handles complex requests, conflicts, unavailable accommodations, or safety concerns.
sops.purpose: To respond respectfully and effectively to seating and access needs without assumptions, embarrassment, delay, or unsafe arrangements.
steps: Acknowledge the request and ask what seating or assistance would work best.
Review available accessible tables, routes, entrances, and restroom access.
Offer practical options without describing the request loudly or drawing unnecessary attention.
Do not touch, lean on, move, or separate mobility devices or personal assistance equipment without permission.
Maintain clear aisles and emergency exits when adjusting tables or chairs.
If a requested table is unavailable, explain available alternatives and involve the manager.
Communicate only necessary information to the server or manager.
Allow additional time for seating and do not rush the guest or party.
Follow restaurant policy and applicable accessibility requirements regarding service animals and reasonable accommodations.
Document unresolved issues or operational barriers for manager follow-up.
sops.checks:
□ Employee asks rather than assumes.
□ Accessible routes and seating are known.
□ Guest equipment is respected.
□ Information is communicated discreetly.
□ Manager is involved when options are limited.
□ Barriers or unresolved concerns are documented.
sops.correction:
• Assuming a guest needs help without asking.
• Speaking to a companion instead of the guest.
• Moving a wheelchair, walker, or other device without permission.
• Blocking aisles or exits to create a quick seating arrangement.
• Refusing a request without manager review.
sops.records:
• Knowledge of accessible entrances, routes, tables, and restrooms
• Approved accommodation policy
• Portable seating equipment if applicable
• Manager contact method

sops.title: Large Party Seating SOP
sops.frequency: For parties meeting the restaurant's large-party threshold or requiring multiple tables, special setup, deposits, contracts, or dedicated staffing.
sops.role: The manager approves the table plan, server assignment, timing, and exceptions. The host controls arrival, check-in, and seating communication.
sops.purpose: To plan and seat large parties safely, fairly, and efficiently without disrupting reservations, server workload, kitchen capacity, or nearby guests.
steps: Review the reservation, party size, arrival time, seating needs, payment plan, and special requests.
Confirm the approved table layout, aisle clearance, accessibility, and service path.
Verify server assignment, support staff, menu restrictions, and kitchen readiness.
Prepare menus, place settings, child seating, celebration items, and approved signs before arrival.
At check-in, confirm the party name, final size, arrival status, and whether seating requirements are met.
Communicate delays or incomplete-party rules clearly and respectfully.
Seat the party using the approved route and help organize seating without creating congestion.
Introduce the primary server or manager when required.
Update the reservation and seating systems and notify the kitchen or bar of the arrival.
Document material changes, no-shows, policy exceptions, or guest concerns.
sops.checks:
□ Table layout is approved and safe.
□ Server and kitchen capacity are confirmed.
□ Party policies are explained accurately.
□ Required setup is complete before seating.
□ Arrival and communication are organized.
□ Exceptions are documented and manager-approved.
sops.correction:
• Combining tables in a way that blocks aisles or exits.
• Seating without confirming server or kitchen readiness.
• Making up deposit, gratuity, or time-limit rules.
• Failing to communicate a party-size change.
• Allowing a large party to overwhelm one server without support.
sops.records:
• Reservation details and contact information
• Approved floor plan and table-combination rules
• Large-party policy
• Server assignment and kitchen communication plan
• High chairs, boosters, accessibility equipment, or event materials

sops.title: Table Assignment and Section Balancing SOP
sops.frequency: Before opening, at shift change, when staffing changes, or whenever sections must be adjusted during service.
sops.role: The manager approves the floor plan and major changes. The host maintains the working assignment and communicates real-time conditions.
sops.purpose: To assign available tables and sections in a way that supports fair workload, timely service, reservations, staffing, and guest needs.
steps: Review scheduled servers, arrival times, training status, and planned cuts.
Review reservations, expected sales, large parties, patio conditions, and special events.
Assign sections with comparable opportunity and manageable travel distance when possible.
Identify tables requiring experienced coverage, accessibility access, or special handling.
Mark closed, held, or unavailable tables clearly.
Review assignments with servers and confirm understanding.
Adjust assignments when call-offs, cuts, guest flow, or service problems change capacity.
Communicate every change to hosts, servers, service assistants, kitchen leadership, and managers as needed.
Update the floor plan immediately.
Record major recurring imbalance or layout problems for future planning. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Assignments match staffing and demand.
□ Sections are balanced and clearly marked.
□ Special areas have appropriate coverage.
□ Employees receive changes promptly.
□ Floor plan remains current.
□ Manager reviews recurring section or workload problems.
sops.correction:
• Creating sections based on favoritism.
• Giving a trainee an unmanageable section.
• Changing sections without telling the host or server.
• Leaving inaccessible or unavailable tables open in the system.
• Failing to rebalance after cuts or call-offs.
sops.records:
• Floor plan
• Employee schedule
• Reservation forecast
• Table capacity and accessibility information
• Manager labor and service notes

sops.title: Child Seating Equipment and Safety SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a party requests a high chair, booster, sling, or other approved child-seating aid.
sops.role: The employee providing the equipment inspects and places it. The manager removes damaged equipment from use and resolves unsafe placement.
sops.purpose: To provide clean, stable, correctly placed high chairs, boosters, and other approved child-seating equipment while protecting aisles and guest safety.

Select equipment that is clean, dry, stable, and appropriate for the requested use.
Inspect straps, buckles, feet, joints, trays, and surfaces for damage or missing parts.
Clean and sanitize according to the approved chemical and contact-time procedure.
Place the equipment at an approved table location that does not block traffic or exits.
Explain any restaurant policy regarding use, placement, or securing the child.
Allow the adult guest to position or secure the child unless assistance is requested and policy allows.
Remove damaged equipment from service immediately and notify the manager.
After use, clean, sanitize, dry, and return the equipment to approved storage.
Document recurring damage, shortages, or unsafe placement concerns. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Aisles and exits remain clear.
□ Damaged equipment is removed and reported.
□ Adult supervision responsibility is respected.
□ Equipment is stored clean and dry.
sops.correction:
• Using a high chair with broken straps or unstable feet.
• Placing equipment in a service aisle or exit path.
• Using a chair or overturned booster as a carrier stand.
• Returning dirty equipment to storage.
• Failing to report missing or damaged parts.

sops.title: Lost and Found Intake SOP

steps: Do not leave the found item unattended or continue carrying it through the restaurant.
Notify the manager or designated custodian immediately.

Transfer cash, identification, cards, medication, keys, electronics, weapons, or high-value items directly to the manager.

Do not mail, ship, or release items to another person without manager approval.
Follow the restaurant retention and disposal policy for unclaimed items. CUSTOMIZATION

• Leaving found property at the host stand.
• Describing the item in detail to an unverified caller.
• Returning an item without documentation.

sops.title: Weather-Related Entry and Patio Guest Management SOP
sops.frequency: Before opening and whenever weather conditions change or affect guest safety, comfort, access, or table availability.
sops.role: The manager decides patio closure, seating pauses, relocation, and emergency action. The host communicates approved options and maintains safe entry flow.
sops.purpose: To protect guests and operations when rain, wind, heat, cold, lightning, ice, smoke, or other weather affects the entrance, waiting area, or patio.
steps: Review weather conditions and manager patio guidance before opening.
Inspect entry mats, drainage, doors, umbrellas, patio furniture, heaters, fans, and lighting.
Place approved mats and signs where moisture or ice may create a hazard.
Advise arriving guests when patio availability is uncertain or weather-dependent.
Monitor conditions and report rapid changes immediately.

Coordinate relocation of seated guests according to table availability and manager priority.
Keep entry doors, exits, accessibility routes, and emergency paths clear during crowding.
Document damaged equipment, guest incidents, or reservations materially affected by weather.
Reopen the patio only after manager inspection and approval. Management SOP - VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Systems and floor plans are updated.
□ Patio reopens only after inspection.
sops.correction:
• Continuing patio seating after unsafe conditions begin.
• Failing to update quoted wait times after losing patio capacity.
• Moving guests without coordinating table and server capacity.
• Leaving wet floors unmarked.
• Allowing furniture or umbrellas to remain unsecured in wind.

sops.title: Host Shift Handoff SOP
sops.frequency: At scheduled host changes, breaks, cuts, meal periods, or emergency position changes.
sops.role: The outgoing host gives a complete handoff. The incoming host confirms understanding and immediately assumes control of the position.
sops.purpose: To transfer accurate guest, reservation, waitlist, table, equipment, and manager information between host employees without service interruption.
steps: Notify the manager or lead host that a handoff is beginning.
Review current waiting parties, quoted times, contact status, and special needs.
Review upcoming, late, canceled, and no-show reservations.
Review table status, server rotation, cuts, section changes, held tables, and large-party plans.
Identify complaints, VIPs, accessibility requests, weather issues, and manager follow-up.
Count and transfer pagers, radios, keys, tablets, phones, and other controlled items.
Show the incoming host unresolved equipment, cleanliness, or facility concerns.
The incoming host checks the systems and repeats critical information back.
Update the log with the handoff time and both employee names.
Do not leave until the incoming host accepts control or the manager approves release. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Floor plan and rotation are current.
□ Special guest and manager notes are transferred.
□ Equipment and keys are accounted for.
□ Handoff is documented.
sops.correction:
• Leaving for a break before the incoming host is ready.
• Giving only a general summary such as "everything is fine."
• Failing to mention a late large party or long-wait complaint.
• Discussing private guest notes loudly.
• Not counting controlled equipment.

Wash hands and gather only approved cleaning and stocking supplies.

Test the POS login, printer, handheld, and payment equipment assigned to the station.

sops.frequency: Immediately after seating and again when a delayed server assumes the table.
sops.role: The assigned server owns the greeting. A covering employee or manager greets when the server is delayed.
sops.purpose: To acknowledge and welcome every newly seated table promptly while establishing the service plan for the meal.

Ask whether the table has immediate questions or allergy concerns.

Enter urgent beverage or allergy information without unnecessary delay.
Return as promised and continue service or transfer ownership clearly. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:

□ Beverages and important menu information are offered.
□ Questions and allergy concerns are handled without guessing.

□ Order is submitted only after discrepancies are resolved.

• Treating a complex order as obvious because it is familiar.

• Sending the order while still uncertain about a required choice.

sops.title: Course Timing and Firing SOP
sops.frequency: For multi-course meals, held entrées, large parties, shared items, and any timing adjustment.
sops.role: The server communicates the guest pace and enters approved timing instructions. Expo and kitchen control production release.
sops.purpose: To coordinate order release so each course arrives at the intended pace, temperature, and sequence.
steps: Identify the table's preferred pace and any fixed timing needs.
Enter appetizers, entrées, desserts, and shared items in the correct courses.
Use approved hold or fire functions instead of vague free-text notes.

Monitor when the current course is delivered and how quickly the table progresses.
Clear or prepare the table before requesting the next course.
Fire the next course at the approved point based on kitchen lead time.

□ Refires and significant failures are escalated.

• Using "hold" with no clear release plan.
• Firing entrées before appetizers are delivered or cleared.
• Trying to slow service by leaving completed food in the window.
• Failing to tell the kitchen when guests leave the table temporarily.
• Promising an exact time without checking production conditions.

sops.role: The delivering employee verifies the beverage and guest position. The assigned server owns follow-up.
sops.purpose: To deliver the correct beverage to the correct guest promptly, safely, and with the required accompaniments.
steps: Compare each beverage to the ticket, modifiers, and assigned seat.
Inspect glassware, garnish, temperature, fill level, and visible cleanliness.
Use a tray or approved carrier when quantity or conditions require it.
Approach safely and identify the correct guest without reaching across others.
Place the beverage securely with the required napkin, coaster, straw, or accompaniment.
State the beverage when clarification is helpful, especially for similar drinks.
Remove empty or unwanted glassware only after confirming with the guest.
Ask whether anything else is needed and note refill expectations.
Correct an inaccurate or unacceptable beverage promptly through the proper station.
Report spills, breakage, delayed drinks, or alcohol concerns to the assigned server or manager. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Tray and safe placement practices are used.
□ Alcohol-service requirements are satisfied.
□ Required accompaniments are present.
□ Errors, spills, and delays receive immediate follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Auctioning several similar beverages with no seat reference.
• Carrying more drinks than can be controlled safely.
• Touching rims, straws, or drinking surfaces.
• Delivering alcohol before required identification is complete.
• Leaving a spill or broken-glass area without guarding it.

□ Check-back occurs early enough for effective recovery.

sops.frequency: Continuously from seating through check presentation and departure.
sops.role: The assigned server owns table condition. Supporting employees maintain it and communicate unresolved needs.
sops.purpose: To keep the table clean, organized, and properly supplied throughout the meal without interrupting the guest experience.

Ask permission when it is not clear whether a guest is finished.
Remove empty glassware, used plates, wrappers, and unneeded service items promptly.
Clear from the approved side and avoid reaching across guests whenever possible.
Use trays or approved methods; do not scrape or stack noisily at the table.
Replace needed utensils, napkins, share plates, or condiments before the next course.
Wipe crumbs or small spills using the approved method without contaminating food.
Keep chairs, aisles, and the area below the table free of service hazards.
Coordinate with service assistants so work is completed without duplication.
Perform a final table reset for dessert, check presentation, or guest departure. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Team members communicate unfinished table needs.
sops.correction:
• Removing a plate while another guest is still eating when policy discourages it.
• Stacking dirty dishes in front of guests.
• Reaching across faces, drinks, or hot food.
• Using a dirty towel on the tabletop.
• Walking past a spill because the table belongs to another server.

sops.role: The assigned server owns refill timing and pricing communication. Supporting employees follow the same standard.

Do not combine different products or pour into visibly contaminated glassware.
Monitor alcohol consumption and pause service when responsible-service concerns appear.

Update the assigned server when another employee provides a refill.
Escalate repeated delays, spills, guest objections, or alcohol concerns to the manager. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Supporting employees communicate completed refills.

• Waiting for guests to wave down the server.
• Charging for a refill without explaining the policy.
• Topping off the wrong beverage or mixing products.
• Refilling alcohol automatically.
• Leaving multiple empty glasses crowded on the table.

sops.title: Check Presentation SOP
sops.frequency: When requested, at the restaurant's normal service point, or before a known departure deadline.
sops.role: The assigned server reviews and presents the check. Managers approve corrections, discounts, or disputed charges.
sops.purpose: To present an accurate check at the right time while preserving guest control, privacy, and service continuity.
steps: Confirm the table is ready for the check or has requested it.
Review table number, guest count, items, quantities, seats, and transferred charges.
Verify approved discounts, coupons, gift cards, comps, taxes, gratuities, and service charges.
Resolve open items, duplicate charges, or missing approvals before printing or sending.
Place the check in the approved presenter or activate the approved digital method.
Present it discreetly to the requesting guest or agreed payer.
Explain unusual charges, service fees, or split arrangements when needed.
Remain available without hovering or signaling that the table must leave.
Correct a questioned charge promptly and involve the manager when authorization is required.
Continue refills, clearing, and farewell service until the table departs. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Check matches the correct table and guest count.
□ Items, quantities, and seat assignments are accurate.
□ Discounts, fees, taxes, and gratuities are correct.
□ Presentation is discreet and properly timed.
□ Questions and errors receive prompt response.
□ Service continues after check presentation.
sops.correction:
• Dropping the check without reviewing it.
• Presenting the check before the table is ready.
• Failing to explain an automatic gratuity or service charge.
• Arguing about a charge instead of verifying it.
• Treating check presentation as the end of service.

• Current POS check and seat detail
• Approved check presenter or digital payment device

sops.title: Payment Collection SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever cash, card, gift card, mobile, or other approved payment is presented.
sops.role: The employee accepting payment maintains control until it is processed and returned. Managers resolve exceptions.
sops.purpose: To receive and process guest payment promptly while maintaining custody, accuracy, privacy, and respectful communication.
steps: Acknowledge the payment promptly and confirm which check or amount it covers.
Keep payment inside the approved presenter or controlled method while transporting it.
Separate multiple payments and label their intended amounts before processing.
Use the correct tender key and approved device for each payment type.
Remain with a guest-owned mobile device; do not take it out of the guest's control.
Follow the specific cash, card, gift card, or split-payment SOP as applicable.
Verify approval, amount, balance due, and receipt before leaving the terminal.
Return card, change, gift card, and receipts promptly to the correct guest.
Handle declines or discrepancies discreetly and request another form without accusation.
Notify the manager of repeated failures, disputed amounts, suspected fraud, or lost payment. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Payment is applied to the correct check and amount.
□ Payment remains secure from collection through return.
□ Approved terminal and tender procedures are used.
□ Receipt, change, card, and remaining balance are accurate.
□ Declines and disputes are handled discreetly.
□ Exceptions are escalated and documented when required.
sops.correction:
• Carrying loose cards or cash without a presenter.
• Combining multiple payments before labeling their amounts.
• Taking a guest's phone away from the table.
• Leaving processed cards or change at the terminal.
• Announcing a declined payment loudly.

Keep the cash visible within the presenter until the amount received is identified.

Count change from the approved bank or drawer without using personal funds.
Recount bills and coins before leaving the payment area.
Return change and receipt promptly in the presenter to the correct guest.

□ Personal and restaurant funds remain separate.
□ Tender errors and suspicious currency are escalated.

• Making change from memory before entering the tender.

• Leaving cash exposed at a service station.
• Arguing with a guest about the amount handed over.
• Fixing a cash-entry error by changing another table.

sops.frequency: Whenever a physical card, contactless card, or approved card-linked device is used.
sops.role: The processing employee controls the card and transaction. Managers handle declines, disputes, manual entry, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To process card payments securely through approved systems while protecting guest information and transaction accuracy.
steps: Confirm the card payment applies to the correct check and amount.
Inspect the terminal for obvious damage or tampering and report concerns before use.
Insert, tap, swipe, or present the card only through the approved device.
Allow the guest to control contactless or tableside entry whenever the system supports it.
Do not copy, photograph, record, or communicate card details outside the payment system.
Verify the authorization result and remaining balance before finalizing.
For a decline, speak discreetly and request another approved payment method.
Return the card and receipt promptly to the correct guest.
Process tips, signatures, adjustments, and closeout according to the approved system.
Escalate manual entry, duplicate charge, lost card, dispute, or terminal failure to the manager. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Approved terminal and employee credentials are used.
□ Card data is not written, photographed, or stored.
□ Authorization and amount are verified.
□ Card and receipt are returned promptly.
□ Declines are handled privately and respectfully.
□ Manual or exception transactions receive manager control.
sops.correction:
• Writing a card number or security code on paper.
• Taking a card to an unapproved device or location.
• Running the same card repeatedly after a decline.
• Returning the wrong card to a guest.
• Using manual entry to bypass a damaged or rejected card without approval.
sops.records:
• Approved payment terminal or POS device
• Correct check and payment amount
• Check presenter and receipt process
• Card-decline, tip, signature, and correction procedures
• Manager approval for manual entry or offline processing

sops.title: Split Checks and Separate Payments SOP
sops.frequency: When guests request separate checks, divided items, shared-item splits, or multiple tenders.
sops.role: The server organizes charges by seat and confirms the requested split. Managers approve reopens, transfers, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To divide charges and accept separate payments accurately without delaying service or creating unauthorized adjustments.
steps: Ask how guests want the check divided before collecting payment.
Clarify shared items, equal splits, individual seats, and fixed payment amounts.
Review seat assignments and correct misplaced items before splitting.
Use the approved POS split function rather than estimating totals manually.
Verify discounts, taxes, gratuities, and service charges on each resulting check.
Present the separated checks and invite guests to review them.
Label or organize each payment with the check or amount it covers.
Process one payment at a time and confirm the remaining balance after each.
Obtain manager help before reopening, transferring, or changing a paid check.
Return all receipts, cards, change, and remaining balances to the correct guests. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Split method matches the guests' request.
□ Items and shared charges are assigned correctly.
□ Tax, discounts, gratuity, and fees remain accurate.
□ Payments are matched to the intended checks.
□ Paid checks are changed only with approval.
□ Final receipts and balances are returned correctly.
sops.correction:
• Waiting until cards are collected to ask how the check should be split.
• Dividing totals manually when the POS can track items.
• Losing track of which card belongs to which check.
• Removing an automatic gratuity without authorization.
• Moving an item off a paid check to force the totals to work.
sops.records:
• Accurate seat-number and item assignment
• POS split, transfer, and payment functions
• Guest instructions for shared items and amounts
• Discount, gratuity, and service-charge rules
• Manager approval process for reopened or paid-check changes

sops.title: Gift Card Redemption SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a physical or digital restaurant gift card is presented for payment.
sops.role: The employee processes the card through the approved system. Managers resolve invalid, damaged, or disputed balances.
sops.purpose: To verify and redeem gift cards accurately while protecting balances, guest privacy, and financial controls.
steps: Confirm the card is an accepted restaurant or program gift card.
Ask whether the guest wants to apply a specific amount or the available balance.
Scan, swipe, enter, or present the card using only the approved system.
Verify the displayed balance and redemption amount before finalizing.
Apply the redemption to the correct check and confirm any remaining amount due.
Return the physical card when a balance remains or policy requires return.
Provide the receipt or approved balance information discreetly.
For digital cards, allow the guest to retain control of the device whenever possible.
Do not manually alter a balance or substitute another tender without approval.
Refer unreadable, inactive, disputed, or system-failed cards to the manager. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Card is valid for the restaurant's approved program.
□ Redemption amount matches guest instruction and available balance.
□ Gift card is applied to the correct check.
□ Remaining balance or amount due is communicated accurately.
□ Card and receipt are returned according to policy.
□ Exceptions and manual actions receive manager approval.
sops.correction:
• Assuming every branded card is accepted at the location.
• Reading the card number or balance aloud.
• Discarding a card that still has value.
• Entering a manual discount when the gift card system fails.
• Applying the full balance when the guest requested a smaller amount.
sops.records:
• Approved gift card and POS system
• Correct guest check and payment amount
• Gift card terms, restrictions, and balance process
• Receipt and remaining-balance procedure
• Manager escalation for unreadable, expired where lawful, or disputed cards

sops.title: Coupon and Promotion Acceptance SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a printed, digital, loyalty, event, or limited-time offer is presented.
sops.role: The employee verifies published terms and enters the approved offer. Managers authorize exceptions and disputed applications.
sops.purpose: To apply coupons and promotions consistently according to approved terms while preserving guest trust and financial control.
steps: Thank the guest and review the coupon or digital offer before promising acceptance.
Verify date, location, qualifying items, purchase threshold, and redemption limit.
Confirm whether the offer may be combined with other discounts or loyalty rewards.
Explain any clear restriction before processing payment.
Apply the designated POS key, code, or scan method to the correct items or check.
Obtain manager approval when the offer requires authorization or appears unclear.
Recheck tax, gratuity, service charge, and final total after application.
Mark, collect, or return the coupon according to program rules.
Document the promotion code or reason when required for audit.
Escalate disputed, altered, duplicated, or system-rejected offers to the manager. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Offer meets date, location, item, and purchase requirements.
□ Stacking and redemption limits are followed.
□ Correct POS key and approval level are used.
□ Final check reflects the intended discount.
□ Coupon disposition and documentation follow policy.
□ Disputes are escalated without arguing.
sops.correction:
• Promising acceptance before reading the terms.
• Using a general discount key instead of the promotion code.
• Applying the offer to excluded alcohol, tax, gratuity, or service charges.
• Keeping a guest's phone to inspect a digital offer.
• Changing the expiration date or terms without authorization.
sops.records:
• Current promotion and coupon terms
• Valid dates, items, locations, and redemption limits
• Approved POS discount key or code
• Guest check and qualifying purchase details
• Manager approval and documentation process

sops.title: Server Checkout SOP
sops.frequency: At shift end, server cut, role transfer, or emergency departure.
sops.role: The server prepares an accurate checkout. The manager verifies discrepancies, approvals, records, and final release.
sops.purpose: To reconcile each server's sales, payments, tips, cash due, open checks, and controlled items before shift release.
steps: Complete active tables or transfer them with manager and receiving-server approval.
Review the POS for open, unpaid, duplicate, or incorrectly assigned checks.
Confirm all card payments, tips, gift cards, discounts, comps, and voids are finalized.
Print or generate the approved checkout and sales report.
Count the assigned bank and separate restaurant cash due from employee tips.
Prepare cash due, receipts, vouchers, and required records in the approved order.
Return handhelds, keys, pagers, banks, and other controlled items.
Complete closing or cut side work and obtain the required sign-off.
Present the checkout to the manager and resolve any shortage, overage, or exception.
Leave only after the manager approves the checkout and releases the employee. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ All tables and checks are closed or formally transferred.
□ Payments and tips are finalized in the POS.
□ Cash due matches the approved checkout.
□ Voids, comps, discounts, and transfers are authorized.
□ Side work and controlled items are complete.
□ Manager documents discrepancies and approves release.
sops.correction:
• Printing the report before finalizing all payments.
• Using another employee's cash or tips to cover a shortage.
• Leaving open checks for the closing server without transfer.
• Discarding receipts or payment records prematurely.
• Leaving after dropping off cash without manager approval.
sops.records:
• POS checkout and sales report
• Assigned bank, cash, receipts, and payment records
• Open-check, void, comp, discount, and transfer report
• Tip declaration or adjustment process
• Side-work sign-off and controlled-item return list

sops.title: Server Closing Side Work SOP
sops.frequency: During controlled closing periods and after the final assigned guest departs.
sops.role: Each server completes assigned work without reducing active guest service. The manager verifies before release.
sops.purpose: To clean, restock, reset, and secure server areas so the restaurant is ready for the next operating period.
steps: Review the assigned closing work and confirm which tasks can begin during service.
Maintain table coverage and obtain permission before leaving the section for side work.
Remove trash, used linen, clutter, and unneeded service items from assigned areas.
Clean and sanitize approved stations, shelves, trays, menus, and touchpoints.
Restock napkins, silverware, condiments, paper goods, and other supplies to par.
Clean and reset tables, chairs, booths, floors, and service stations.
Return food, beverages, chemicals, and equipment to approved storage locations.
Shut down or secure assigned devices only after manager approval.
Report shortages, breakage, maintenance needs, pest evidence, or incomplete shared work.
Complete the checklist and obtain manager verification before checkout and release. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Active guests continue receiving full service.
□ Assigned stations and section are clean and reset.
□ Supplies are restocked to the approved par.
□ Waste, linen, food, and chemicals are handled correctly.
□ Equipment and controlled areas are secured.
□ Shortages and maintenance concerns are documented.
sops.correction:
• Starting noisy cleaning around guests too early.
• Leaving the section unattended to complete side work.
• Using spray chemicals near food or clean tableware.
• Filling containers without cleaning or rotating them as required.
• Signing off shared tasks without inspecting them.
sops.records:
• Closing side-work chart or checklist
• Approved cleaning and sanitizing supplies
• Restocking pars and storage locations
• Trash, recycling, and linen procedures
• Equipment shutdown and security instructions

sops.title: Guest Allergy Communication by Servers SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest reports an allergy, allergen avoidance need, or concern about ingredients or cross-contact.
sops.role: The server captures the guest's exact concern and initiates the approved alert. The manager and kitchen determine available options and required controls.
sops.purpose: To communicate a guest-reported food allergy accurately from the table through preparation and verified delivery.
steps: Stop ordinary order entry and listen to the guest's exact allergen concern.
Repeat the allergen back and clarify the item or ingredients the guest must avoid.
Tell the guest that the manager or kitchen must verify available options.
Notify the manager and designated kitchen contact using the approved alert words.
Consult only current approved ingredient information; do not infer from item names.
Enter the allergy alert, item, modifiers, and seat using designated POS keys.
Obtain verbal acknowledgment from the responsible kitchen or expo employee.
Do not change, add, or substitute ingredients after approval without restarting verification.
Verify the identified plate and deliver it directly through the approved controlled handoff.
Check back promptly; if symptoms are reported, summon the manager and activate the emergency-response SOP immediately. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ Guest's allergen concern is repeated and recorded accurately.
□ Manager and kitchen receive both required POS and verbal notice.
□ Approved ingredient information is used.
□ No unsupported safety guarantee is made.
□ Plate and guest identity are verified at delivery.
□ Suspected reaction triggers immediate emergency response.
sops.correction:
• Treating an allergy as an ordinary preference modifier.
• Saying an item is safe because it has been served before.
• Entering a note but failing to notify the kitchen verbally.
• Allowing an unapproved substitution after the order is verified.
• Auctioning an allergy-designated plate at the table.
sops.records:
• Current ingredient and allergen reference
• Approved POS allergy alert and modifier keys
• Manager and kitchen communication channel
• Allergy-order identification and delivery method
• Emergency-response procedure for a suspected reaction

sops.frequency: Whenever a guest expresses dissatisfaction beyond the employee's authority or raises a safety, illness, injury, allergy, conduct, or payment concern.
sops.role: The employee listens, stabilizes immediate service, and contacts the manager. The manager owns investigation, authorization, and follow-up.
sops.purpose: To recognize complaints that require leadership involvement and transfer them to a manager without delay, argument, or loss of facts.
steps: Stop, make eye contact, and allow the guest to explain without interruption.
Thank the guest for telling you and acknowledge the experience professionally.
Clarify the requested outcome and determine whether an immediate safety issue exists.
Correct a simple service need only within your approved authority.
Tell the guest when manager involvement is needed and contact the manager promptly.
Give the manager the table, guest, exact concern, timing, item, and actions already taken.
Remain available and do not debate fault, policy, or compensation with the guest.
Preserve relevant food, foreign objects, receipts, or transaction details when instructed.
Follow through on assigned corrections and check back after the manager response.
Document required facts before the shift ends and report any unresolved concern. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Required evidence and documentation are preserved.

• Defending the restaurant before understanding the concern.
• Promising a refund, comp, firing, or other outcome without authority.
• Waiting until checkout to mention a serious complaint.
• Summarizing the concern vaguely and omitting what was already promised.
• Discarding the food, object, receipt, or record involved in the complaint.

sops.title: Expo-to-Runner Handoff SOP
sops.station: Part 3 — Service Assistants, Food Running, To-Go & Delivery
sops.frequency: Whenever responsibility, custody, information, or an active order transfers between employees.
sops.role: The releasing employee gives complete information. The receiving employee confirms acceptance; management resolves exceptions.
sops.purpose: To transfer complete ticket, table, seat, timing, allergy, and quality information from expo to the assigned food runner.
steps: Identify the exact order, guest, station, transaction, custody, and time period covered by expo-to-runner handoff.
Conduct the transfer directly whenever possible and use the approved written or electronic record.
Review active work, deadlines, high-risk conditions, and items awaiting manager action.
Expo identifies table, seat numbers, item count, course, allergy flags, and special handling before release.
The runner repeats back critical information and visually compares the ticket to the completed plates.
Both employees confirm sauces, sides, garnishes, and missing items before the runner lifts the order.
The runner reports delivery, table-access problems, or rejected items so expo can close the handoff loop.
Require repeat-back of critical allergy, cash, identity, safety, timing, and guest information.
Assign a named owner and due time for every unresolved item and inform management of exceptions.
Both employees acknowledge the transfer; responsibility remains with the releasing employee until acceptance is clear. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Both employees confirm sauces, sides, garnishes, and missing items before the runner lifts the order.
□ The runner reports delivery, table-access problems, or rejected items so expo can close the handoff loop.
□ Assign a named owner and due time for every unresolved item and inform management of exceptions.

sops.title: Hot Food Delivery Priority SOP
sops.station: Part 3 — Service Assistants, Food Running, To-Go & Delivery
sops.frequency: Whenever hot food delivery priority is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The assigned employee performs the service and communicates needs. The manager handles exceptions and actions beyond employee authority.
sops.purpose: To prioritize and deliver hot food immediately so temperature, presentation, ticket completeness, and guest timing are protected.
steps: Review the expo screen or ticket rail continuously and identify hot entrées, sides, and sauces that are fully assembled and released for delivery.
Confirm the table number, seat positions, item names, modifiers, allergy indicators, and required accompaniments before touching the plates.
Give immediate priority to released hot food; pause lower-priority side work and request runner assistance when more plates are ready than one person can carry safely.
Use clean, dry service cloths or approved trays and handle plates only by safe, non-food-contact surfaces.
Deliver all available items for the table together when practical, while never holding a completed hot plate solely to wait for a delayed item without manager or expo direction.
Announce each item clearly at the correct seat and verify special modifications discreetly without describing a guest's medical information.
Place plates safely, keep hands and clothing away from food-contact areas, and warn guests about unusually hot plates when appropriate.
Notify the server and expo immediately about missing items, incorrect temperatures, damaged presentation, or a guest who questions the order.
Return rejected or incorrect food through the approved correction process; never relocate garnish, sauce, or food between guest plates.
Clear the delivery path, confirm the table has necessary utensils and condiments, and communicate any unresolved need before leaving. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the correct guest, table, order, service trigger, and manager escalation point for hot food delivery priority.
□ Confirm the table number, seat positions, item names, modifiers, allergy indicators, and required accompaniments before touching the plates.
□ Use clean, dry service cloths or approved trays and handle plates only by safe, non-food-contact surfaces.
□ Announce each item clearly at the correct seat and verify special modifications discreetly without describing a guest's medical information.
□ Notify the server and expo immediately about missing items, incorrect temperatures, damaged presentation, or a guest who questions the order.
□ Clear the delivery path, confirm the table has necessary utensils and condiments, and communicate any unresolved need before leaving.
sops.correction:
• Allowing released hot food to sit while completing side work or waiting unnecessarily for another item.
• Delivering to the wrong seat or missing modifiers, allergy indicators, sauces, or accompaniments.
• Carrying unsafe plate quantities, touching food-contact surfaces, or using soiled service cloths.
• Delivering visibly incorrect, cooling, damaged, or incomplete food instead of returning it to expo.
• Failing to tell the server or expo about delayed, rejected, or missing items.

sops.title: Cold Food Delivery Priority SOP
sops.station: Part 3 — Service Assistants, Food Running, To-Go & Delivery
sops.frequency: Whenever cold food delivery priority is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The assigned employee performs the service and communicates needs. The manager handles exceptions and actions beyond employee authority.
sops.purpose: To protect cold-food temperature, presentation, and order accuracy while coordinating delivery with the rest of the table.
steps: Monitor the expo area for released salads, chilled appetizers, desserts, cold sides, and other temperature-sensitive cold items.
Match each item to the ticket, table, seat, modifier, allergy indicator, garnish, dressing, and required service piece before delivery.
Deliver released cold food promptly and keep it away from heat lamps, hot plates, steam, direct sunlight, and other warming sources.
Use clean trays or approved carrying methods and protect chilled food from bare-hand contact, cross-contact, spills, and stacked plate damage.
Coordinate with expo when hot and cold courses must arrive together, but do not allow cold food to warm while waiting without manager direction.
Announce each item at the correct seat and confirm dressings, sauces, chilled accompaniments, and special modifications.
Observe appearance and temperature; return wilted, melting, warm, damaged, or incorrectly garnished items before they reach the guest.
Notify the server immediately when an item is delivered separately, delayed, corrected, or refused.
Handle returned or questioned cold food through the approved remake and discard process; never re-serve food that reached a guest.
Confirm the guest has the correct utensils and accompaniments, then clear the pickup area so the next cold item remains protected. & CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can identify the correct guest, table, order, service trigger, and manager escalation point for cold food delivery priority.
□ Match each item to the ticket, table, seat, modifier, allergy indicator, garnish, dressing, and required service piece before delivery.
□ Use clean trays or approved carrying methods and protect chilled food from bare-hand contact, cross-contact, spills, and stacked plate damage.
□ Announce each item at the correct seat and confirm dressings, sauces, chilled accompaniments, and special modifications.
□ Notify the server immediately when an item is delivered separately, delayed, corrected, or refused.
□ Confirm the guest has the correct utensils and accompaniments, then clear the pickup area so the next cold item remains protected.

sourceSections.procedure:
1. Monitor the expo area for released salads, chilled appetizers, desserts, cold sides, and other temperature-sensitive cold items.
2. Match each item to the ticket, table, seat, modifier, allergy indicator, garnish, dressing, and required service piece before delivery.
3. Deliver released cold food promptly and keep it away from heat lamps, hot plates, steam, direct sunlight, and other warming sources.
4. Use clean trays or approved carrying methods and protect chilled food from bare-hand contact, cross-contact, spills, and stacked plate damage.
5. Coordinate with expo when hot and cold courses must arrive together, but do not allow cold food to warm while waiting without manager direction.
6. Announce each item at the correct seat and confirm dressings, sauces, chilled accompaniments, and special modifications.
7. Observe appearance and temperature; return wilted, melting, warm, damaged, or incorrectly garnished items before they reach the guest.
8. Notify the server immediately when an item is delivered separately, delayed, corrected, or refused.
9. Handle returned or questioned cold food through the approved remake and discard process; never re-serve food that reached a guest.
10. Confirm the guest has the correct utensils and accompaniments, then clear the pickup area so the next cold item remains protected. & CUSTOMIZATION

steps: Review current status, timing, staffing, volume, standards, and manager priorities relevant to verifying to-go order accuracy.

Identify immediate hazards, delays, capacity limits, mismatches, and work without a clear owner.
Match guest name, order number, item count, sizes, modifiers, sides, and special instructions to the final ticket.
Inspect containers and labels without contaminating food or breaking required seals.
Confirm sauces, condiments, utensils, beverages, desserts, and paid add-ons are present.
Obtain required second verification for allergy, large, high-value, or other designated orders.
Assign corrections to named employees, communicate status, and set completion and recheck times.
Recheck the highest-risk items and escalate when the process exceeds authority, capacity, or safe limits.
Record decisions, exceptions, and follow-up for management review. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Curbside Pickup SOP
sops.station: Part 3 — Service Assistants, Food Running, To-Go & Delivery
sops.frequency: Whenever curbside pickup is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The releasing employee gives complete information. The receiving employee confirms acceptance; management resolves exceptions.
sops.purpose: To release curbside orders to the verified guest or vehicle safely, promptly, accurately, and with documented payment and handoff status.
steps: Identify the exact order, guest, station, transaction, custody, and time period covered by curbside pickup.
Conduct the transfer directly whenever possible and use the approved written or electronic record.
Review active work, deadlines, high-risk conditions, and items awaiting manager action.
Confirm guest arrival, vehicle description or pickup location, guest name, order number, and payment status.
Carry the sealed order by the approved route while watching traffic, curbs, weather, and parking-lot hazards.
Verify the recipient before release and complete any permitted payment or identification requirement.
Provide receipt or final instructions and close the pickup in the ordering system.
Require repeat-back of critical allergy, cash, identity, safety, timing, and guest information.
Assign a named owner and due time for every unresolved item and inform management of exceptions.
Both employees acknowledge the transfer; responsibility remains with the releasing employee until acceptance is clear. CUSTOMIZATION

Notify the responsible employee or manager of completion and every remaining guest need.
Return equipment, reset the area or system, and document material exceptions before the next task. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Drink Preparation SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever drink preparation is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows approved recipes, tools, sanitation, and quality controls. The manager verifies exceptions and waste.
sops.purpose: To prepare each beverage from the approved recipe using correct ingredients, portions, glassware, garnish, sanitation, and presentation.
steps: Review the current drink preparation recipe, process, manufacturer instruction, assignment, or production need.
Prepare a clean, organized area with approved tools, containers, and protective equipment.
Inspect product, ingredients, glassware, containers, and equipment and remove unsafe or unapproved items.
Read the full ticket or approved recipe, including size, brand, modifier, allergy note, glass, portion, and garnish.
Measure controlled ingredients with the required jigger, pour device, or portion tool.
Build, shake, stir, blend, or pour in the approved sequence while preventing cross-contact and waste.
Inspect fill, appearance, garnish, glass, and ticket identity before placing the drink in the pickup position.
Check portion, quality, label, temperature, cleanliness, safety, and final presentation against standard.
Correct or discard unacceptable work and report recurring waste, malfunction, or shortage.
Clean, store, reset, and document the area or equipment before the task is complete. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Responsible Alcohol Service SOP
sops.frequency: Before and throughout any alcohol-related transaction or whenever eligibility or safety is uncertain.
sops.role: Every employee stops and escalates questionable alcohol service. The manager leads refusal, safety planning, and documentation.
sops.purpose: To serve alcohol responsibly by monitoring guest condition, drink pace, food intake, age requirements, and manager escalation triggers.
steps: Review the restaurant's current alcohol-service policy, state/local requirements, and manager escalation contacts before service.
Confirm every alcohol-serving employee is trained and authorized for the assigned role.
Observe guest age, behavior, speech, coordination, pace of consumption, food intake, and group dynamics without stereotyping.
Verify identification whenever required and use only approved forms of identification and inspection methods.
Serve only approved portions and recipes; do not free-pour, over-serve, encourage rapid consumption, or bypass refusal decisions.
Communicate concerns discreetly with the manager and other authorized servers so service limits remain consistent.
Slow, delay, substitute, or stop service only within approved authority and offer nonalcoholic options or food when appropriate.
Arrange safe-transport assistance through the approved process without promising custody or transportation the restaurant cannot provide.
Document refusals, incidents, disputed identification, threats, injuries, or law-enforcement contact according to policy.
Transfer unresolved concerns during handoff and confirm management ownership before leaving the area. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Transfer unresolved concerns during handoff and confirm management ownership before leaving the area.

• Treating responsible service as only an age-check issue and ignoring pace, behavior, impairment, and transportation risk.

• Arguing, shaming, stereotyping, or physically confronting a guest unnecessarily.
• Failing to document refusal, transportation, responder contact, and employee handoff.

steps: Identify every alcohol purchase or service situation that requires age verification under restaurant policy or law.
Ask the guest for an approved, unexpired identification document before preparing or delivering alcohol.
Hold the identification in the approved manner and compare the photograph, physical description, birth date, and expiration date to the guest.

Decline service and notify the manager when identification is absent, expired, altered, borrowed, inconsistent, or otherwise unacceptable.
Return the identification to the guest unless law or approved policy directs another action; do not confiscate it on personal judgment.
Record disputed or refused identification when required and communicate the decision to authorized service employees.
Continue to monitor responsible service after age is verified; age verification does not remove intoxication controls. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Refusal of Alcohol Service SOP
sops.frequency: Before and throughout any alcohol-related transaction or whenever eligibility or safety is uncertain.
sops.role: Every employee stops and escalates questionable alcohol service. The manager leads refusal, safety planning, and documentation.
sops.purpose: To refuse alcohol service calmly, consistently, and safely while involving management and documenting the reason when required.
steps: Identify the reason service must be refused, including age, identification, intoxication, prior manager decision, behavior, or policy restriction.
Notify the manager before refusal whenever time and safety allow and coordinate one consistent message.
Approach calmly, maintain safe distance, and use brief approved wording without accusation, debate, or public embarrassment.
State that no additional alcohol will be served and do not negotiate another drink, another server, or a different payment method.
Remove or secure pending alcohol only when safe and authorized; do not touch guest property or use physical force.
Offer approved nonalcoholic options, food, check settlement, or safe-transport assistance when appropriate.
Alert authorized employees so another server or bar position does not unknowingly continue service.
Escalate threats, violence, medical concerns, impaired driving risk, or refusal to leave according to the emergency and security plan.
Document the time, reason, employees involved, guest response, manager action, and any transportation or responder contact.
Review the incident at handoff and preserve relevant checks, video, witness, and transaction information. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Offer approved nonalcoholic options, food, check settlement, or safe-transport assistance when appropriate.
□ Escalate threats, violence, medical concerns, impaired driving risk, or refusal to leave according to the emergency and security plan.
□ Review the incident at handoff and preserve relevant checks, video, witness, and transaction information.

• Refusing service without coordinating with the manager and other authorized servers.

• Failing to document the reason, guest response, transportation, threats, and manager actions.

sops.title: Intoxicated Guest Escalation SOP
sops.frequency: Before and throughout any alcohol-related transaction or whenever eligibility or safety is uncertain.
sops.role: Every employee stops and escalates questionable alcohol service. The manager leads refusal, safety planning, and documentation.
sops.purpose: To protect an apparently intoxicated guest and others by stopping service, notifying management, arranging safe next steps, and documenting the event.
steps: Observe and confirm specific behaviors that may indicate impairment, medical distress, escalating aggression, or inability to travel safely.
Notify the manager immediately and stop additional alcohol service while the situation is assessed.
Review the guest's check, known consumption, food intake, companions, prior refusals, and transportation plan without making a diagnosis.
Approach with a second authorized employee when appropriate and use calm, nonjudgmental language.
Remove additional alcohol only when safe and authorized; provide water, food, or a quieter area if approved and helpful.
Encourage a sober companion, rideshare, taxi, or other approved safe-transport option and record who accepted responsibility when policy requires.
Do not allow employees to physically restrain, search, or transport the guest unless specifically trained and authorized.
Call emergency services or law enforcement when there is medical distress, violence, a weapon, immediate driving danger, or another urgent threat.
Protect other guests, employees, exits, and evidence while maintaining privacy and avoiding unnecessary confrontation.
Complete the incident record and manager follow-up, including service history, decisions, transportation, responders, and employee handoff. & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Encourage a sober companion, rideshare, taxi, or other approved safe-transport option and record who accepted responsibility when policy requires.
□ Call emergency services or law enforcement when there is medical distress, violence, a weapon, immediate driving danger, or another urgent threat.
□ Complete the incident record and manager follow-up, including service history, decisions, transportation, responders, and employee handoff.
sops.correction:
• Treating suspected impairment as a diagnosis or relying on one behavior without reviewing the situation.
• Continuing alcohol service while management decides what to do.
• Physically restraining, searching, or personally transporting the guest without training and authority.
• Ignoring medical distress, aggression, weapons, or immediate impaired-driving risk.
• Closing the incident without objective observations, service history, transportation, responder, and follow-up records.

sops.frequency: Whenever service well is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
