steps: Confirm the correct guest, table, seat, order, timing, and responsible employee for service well.
Inspect the ticket, item, tools, identifiers, and required accompaniments before beginning.
Choose the approved service method and safe route and obtain help rather than taking an unsafe shortcut.
Organize current tickets, clean tools, glassware, garnishes, ingredients, and designated pickup positions.
Follow the approved first-in sequence while recognizing allergy, remake, missing-drink, and manager-approved priorities.
Place completed drinks with clear ticket, table, and seat identification and communicate realistic delays.
Report unclaimed drinks, recurring waits, shortages, or quality decline before remaking or discarding.
Stop when identity, allergy, quality, temperature, or safety information does not match.
Notify the responsible employee or manager of completion and every remaining guest need.
Return equipment, reset the area or system, and document material exceptions before the next task. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Draft Beer Service SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever draft beer service is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows approved recipes, tools, sanitation, and quality controls. The manager verifies exceptions and waste.
sops.purpose: To pour and serve draft beer with the correct glassware, temperature, head, portion, sanitation, and product-loss controls.
steps: Confirm the correct beer, keg, tap, glassware, temperature, and service size before pouring.
Inspect the glass for cleanliness, chips, lipstick, detergent film, odor, and correct style.
Open the tap fully in one motion; do not partially open it or allow the faucet to contact the glass or beer.
Hold the glass at the approved angle and position to control foam without touching the faucet.
Straighten the glass near completion and create the restaurant's approved head.
Stop and report excessive foam, flat beer, off odor, unusual color, warm product, slow flow, or suspected line contamination.
Never mix old and new pours, return overflow to service, or serve from an unapproved tap.
Wipe the exterior, verify presentation, and deliver promptly with the correct check or ticket.
Record waste or comp according to policy and communicate keg or line concerns to the manager.
Keep the faucet, drip tray, surrounding area, and glass-storage zone clean during service. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Hold the glass at the approved angle and position to control foam without touching the faucet.
□ Stop and report excessive foam, flat beer, off odor, unusual color, warm product, slow flow, or suspected line contamination.
□ Wipe the exterior, verify presentation, and deliver promptly with the correct check or ticket.
□ Keep the faucet, drip tray, surrounding area, and glass-storage zone clean during service.
sops.correction:
• Partially opening the tap, touching the faucet to the glass, or using warm, dirty, chipped, or incorrect glassware.
• Serving excessive foam, flat beer, off odor, wrong product, or poor temperature without investigation.
• Mixing old and new pours or returning overflow to service.
• Failing to report line, keg, regulator, temperature, or sanitation problems.
• Omitting waste, comp, keg-change, or maintenance documentation.

sops.title: Wine Service SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever wine service is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows approved recipes, tools, sanitation, and quality controls. The manager verifies exceptions and waste.
sops.purpose: To present, open, pour, and serve wine according to the restaurant's service level, responsible-service policy, and product standards.
steps: Confirm the wine, vintage when relevant, bottle or glass size, price, service temperature, and guest order.
Select clean, odor-free, chip-free glassware appropriate to the restaurant's service standard.
Present the bottle label to the ordering guest before opening when full-bottle service is used.
Open the bottle safely with the approved tool and inspect the closure, neck, and wine for obvious defects.
Offer the approved verification pour when required and wait for guest confirmation without debating preference.
Pour the approved portion without touching the glass rim or overfilling.
Keep the label visible, wipe drips, and place or chill the bottle according to the service standard.
For by-the-glass service, protect open bottles with the approved date, preservation, storage, and discard controls.
Escalate suspected cork taint, oxidation, wrong vintage, broken cork, or guest rejection to the manager.
Record waste, replacement, comp, or open-bottle transfer and return tools and wine to proper storage. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can state the product or service trigger, responsible-service limit, assigned authority, and escalation point for wine service.
□ Select clean, odor-free, chip-free glassware appropriate to the restaurant's service standard.
□ Open the bottle safely with the approved tool and inspect the closure, neck, and wine for obvious defects.
□ Pour the approved portion without touching the glass rim or overfilling.
□ For by-the-glass service, protect open bottles with the approved date, preservation, storage, and discard controls.
□ Record waste, replacement, comp, or open-bottle transfer and return tools and wine to proper storage.
sops.correction:
• Opening the wrong wine, vintage, size, or price before guest confirmation.
• Using dirty, chipped, warm, or strongly scented glassware.
• Overpouring, touching the rim, hiding the label, or skipping the approved verification pour.
• Serving oxidized, corked, improperly stored, or overdue open wine.
• Failing to document replacement, waste, comp, and open-bottle control.

sops.title: Bar Glassware Handling SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever bar glassware handling is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows approved recipes, tools, sanitation, and quality controls. The manager verifies exceptions and waste.
sops.purpose: To wash, inspect, polish, handle, and store bar glassware without contaminating rims, nesting glasses, or returning damaged pieces to service.
steps: Review the current bar glassware handling recipe, process, manufacturer instruction, assignment, or production need.
Prepare a clean, organized area with approved tools, containers, and protective equipment.
Inspect product, ingredients, glassware, containers, and equipment and remove unsafe or unapproved items.
Handle glassware by approved surfaces and avoid contact with rims and interior drinking areas.
Inspect every glass for chips, cracks, residue, lipstick, odor, heat damage, and improper cooling.
Separate broken or questionable glassware and follow the broken-glass cleanup procedure.
Wash, air-dry, polish when approved, and store glassware without nesting or exposure to splash and debris.
Check portion, quality, label, temperature, cleanliness, safety, and final presentation against standard.
Correct or discard unacceptable work and report recurring waste, malfunction, or shortage.
Clean, store, reset, and document the area or equipment before the task is complete. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Separate broken or questionable glassware and follow the broken-glass cleanup procedure.
□ Wash, air-dry, polish when approved, and store glassware without nesting or exposure to splash and debris.
□ Correct or discard unacceptable work and report recurring waste, malfunction, or shortage.

• Beginning bar glassware handling without the current recipe, approved tools, clean equipment, and correct product.

• Serving or storing work that fails quality, sanitation, portion, or presentation checks.

sops.title: Bar Cleaning SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever bar cleaning is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: Assigned employees complete closing work. The manager verifies sanitation, cash, security, and unresolved conditions before release.
sops.purpose: To keep the bar clean and sanitary during service and complete the approved closing-cleaning sequence without contaminating food or beverages.
steps: Review the current bar cleaning checklist and confirm management has approved the start of closing work.
Identify active guests, orders, checks, cash, controlled product, and duties that must remain available.
Gather approved cleaning, storage, waste, and security supplies without obstructing operating areas.
Remove food, glassware, tools, mats, trash, and movable supplies from the cleaning zone.
Wash, rinse, and sanitize food-contact tools and surfaces with approved chemical concentration and contact time.
Clean sinks, rails, wells, shelves, equipment exteriors, drains, floors, and high-touch points.
Air-dry and restore items and document maintenance, pest, chemical, or damage concerns.
Report breakage, shortage, maintenance, safety, cash, or guest issues and assign unresolved follow-up.
Complete the final checklist and walk the area with the manager or designated verifier.
Sign off only after work is accepted and remaining responsibility is formally transferred. CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can state the product or service trigger, responsible-service limit, assigned authority, and escalation point for bar cleaning.
□ Remove food, glassware, tools, mats, trash, and movable supplies from the cleaning zone.
□ Wash, rinse, and sanitize food-contact tools and surfaces with approved chemical concentration and contact time.
□ Clean sinks, rails, wells, shelves, equipment exteriors, drains, floors, and high-touch points.
□ Air-dry and restore items and document maintenance, pest, chemical, or damage concerns.
□ Complete the final checklist and walk the area with the manager or designated verifier.

• Leaving shortages, damage, maintenance, or safety concerns undocumented.
• Releasing keys, cash, product, or records without confirmed custody.
• Leaving before the manager accepts the closing assignment.

sourceSections.procedure:
1. Review the current bar cleaning checklist and confirm management has approved the start of closing work.
2. Identify active guests, orders, checks, cash, controlled product, and duties that must remain available.
3. Gather approved cleaning, storage, waste, and security supplies without obstructing operating areas.
4. Remove food, glassware, tools, mats, trash, and movable supplies from the cleaning zone.
5. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food-contact tools and surfaces with approved chemical concentration and contact time.
6. Clean sinks, rails, wells, shelves, equipment exteriors, drains, floors, and high-touch points.
7. Air-dry and restore items and document maintenance, pest, chemical, or damage concerns.
8. Report breakage, shortage, maintenance, safety, cash, or guest issues and assign unresolved follow-up.

sops.frequency: Whenever responsibility, custody, information, or an active order transfers between employees.

steps: Identify the exact order, guest, station, transaction, custody, and time period covered by bar shift handoff.
Conduct the transfer directly whenever possible and use the approved written or electronic record.
Review active work, deadlines, high-risk conditions, and items awaiting manager action.
Review active guests, tabs, pending food, drink tickets, refusals, and special requests face to face.
Count or transfer banks, keys, devices, controlled items, and signed receipts according to policy.
Identify shortages, draft or equipment issues, spills, prep levels, cleaning, and pending approvals.
Both employees confirm acceptance and management records unresolved financial, safety, or guest issues.
Require repeat-back of critical allergy, cash, identity, safety, timing, and guest information.
Assign a named owner and due time for every unresolved item and inform management of exceptions.
Both employees acknowledge the transfer; responsibility remains with the releasing employee until acceptance is clear. CUSTOMIZATION

steps: Review the employee handoff, guest check, order, timing, prior actions, and any safety or legal concerns before approaching.

Confirm the guest's preferred contact method and follow-up commitment when additional review is required.

Review the underlying system failure and assign coaching, repair, menu, staffing, or SOP follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Service Recovery Authorization SOP
sops.station: Part 5 — Guest Experience, Recovery & Special Situations
sops.frequency: Whenever service recovery authorization is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.
sops.role: The employee listens, confirms facts, and stays within authority. The manager selects recovery, documents the decision, and assigns follow-up.
sops.purpose: To define who may authorize service recovery, what limits apply, and how every approval, guest response, and follow-up is documented.
steps: Listen without interruption and identify the guest, order, visit timing, and exact concern connected to service recovery authorization.
Acknowledge the concern without arguing, blaming, admitting liability, or promising an outcome outside authority.
Verify relevant ticket, product, employee, payment, timing, and prior-action facts while keeping the guest informed.
Identify the guest concern, affected item, check amount, prior actions, and requested resolution.
Confirm the employee and manager authority levels before committing to a remake, comp, discount, refund, or credit.
Enter the approved recovery under the correct POS reason code with required notes and credentials.
Communicate the action and timing to the guest and team and verify completion and pattern review.
Explain the approved resolution, responsible manager, expected timing, and any action the guest must take.
Follow up before departure or by the promised deadline and confirm whether another authorized response is needed.
Document the concern, facts reviewed, authority used, resolution, guest response, and assigned follow-up. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.station: Part 5 — Guest Experience, Recovery & Special Situations
sops.frequency: Whenever incorrect order recovery is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.

sops.purpose: To correct an inaccurate or incomplete order quickly while protecting allergy controls, remake timing, guest communication, and transaction accuracy.
steps: Listen without interruption and identify the guest, order, visit timing, and exact concern connected to incorrect order recovery.
Acknowledge the concern without arguing, blaming, admitting liability, or promising an outcome outside authority.

2. Acknowledge the concern without arguing, blaming, admitting liability, or promising an outcome outside authority.
3. Verify relevant ticket, product, employee, payment, timing, and prior-action facts while keeping the guest informed.
4. Confirm actual ticket time, course, table status, kitchen position, and cause before approaching the guest.
5. Obtain a realistic completion estimate from kitchen or expo and do not promise an unverified time.
6. Update the guest proactively and offer approved support based on the delay and meal stage.
7. Monitor completion through delivery, adjust the check when authorized, and record significant delay causes.
8. Explain the approved resolution, responsible manager, expected timing, and any action the guest must take.
9. Follow up before departure or by the promised deadline and confirm whether another authorized response is needed.
10. Document the concern, facts reviewed, authority used, resolution, guest response, and assigned follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Follow up before departure or by the promised deadline and confirm whether another authorized response is needed.

• Offering recovery for delayed ticket recovery before hearing the full concern and confirming the guest, order, timing, and facts.
• Arguing, blaming another employee, minimizing the concern, or making an unsupported promise.
• Offering compensation outside authority or without recording the reason and approval.
• Failing to explain the resolution, expected timing, responsible manager, or remaining guest action.
• Ending the recovery without follow-up, guest-response notes, and pattern documentation.

sops.title: Allergy Concern Response SOP
sops.station: Part 5 — Guest Experience, Recovery & Special Situations
sops.frequency: Immediately when the concern, report, unsafe condition, or incident is observed or received.
sops.role: Employees protect immediate safety and notify management. The manager controls response, recovery, records, and authorized follow-up.
sops.purpose: To respond immediately to a guest-reported allergy concern, stop unsafe service, involve management, preserve facts, and coordinate approved follow-up.
steps: Protect immediate safety and notify the manager before beginning the formal allergy concern response.
Contact emergency, security, law-enforcement, HR, ownership, or other approved resources when required.
Preserve the scene, item, check, records, and other evidence without creating additional risk.
Stop service of the questioned item and notify the manager and designated kitchen leader immediately.
Confirm what the guest reported without guessing ingredients, severity, diagnosis, or medical outcome.
Follow the emergency plan and contact emergency services when symptoms or an emergency are reported.
Preserve relevant ticket and food information and document objective facts for authorized follow-up.
Collect separate witness names and distinguish direct observations from information reported by others.
Do not diagnose, admit liability, assign unsupported blame, threaten, or promise outcomes outside authority.
Complete, sign, secure, and route the report promptly and assign authorized follow-up. & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Guest Injury Initial Response SOP
sops.station: Part 5 — Guest Experience, Recovery & Special Situations
sops.frequency: Immediately when the concern, report, unsafe condition, or incident is observed or received.
sops.role: Employees protect immediate safety and notify management. The manager controls response, recovery, records, and authorized follow-up.
sops.purpose: To provide an immediate, calm response to a guest injury, obtain appropriate help, secure the scene, and document objective facts.
steps: Protect immediate safety and notify the manager before beginning the formal guest injury response.
Contact emergency, security, law-enforcement, HR, ownership, or other approved resources when required.
Preserve the scene, item, check, records, and other evidence without creating additional risk.
Stop nearby activity, protect the guest from additional danger, and contact the manager.
Ask whether emergency medical assistance is needed and call emergency services according to the response plan.
Do not move the guest unless immediate safety requires it and do not diagnose, assign fault, or offer medication.
Preserve the scene, identify witnesses, document objective facts, and route follow-up through management.
Collect separate witness names and distinguish direct observations from information reported by others.
Do not diagnose, admit liability, assign unsupported blame, threaten, or promise outcomes outside authority.
Complete, sign, secure, and route the report promptly and assign authorized follow-up. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Special Occasion Recognition SOP

sops.frequency: Whenever special occasion recognition is required during opening, service, shift transition, or closing.

2. Inspect the ticket, item, tools, identifiers, and required accompaniments before beginning.
3. Choose the approved service method and safe route and obtain help rather than taking an unsafe shortcut.
4. Use simple respectful language, visual menu references, written numbers, approved translation tools, or a qualified employee interpreter.
5. Confirm meaning through teach-back, pointing, or written confirmation rather than repeated louder speech.
6. Do not use children or unapproved bystanders for sensitive payment, medical, employment, or complaint interpretation.
7. Escalate unresolved allergy, safety, consent, or payment questions before proceeding.
8. Stop when identity, allergy, quality, temperature, or safety information does not match.
9. Notify the responsible employee or manager of completion and every remaining guest need.
10. Return equipment, reset the area or system, and document material exceptions before the next task. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: POS Login and Security SOP
sops.station: Part 6 — Pos, Cash, Discounts & Financial Controls
sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To protect POS access and transaction accountability by requiring individual credentials, secure login practices, role-based permissions, and prompt reporting of suspicious activity.
steps: Identify the employee, guest check, drawer, payment, item, amount, and reason connected to POS login and security.
Use only individual credentials and confirm the correct system, business date, location, and assigned custody.
Review the original ticket, receipt, authorization, balance, or supporting record before moving value.
Use only individually assigned credentials and confirm the correct employee profile, location, drawer, printer, and permissions.
Lock or log out whenever leaving the device and shield credentials and guest information from view.
Never share passwords, cards, codes, or another employee profile to bypass permissions.
Report lost credentials, suspicious access, incorrect permissions, or compromised devices immediately.
Stop for manager review when identity, amount, authority, payment data, cash count, or audit information does not agree.
Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
Secure funds and records and document approvals, variances, disputes, and unusual activity. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for POS login and security.
□ Use only individually assigned credentials and confirm the correct employee profile, location, drawer, printer, and permissions.
□ Lock or log out whenever leaving the device and shield credentials and guest information from view.
□ Never share passwords, cards, codes, or another employee profile to bypass permissions.
□ Report lost credentials, suspicious access, incorrect permissions, or compromised devices immediately.
□ Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
sops.correction:
• Beginning POS login and security without verifying the check, drawer, amount, reason, authority, and business date.
• Sharing credentials, bypassing required approval, or moving value outside the recorded system.
• Counting or reviewing funds where unauthorized employees or guests can observe or interfere.
• Forcing a transaction through when the receipt, tender, balance, or audit record does not agree.
• Closing the record without manager verification, secure custody, and documented variance.

sops.title: POS Table Transfer SOP
sops.station: Part 6 — Pos, Cash, Discounts & Financial Controls
sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To transfer a POS table only after verifying the correct checks, destination table, server responsibility, guest status, and manager authority.
steps: Confirm the guest is physically moving to a different table and identify the current table, destination table, server assignment, and open checks involved.
Obtain manager approval when required, especially when the move crosses sections, combines parties, affects reservations, or changes server ownership.
Verify that the destination table is available, clean, correctly configured, and not reserved or blocked in the POS or seating system.

sops.title: POS Check Transfer Between Servers SOP
sops.station: Part 6 — Pos, Cash, Discounts & Financial Controls
sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To transfer an open check between servers without losing payment custody, table responsibility, discounts, tips, or the transaction audit trail.
steps: Identify the specific guest check or seat being reassigned and confirm the releasing server, receiving server, table, and reason for transfer.
Obtain required approval before transferring ownership, particularly after payment activity, discounts, alcohol service, tip entry, or shift checkout has begun.
Have both servers review the open items, modifiers, coursing, allergies, payments, guest requests, and unresolved service issues.
Select the approved POS check-transfer or server-transfer function; do not share login credentials or ring future items under the wrong employee.
Transfer only the intended check, seats, or items to the receiving server and preserve the original transaction history.
Confirm the receiving server can open the transferred check and that the releasing server no longer owns the transferred balance.
Verify totals, payment status, discounts, gratuity settings, and alcohol accountability after the transfer.
Communicate the handoff directly to the guest when appropriate and identify who will complete service and payment.
Escalate duplicate checks, locked checks, prior payments, tip disputes, or transfer errors to a manager before either employee checks out.
Record the transfer reason and approval when required and include the check in both servers' checkout review. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for POS check transfer between servers.

□ Select the approved POS check-transfer or server-transfer function; do not share login credentials or ring future items under the wrong employee.
□ Confirm the receiving server can open the transferred check and that the releasing server no longer owns the transferred balance.
□ Communicate the handoff directly to the guest when appropriate and identify who will complete service and payment.
□ Record the transfer reason and approval when required and include the check in both servers' checkout review.
sops.correction:
• Transferring a check without direct communication between releasing and receiving servers.
• Sharing employee login credentials or continuing to ring items under the wrong server.
• Moving the wrong seats or losing payment, discount, gratuity, or alcohol accountability.
• Allowing either server to check out before transfer discrepancies are resolved.
• Treating a server transfer as a table move and changing the guest location unnecessarily.

sops.purpose: To split POS checks accurately while preserving items, taxes, discounts, gratuities, payments, and guest-approved allocation.
steps: Identify the employee, guest check, drawer, payment, item, amount, and reason connected to POS split check.
Use only individual credentials and confirm the correct system, business date, location, and assigned custody.
Review the original ticket, receipt, authorization, balance, or supporting record before moving value.
Clarify whether the split is by seat, item, amount, percentage, or payment method before changing the check.
Assign every item, shared charge, tax, service charge, promotion, and tip line to the correct resulting check.
Review subtotals and explain any item that cannot be divided under policy before payment.
Process one payment at a time, return receipts correctly, and verify no balance remains.
Stop for manager review when identity, amount, authority, payment data, cash count, or audit information does not agree.
Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
Secure funds and records and document approvals, variances, disputes, and unusual activity. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.purpose: To review cash drawers for correct balance, transaction support, authorized adjustments, secure custody, and documented variances.
steps: Identify the drawer, assigned employee, shift, starting bank, sales period, drops, refunds, paid-outs, and authorized movements.
Secure the drawer in the approved count area with required employee or witness presence.
Count all cash and noncash items using the approved sequence and recount unusual denominations or bundles.
Compare the actual count with the POS expected amount and supporting transaction records.
Review drops, refunds, voids, comps, paid-outs, gift cards, and drawer transfers before classifying a variance.
Recount and verify the business date, employee, terminal, and tender report when totals do not agree.
Document the exact overage, shortage, explanation, employees present, and manager action.
Do not replace funds, borrow from another drawer, alter transactions, or ask an employee to repay outside policy.
Transfer funds and records into approved custody and restrict access after the count.
Sign the review and route repeated or material variances for authorized investigation and follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Sign the review and route repeated or material variances for authorized investigation and follow-up.

• Replacing, borrowing, or moving funds to hide a variance.

• Failing to document the variance, custody transfer, trend review, and authorized follow-up.

Complete the void under the manager's individual credentials without sharing access.
Verify the guest check, tax, tip, payment, inventory, and reporting effect after the void.
Document coaching, system error, product loss, or investigation follow-up when indicated.
Review void trends by employee, item, reason, and shift during reconciliation. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Approve only within assigned authority; escalate high-value, repeated, late, or suspicious requests.

sops.purpose: To approve comps only for authorized business reasons, within established limits, with accurate guest- check and manager documentation.
steps: Identify the guest, check, item, amount, complaint, and employee requesting the comp.
Verify the guest concern and distinguish a service-recovery comp from a void, discount, refund, spill, or employee meal.

Select the correct comp item and reason code and enter factual notes without private or inflammatory language.

Apply the comp under individual credentials and verify tax, tip, balance, and payment status.

□ Preserve product, check, witness, or incident information when the comp relates to safety or a disputed event.

• Failing to connect repeated comps with coaching, quality, timing, or system correction.

sops.title: Discount and Promotion Approval SOP
sops.station: Part 6 — Pos, Cash, Discounts & Financial Controls
sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To apply discounts and promotions only when eligibility, terms, dates, item limits, authorization, and POS entries are verified.
steps: Confirm the promotion, coupon, eligibility, date, location, items, exclusions, and required guest evidence.
Inspect the offer for alteration, duplication, expiration, unauthorized screenshots, or terms that do not match the current program.
Verify whether the offer can be combined with other discounts, gift cards, loyalty rewards, alcohol, or employee benefits.
Match the discount to the correct guest check and eligible items before applying it.
Obtain manager approval for overrides, exceptions, manual codes, or unclear terms.
Apply the approved code under individual credentials and retain or mark the coupon as required.
Verify the final price, tax, tip basis, tender, and guest receipt.
Explain any denial or limitation respectfully using the offer terms rather than personal judgment.
Document fraud concerns, repeated misuse, system problems, or guest disputes.
Reconcile manual discounts and retained offers at checkout or end of day. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for discount and promotion approval.
□ Inspect the offer for alteration, duplication, expiration, unauthorized screenshots, or terms that do not match the current program.
□ Match the discount to the correct guest check and eligible items before applying it.
□ Apply the approved code under individual credentials and retain or mark the coupon as required.
□ Explain any denial or limitation respectfully using the offer terms rather than personal judgment.
□ Reconcile manual discounts and retained offers at checkout or end of day.
sops.correction:
• Applying an expired, altered, duplicated, ineligible, or noncombinable offer.
• Discounting the wrong items or guest check.
• Overriding unclear terms without manager approval.
• Failing to retain, mark, or document the offer and manual code as required.
• Ending without verifying final price, tax, tip basis, tender, and misuse concerns.

sops.purpose: To process refunds through the original or approved payment method with verified authority, supporting records, and guest communication.
steps: Identify the employee, guest check, drawer, payment, item, amount, and reason connected to refund processing.
Use only individual credentials and confirm the correct system, business date, location, and assigned custody.
Review the original ticket, receipt, authorization, balance, or supporting record before moving value.
Verify the original transaction, guest identity as required, issue, payment method, amount, and prior recovery.
Obtain required approval and explain expected processing timing without promising bank-controlled results.
Process the refund through the approved system and original method unless policy authorizes otherwise.
Provide documentation, secure sensitive records, and reconcile the transaction.
Stop for manager review when identity, amount, authority, payment data, cash count, or audit information does not agree.
Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
Secure funds and records and document approvals, variances, disputes, and unusual activity. CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for refund processing.
□ Verify the original transaction, guest identity as required, issue, payment method, amount, and prior recovery.
□ Obtain required approval and explain expected processing timing without promising bank-controlled results.
□ Process the refund through the approved system and original method unless policy authorizes otherwise.
□ Provide documentation, secure sensitive records, and reconcile the transaction.
□ Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
sops.correction:
• Beginning refund processing without verifying the check, drawer, amount, reason, authority, and business date.
• Sharing credentials, bypassing required approval, or moving value outside the recorded system.
• Counting or reviewing funds where unauthorized employees or guests can observe or interfere.
• Forcing a transaction through when the receipt, tender, balance, or audit record does not agree.
• Closing the record without manager verification, secure custody, and documented variance.

sops.title: Gift Card Sale SOP
sops.station: Part 6 — Pos, Cash, Discounts & Financial Controls
sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To sell and activate gift cards accurately while protecting payment information, card inventory, activation records, and guest receipts.
steps: Confirm the requested gift-card type, amount, activation method, tender, fees, and any purchase limits.
Use only approved physical or digital cards from secure inventory.
Enter the sale under the correct POS function and verify the amount before activation.
Accept payment through the approved tender process and never activate a card without completed payment.
Confirm the activation result in the system and on the receipt without exposing the full card number or access code.
Provide the guest with the card, receipt, terms, and balance-check instructions.
Secure unused cards and record inventory movement when required.
Stop and notify the manager if activation fails, the card is damaged, inventory does not agree, or the transaction is disputed.
Process corrections or refunds only under the approved gift-card policy and authority.
Reconcile gift-card sales, activations, failures, and inventory at the required checkpoint. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for gift card sale.
□ Use only approved physical or digital cards from secure inventory.
□ Accept payment through the approved tender process and never activate a card without completed payment.
□ Provide the guest with the card, receipt, terms, and balance-check instructions.
□ Stop and notify the manager if activation fails, the card is damaged, inventory does not agree, or the transaction is disputed.
□ Reconcile gift-card sales, activations, failures, and inventory at the required checkpoint.
sops.correction:
• Activating a gift card before payment is complete or for the wrong amount.
• Using unsecured, damaged, or unapproved card inventory.
• Exposing the full card number or access code on notes or screens.
• Promising activation when the system result is uncertain.
• Failing to reconcile sales, activations, failures, corrections, and inventory.

sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To verify gift-card balances and redemptions accurately while protecting card information, remaining value, transaction records, and guest trust.
steps: Ask the guest to present the approved physical or digital gift card and confirm the requested use.
Access the gift-card function through individual credentials without writing down or exposing the full card number.
Verify the available balance through the approved system before promising payment coverage.
Apply the correct amount to the correct guest check and retain any remaining balance in the system.
Collect another tender for any unpaid balance and follow split-payment rules.
Return the physical card when required and provide a receipt showing the transaction and remaining balance when available.
Do not manually alter balances, transfer value, or override a failed redemption without authorization.
Stop and escalate damaged, unreadable, inactive, disputed, or suspicious cards.
Document system failures, guest disputes, duplicate charges, or manager-approved adjustments.
Verify gift-card activity during checkout or end-of-day reconciliation. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for gift card balance and redemption.
□ Access the gift-card function through individual credentials without writing down or exposing the full card number.
□ Apply the correct amount to the correct guest check and retain any remaining balance in the system.
□ Return the physical card when required and provide a receipt showing the transaction and remaining balance when available.
□ Stop and escalate damaged, unreadable, inactive, disputed, or suspicious cards.
□ Verify gift-card activity during checkout or end-of-day reconciliation.
sops.correction:
• Promising a balance before checking the approved system.
• Writing down, exposing, or manually changing gift-card credentials.
• Applying the card to the wrong check or amount.
• Overriding an inactive, damaged, suspicious, or failed card without authorization.
• Failing to provide the receipt, remaining balance, dispute record, and reconciliation.

sops.title: Chargeback and Payment Dispute Documentation SOP
sops.station: Part 6 — Pos, Cash, Discounts & Financial Controls
sops.frequency: Whenever the related POS, cash, payment, approval, refund, or reconciliation action is required.
sops.role: The employee uses individual credentials and preserves custody. The manager verifies authority, records, balances, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To document chargebacks and payment disputes with preserved receipts, approvals, transaction records, communication, and assigned response deadlines.
steps: Identify the employee, guest check, drawer, payment, item, amount, and reason connected to chargeback and payment dispute documentation.
Use only individual credentials and confirm the correct system, business date, location, and assigned custody.
Review the original ticket, receipt, authorization, balance, or supporting record before moving value.
Locate the exact transaction, date, time, amount, payment method, employee, and guest communication.
Collect itemized receipts, authorization records, refund history, tip record, and system logs.
Write an objective chronology and identify policy exceptions, equipment issues, and employee statements.
Route the packet securely by the deadline and record response and final outcome.
Stop for manager review when identity, amount, authority, payment data, cash count, or audit information does not agree.
Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
Secure funds and records and document approvals, variances, disputes, and unusual activity. Documentation SOP - VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can identify the authorized user, transaction record, approval requirement, custody point, and exception trigger for chargeback and payment dispute documentation.

□ Collect itemized receipts, authorization records, refund history, tip record, and system logs.
□ Write an objective chronology and identify policy exceptions, equipment issues, and employee statements.
□ Route the packet securely by the deadline and record response and final outcome.
□ Verify the final balance, receipt, tender, reason code, custody, and system status.
sops.correction:
• Beginning chargeback and payment dispute documentation without verifying the check, drawer, amount, reason, authority, and business date.
• Sharing credentials, bypassing required approval, or moving value outside the recorded system.
• Counting or reviewing funds where unauthorized employees or guests can observe or interfere.
• Forcing a transaction through when the receipt, tender, balance, or audit record does not agree.
• Closing the record without manager verification, secure custody, and documented variance.

sops.title: Manager Opening Walkthrough SOP
sops.frequency: Before the assigned station, department, or building begins service or changes opening responsibility.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To verify the restaurant is ready to open through a complete manager walkthrough of people, food, equipment, cleanliness, safety, cash, and systems.
steps: Review manager notes, staffing, reservations, events, weather, deliveries, maintenance holds, and expected business.
Inspect the exterior, parking, entrance, lobby, dining room, patio, restrooms, pickup area, and guest routes.
Verify lighting, climate, music, phones, reservations, POS, payment devices, alarms, locks, and required utilities.
Inspect bar, kitchen access, hand sinks, refrigeration, hot equipment, dish, storage, chemicals, and life-safety routes.
Confirm food-safety logs, temperatures, cleaning, product readiness, cash custody, keys, and department opening checklists.
Verify staffing assignments, call-offs, training needs, breaks, manager zones, and recovery authority.
Assign every correction to a named employee with priority and completion time.
Recheck hazards, food safety, cash, access, equipment, and guest-facing conditions before opening.
Restrict or delay any operation that cannot meet required safety or legal controls.
Sign the opening review and communicate remaining limitations and follow-up. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The manager begins manager opening walkthrough with current data and direct observation and assigns every unresolved item to an owner and deadline.
□ Inspect the exterior, parking, entrance, lobby, dining room, patio, restrooms, pickup area, and guest routes.
□ Inspect bar, kitchen access, hand sinks, refrigeration, hot equipment, dish, storage, chemicals, and life-safety routes.
□ Verify staffing assignments, call-offs, training needs, breaks, manager zones, and recovery authority.
□ Recheck hazards, food safety, cash, access, equipment, and guest-facing conditions before opening.
□ Sign the opening review and communicate remaining limitations and follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Relying on department sign-offs without physically inspecting critical conditions.
• Opening with unresolved food-safety, fire, access, cash, equipment, or guest-route hazards.
• Giving broad instructions without named owners, deadlines, and rechecks.
• Failing to restrict or delay an operation that cannot meet required controls.
• Signing ready without documenting limitations and next follow-up.

sops.title: Manager Closing Walkthrough SOP
sops.frequency: After active service ends and before employees are released or the building is secured.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To verify the restaurant is safely and completely closed through a manager walkthrough of guests, cash, food, equipment, utilities, security, and unfinished work.
steps: Review active guests, checks, employees, deliveries, incidents, maintenance, and unfinished department work.
Walk the exterior, parking, patio, entrance, dining room, restrooms, pickup area, and all guest-accessible spaces.
Confirm guests and employees have departed or are accounted for and no one remains in restricted areas.
Verify bar, kitchen, dish, storage, refrigeration, chemicals, grease, waste, and food disposition are complete.
Confirm cash, deposits, payment devices, keys, sensitive records, gift cards, and controlled product are secured.
Shut down or leave required equipment operating according to approved instructions and document exceptions.
Check doors, windows, exits, fire lanes, utilities, lights, climate, alarms, cameras, and locks.
Assign and recheck any incomplete cleaning, safety, maintenance, or security item before releasing employees.
Record unresolved conditions, service calls, incidents, and next-shift priorities in the manager log.
Complete final lock-up, arm the alarm, and transfer custody according to the keyholder process. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The manager begins manager closing walkthrough with current data and direct observation and assigns every unresolved item to an owner and deadline.
□ Walk the exterior, parking, patio, entrance, dining room, restrooms, pickup area, and all guest-accessible spaces.
□ Verify bar, kitchen, dish, storage, refrigeration, chemicals, grease, waste, and food disposition are complete.
□ Shut down or leave required equipment operating according to approved instructions and document exceptions.
□ Assign and recheck any incomplete cleaning, safety, maintenance, or security item before releasing employees.
□ Complete final lock-up, arm the alarm, and transfer custody according to the keyholder process.
sops.correction:
• Releasing employees before guests, active checks, food, cash, keys, and unfinished work are accounted for.
• Shutting down required equipment or leaving unsafe equipment, utilities, or product uncontrolled.
• Locking or arming without checking all rooms, exits, contractors, and remaining employees.
• Leaving unresolved cleaning, maintenance, incident, or security items undocumented.
• Failing to transfer final custody and next-shift priorities.

sourceSections.procedure:
1. Review active guests, checks, employees, deliveries, incidents, maintenance, and unfinished department work.
2. Walk the exterior, parking, patio, entrance, dining room, restrooms, pickup area, and all guest-accessible spaces.
3. Confirm guests and employees have departed or are accounted for and no one remains in restricted areas.
4. Verify bar, kitchen, dish, storage, refrigeration, chemicals, grease, waste, and food disposition are complete.
5. Confirm cash, deposits, payment devices, keys, sensitive records, gift cards, and controlled product are secured.
6. Shut down or leave required equipment operating according to approved instructions and document exceptions.
7. Check doors, windows, exits, fire lanes, utilities, lights, climate, alarms, cameras, and locks.
8. Assign and recheck any incomplete cleaning, safety, maintenance, or security item before releasing employees.
9. Record unresolved conditions, service calls, incidents, and next-shift priorities in the manager log.
10. Complete final lock-up, arm the alarm, and transfer custody according to the keyholder process. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Ticket-Time Monitoring SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled management checkpoint and whenever operating conditions require an additional review.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To monitor ticket times by service stage, identify emerging delays, assign corrective action, communicate updates, and document recurring causes.
steps: Review current staffing, guest, sales, ticket, safety, cash, and department information relevant to ticket-time monitoring.
Walk or observe the actual operation and compare conditions to the current approved standard.
Identify hazards, guest-impacting delays, capacity limits, and work that lacks a clear owner.
Review display or printed ticket times at regular intervals against standards by course and daypart.
Identify orders waiting on one station, held for timing, remade, missing, or not acknowledged.
Assign follow-up and obtain a realistic completion estimate from kitchen, expo, server, or manager.
Update guests proactively, track recovery, and record repeated delay causes.
Assign corrections to named employees with priority and completion times and communicate cross-department effects.
Recheck high-risk items and adjust the plan when conditions change or results remain below standard.
Record material decisions, exceptions, recoveries, and follow-up for the next manager or review cycle. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The manager begins ticket-time monitoring with current data and direct observation and assigns every unresolved item to an owner and deadline.
□ Review display or printed ticket times at regular intervals against standards by course and daypart.
□ Identify orders waiting on one station, held for timing, remade, missing, or not acknowledged.
□ Assign follow-up and obtain a realistic completion estimate from kitchen, expo, server, or manager.
□ Update guests proactively, track recovery, and record repeated delay causes.
□ Recheck high-risk items and adjust the plan when conditions change or results remain below standard.
sops.correction:
• Making a decision about ticket-time monitoring from reports alone without observing actual conditions.
• Giving a general instruction without a named owner, priority, completion time, and recheck.
• Allowing guest, safety, staffing, cash, or quality risks to remain unassigned.
• Failing to communicate cross-department effects or changing conditions.
• Ending the review without documenting material decisions, exceptions, and follow-up.

sops.title: Quality and Cleanliness Walkthrough SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled management checkpoint and whenever operating conditions require an additional review.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To inspect food quality, cleanliness, safety, organization, and guest-facing conditions throughout the shift and verify timely corrections.
steps: Review current staffing, guest, sales, ticket, safety, cash, and department information relevant to quality and cleanliness walkthrough.
Walk or observe the actual operation and compare conditions to the current approved standard.
Identify hazards, guest-impacting delays, capacity limits, and work that lacks a clear owner.
Walk exterior, entrance, host, dining, bar, restrooms, service stations, visible kitchen, and pickup zones.
Check floors, tables, touchpoints, trash, odors, lighting, temperatures, music, uniforms, food presentation, and clutter.

Recheck completion and document maintenance or repeated failures.
Assign corrections to named employees with priority and completion times and communicate cross-department effects.

sops.title: Manager Table Visit SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled management checkpoint and whenever operating conditions require an additional review.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To conduct purposeful manager table visits that confirm guest satisfaction, identify concerns early, and support the service team without interrupting the meal.
steps: Review current staffing, guest, sales, ticket, safety, cash, and department information relevant to manager table visit.
Walk or observe the actual operation and compare conditions to the current approved standard.
Identify hazards, guest-impacting delays, capacity limits, and work that lacks a clear owner.
Review table, server, order status, special occasion, allergy, delay, or recovery reason before approaching.
Introduce yourself, ask a focused open question, and observe food, beverages, table condition, and guest response.
Address simple needs immediately and take ownership of concerns.

sops.title: Manager Cash Drawer Review SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled management checkpoint and whenever operating conditions require an additional review.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To review manager-controlled cash drawers for correct balance, authorization, supporting records, custody, and timely investigation of variances.
steps: Review current staffing, guest, sales, ticket, safety, cash, and department information relevant to manager cash drawer review.
Walk or observe the actual operation and compare conditions to the current approved standard.
Identify hazards, guest-impacting delays, capacity limits, and work that lacks a clear owner.
Confirm the assigned employee, drawer, starting bank, sales period, drops, paid-outs, refunds, and authorized movements.
Count cash in the approved secure area with required employee or second-manager presence.
Compare actual funds to expected cash and review transaction records before concluding a variance exists.
Recount, document explanations, secure funds and evidence, and follow the approved variance process.
Assign corrections to named employees with priority and completion times and communicate cross-department effects.
Recheck high-risk items and adjust the plan when conditions change or results remain below standard.
Record material decisions, exceptions, recoveries, and follow-up for the next manager or review cycle. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.frequency: Immediately when the concern, report, unsafe condition, or incident is observed or received.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To document incidents with objective facts, protected information, required evidence, notifications, corrective action, and assigned follow-up.
steps: Review current staffing, guest, sales, ticket, safety, cash, and department information relevant to manager incident documentation.
Walk or observe the actual operation and compare conditions to the current approved standard.
Identify hazards, guest-impacting delays, capacity limits, and work that lacks a clear owner.
Secure immediate safety, preserve the scene or records, and identify the reporting manager.
Collect separate statements, witness contacts, times, locations, checks, photographs, and system information as permitted.
Write a chronological account distinguishing direct observation from reported information.
Record actions and notifications, sign and secure the report, and assign follow-up.
Assign corrections to named employees with priority and completion times and communicate cross-department effects.

sops.title: Manager Daily SOP Compliance Review SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled management checkpoint and whenever operating conditions require an additional review.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To verify daily compliance with selected high-risk and high-frequency SOPs, document exceptions, assign correction, and confirm retraining when needed.
steps: Review the shift's assigned SOP compliance priorities, high-risk tasks, prior exceptions, and outstanding corrective actions before the first walkthrough.
Observe employees performing selected procedures in real time rather than relying only on completed checklists or verbal assurances.
Compare observed actions with the current approved SOP, including sequence, safety controls, required documentation, and escalation points.
Verify critical records such as temperatures, cash approvals, cleaning checks, training sign-offs, or opening/closing tasks against observable conditions.
Correct immediate safety, food-safety, security, or financial-control failures at once and stop the task when continuation would create risk.
Coach minor execution gaps using the exact standard, then require the employee to repeat or demonstrate the corrected step.
Record the SOP reviewed, employees or area observed, result, exception, correction, and responsible follow-up owner.
Look for patterns across employees, shifts, equipment, workload, or unclear instructions instead of treating every miss as individual carelessness.
Escalate repeated, serious, or system-wide noncompliance according to the restaurant's accountability and retraining process.
Close the daily review by confirming urgent corrections are complete and carrying unresolved items into the manager log and next-shift handoff. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Manager Weekly SOP Review SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled management checkpoint and whenever operating conditions require an additional review.
sops.role: The manager reviews conditions, assigns owners and deadlines, verifies completion, and documents material exceptions.
sops.purpose: To review SOP performance weekly, identify recurring failures or outdated procedures, assign revisions, and verify training and document control.
steps: Gather the week's daily compliance reviews, incident reports, retraining records, audit results, guest complaints, safety events, and manager logs.
Group findings by SOP, department, shift, employee role, risk level, and recurrence so isolated errors are separated from operating patterns.
Verify that every high-risk exception received immediate containment and that promised corrective actions were completed.
Identify procedures that are unclear, outdated, impractical, poorly trained, inconsistently supervised, or affected by changed equipment or policy.
Review completion and quality trends for required logs, checklists, approvals, and sign-offs rather than counting paperwork alone.
Select the highest-priority SOPs for observation, coaching, retraining, revision, or leadership follow-up during the coming week.
Assign a named owner, due date, verification method, and escalation threshold for each corrective action.
Communicate relevant findings to department leaders without exposing confidential employee information or using the review to shame individuals.
Update the master SOP review or revision record when a procedure requires formal change, approval, version control, and retraining.
Document the weekly conclusion, unresolved risks, next review date, and items that must be reported to ownership or senior leadership. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.purpose: To receive employee call-offs consistently, document required facts, protect privacy, assess coverage, and apply attendance policy through authorized management.
steps: Review the current schedule, policy, SOP, training record, and facts relevant to employee call-off.
Meet or communicate through the approved channel and protect privacy from guests and uninvolved employees.
State or request specific facts and listen without labels, rumors, ridicule, diagnosis, or premature conclusions.
Record employee, shift, position, call time, approved contact method, and stated availability information.
Avoid unnecessary medical details and explain required documentation or next steps under policy.
Notify management, update the schedule, and begin qualified coverage without making premature promises.
Confirm receipt, record attempts and decisions, and route protected-leave questions appropriately.
Explain the next operational step, expected conduct, coverage, training, or authorized review process.
Document necessary facts and route protected, formal, safety, or job-status matters to authorized leadership.
Set a follow-up owner and time and verify coverage, nonretaliation, training, or corrective commitments. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:

□ Record employee, shift, position, call time, approved contact method, and stated availability information.
□ Avoid unnecessary medical details and explain required documentation or next steps under policy.
□ Notify management, update the schedule, and begin qualified coverage without making premature promises.
□ Confirm receipt, record attempts and decisions, and route protected-leave questions appropriately.
□ Document necessary facts and route protected, formal, safety, or job-status matters to authorized leadership.
sops.correction:
• Addressing employee call-off publicly or relying on rumor, labels, personality judgments, or unnecessary medical details.
• Applying a standard inconsistently or making a job-status promise outside assigned authority.
• Failing to protect good-faith reporting, accommodation routing, privacy, or nonretaliation requirements.
• Documenting conclusions instead of specific observed or reported facts and employee response.
• Ending the conversation without a clear operational next step, owner, timing, and follow-up.

sops.title: No-Call/No-Show Response SOP
sops.frequency: Immediately when the concern, report, unsafe condition, or incident is observed or received.
sops.role: The manager responds privately and consistently, records objective facts, and routes protected or formal matters to authorized leadership.
sops.purpose: To respond to a no-call/no-show promptly through welfare and contact checks, coverage decisions, objective documentation, and authorized policy action.
steps: Review the current schedule, policy, SOP, training record, and facts relevant to no-call/no-show response.
Meet or communicate through the approved channel and protect privacy from guests and uninvolved employees.
State or request specific facts and listen without labels, rumors, ridicule, diagnosis, or premature conclusions.
Verify the schedule, approved changes, prior messages, and that the employee has not contacted another leader.
Attempt contact through approved methods and record each attempt without broad disclosure.

sops.title: Shift Swap Approval SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the related employee communication, conduct, scheduling, training, or documentation need occurs.
sops.role: The manager responds privately and consistently, records objective facts, and routes protected or formal matters to authorized leadership.
sops.purpose: To approve or deny shift swaps only after verifying employee qualifications, overtime impact, coverage, accountability, and required manager authorization.
steps: Review the current schedule, policy, SOP, training record, and facts relevant to shift swap approval.
Meet or communicate through the approved channel and protect privacy from guests and uninvolved employees.
State or request specific facts and listen without labels, rumors, ridicule, diagnosis, or premature conclusions.
Require the request through the approved method with employees, shifts, positions, and dates clearly identified.
Verify agreement, training, availability, hour limits, and absence of unapproved conflicts.
Obtain manager approval before the change is treated as final and update the official schedule.
Notify affected leaders and document who retains responsibility until approval.
Explain the next operational step, expected conduct, coverage, training, or authorized review process.
Document necessary facts and route protected, formal, safety, or job-status matters to authorized leadership.
Set a follow-up owner and time and verify coverage, nonretaliation, training, or corrective commitments. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Notify affected leaders and document who retains responsibility until approval.

sops.title: Uniform and Grooming Check SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the related employee communication, conduct, scheduling, training, or documentation need occurs.
sops.role: The manager responds privately and consistently, records objective facts, and routes protected or formal matters to authorized leadership.
sops.purpose: To verify uniform and grooming standards respectfully before and during the shift and correct safety, sanitation, or presentation issues consistently.
steps: Review the current schedule, policy, SOP, training record, and facts relevant to uniform and grooming check.
Meet or communicate through the approved channel and protect privacy from guests and uninvolved employees.
State or request specific facts and listen without labels, rumors, ridicule, diagnosis, or premature conclusions.
Inspect required uniform pieces, cleanliness, name tag, hair restraint, hands, nails, jewelry, footwear, and role-specific protective items.
Address concerns privately and identify the exact standard rather than making personal comments.
Provide or approve a reasonable correction and remove the employee from unsafe duties until corrected.
Document repeated issues and route accommodation or medical questions to authorized leadership.
Explain the next operational step, expected conduct, coverage, training, or authorized review process.
Document necessary facts and route protected, formal, safety, or job-status matters to authorized leadership.

sops.title: Trainer Assignment and Handoff SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever responsibility, custody, information, or an active order transfers between employees.
sops.role: The releasing employee gives complete information. The receiving employee confirms acceptance; management resolves exceptions.
sops.purpose: To assign the correct trainer and transfer the training plan, completed work, employee needs, standards, and next verification responsibilities.
steps: Identify the exact order, guest, station, transaction, custody, and time period covered by trainer assignment and handoff.
Conduct the transfer directly whenever possible and use the approved written or electronic record.
Review active work, deadlines, high-risk conditions, and items awaiting manager action.
Confirm the trainer is qualified, scheduled, and informed of the employee role and planned tasks.
Review completed modules, strengths, safety limits, unfinished practice, questions, and verification results.
Set next-shift objectives, demonstration tasks, practice limits, and manager checkpoints.
Both trainers and management acknowledge the handoff and update the official training record.
Require repeat-back of critical allergy, cash, identity, safety, timing, and guest information.
Assign a named owner and due time for every unresolved item and inform management of exceptions.
Both employees acknowledge the transfer; responsibility remains with the releasing employee until acceptance is clear. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

Meet or communicate through the approved channel and protect privacy from guests and uninvolved employees.
State or request specific facts and listen without labels, rumors, ridicule, diagnosis, or premature conclusions.
Record the date, shift, specific behavior, standard demonstrated, and positive impact.
Confirm the recognition is accurate and protects private guest and employee information.
Deliver praise promptly and specifically through the approved public or private method.
Add the note to the appropriate performance record and consider fair formal recognition.
Explain the next operational step, expected conduct, coverage, training, or authorized review process.
Document necessary facts and route protected, formal, safety, or job-status matters to authorized leadership.
Set a follow-up owner and time and verify coverage, nonretaliation, training, or corrective commitments. SOP - VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

PART 9 OPENING, CLOSING & BUILDING SECURITY 5 ready-to-customize SOPs These SOPs coordinate front-of-house opening and closing, final building checks, alarm control, locks, keys, and access accountability.

sops.title: FOH Opening SOP
sops.frequency: Before the assigned station, department, or building begins service or changes opening responsibility.
sops.role: Assigned employees complete the opening work. The manager or shift lead verifies readiness before service begins.
sops.purpose: To open front-of-house areas with verified cleanliness, supplies, equipment, cash controls, staffing, safety, and manager release.
steps: Review the current FOH opening checklist, expected business, assignments, and manager notes.
Gather approved tools and obtain only authorized cash, keys, product, or system access.
Inspect the assigned area for damage, contamination, shortages, unsafe conditions, and incomplete prior work.
Inspect entrances, exterior approach, lobby, dining, restrooms, bar, patio, pickup, and service stations.
Activate or secure lighting, climate, music, POS, phones, reservations, payment, cash, menus, alcohol access, and devices.
Verify or complete tables, supplies, cleaning, accessibility routes, staffing, active checks, and department assignments.
Correct hazards and shortages, complete sign-offs, and obtain manager authorization to open or proceed to lock-up.
Correct and report shortages, equipment problems, unsafe conditions, or incomplete work before service.
Complete a final readiness check and demonstrate critical controls requested by management.
Record completion and obtain manager or shift-lead release before the area begins service. CUSTOMIZATION

□ The assigned keyholder confirms authority, people, access devices, security contacts, and unresolved conditions before FOH opening.

□ Activate or secure lighting, climate, music, POS, phones, reservations, payment, cash, menus, alcohol access, and devices.
□ Verify or complete tables, supplies, cleaning, accessibility routes, staffing, active checks, and department assignments.
□ Correct hazards and shortages, complete sign-offs, and obtain manager authorization to open or proceed to lock-up.
□ Complete a final readiness check and demonstrate critical controls requested by management.
sops.correction:
• Starting FOH opening from memory instead of the current checklist and manager notes.
• Opening with a shortage, hazard, unverified system, or incomplete prior-shift work.
• Using unassigned cash, keys, product, credentials, or equipment access.
• Correcting a problem without recording it or informing the responsible manager.
• Signing the area ready before the final manager verification.

sops.title: FOH Closing SOP
sops.frequency: After active service ends and before employees are released or the building is secured.
sops.role: Assigned employees complete closing work. The manager verifies sanitation, cash, security, and unresolved conditions before release.
sops.purpose: To close front-of-house areas by completing guest service, cash and key custody, cleaning, restocking, security, and next-shift preparation.
steps: Review the current FOH closing checklist and confirm management has approved the start of closing work.
Identify active guests, orders, checks, cash, controlled product, and duties that must remain available.
Gather approved cleaning, storage, waste, and security supplies without obstructing operating areas.
Inspect entrances, exterior approach, lobby, dining, restrooms, bar, patio, pickup, and service stations.
Activate or secure lighting, climate, music, POS, phones, reservations, payment, cash, menus, alcohol access, and devices.
Verify or complete tables, supplies, cleaning, accessibility routes, staffing, active checks, and department assignments.
Correct hazards and shortages, complete sign-offs, and obtain manager authorization to open or proceed to lock-up.
Report breakage, shortage, maintenance, safety, cash, or guest issues and assign unresolved follow-up.
Complete the final checklist and walk the area with the manager or designated verifier.
Sign off only after work is accepted and remaining responsibility is formally transferred. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: End-of-Night Building Check SOP
sops.frequency: After active service ends and before employees are released or the building is secured.
sops.role: The authorized manager completes the security sequence, controls credentials, and transfers unresolved risk to the proper contact.
sops.purpose: To verify at the end of night that all people have exited, hazards are controlled, utilities and equipment are secure, and required records are complete.
steps: Confirm authorization and obtain the checklist, keys, access devices, contacts, and accountability information for end-of-night building check.
Account for employees, guests, contractors, active transactions, and conditions that prevent secure closure or access control.
Use the approved route and sequence; do not enter or remain in an area that appears unsafe or unlawfully accessed.
Inspect dining, bar, kitchen, restrooms, office, storage, coolers, exterior, and hidden areas by the approved route.
Confirm no guest, employee, contractor, open flame, active cooking, leak, unsecured chemical, or immediate hazard remains.
Check refrigeration, ventilation, doors, windows, gates, cash storage, keys, and systems that must remain on or off.
Document unresolved conditions and do not leave until responsibility is transferred.
Stop and contact management, alarm company, security, or emergency services when a condition cannot be resolved.
Verify locks, alarms, keys, utilities, access, and final custody through physical or system confirmation.
Record time, employee, credential, result, and exception before departure or transfer. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Confirm no guest, employee, contractor, open flame, active cooking, leak, unsecured chemical, or immediate hazard remains.
□ Check refrigeration, ventilation, doors, windows, gates, cash storage, keys, and systems that must remain on or off.
□ Document unresolved conditions and do not leave until responsibility is transferred.
□ Verify locks, alarms, keys, utilities, access, and final custody through physical or system confirmation.

• Sharing keys, codes, cards, or access information or leaving credentials unsecured.
• Locking, arming, or leaving without accounting for people and unresolved building conditions.
• Ignoring an alarm fault, lost credential, unsafe entry condition, or incomplete custody transfer.
• Failing to record time, employee, credential, result, exception, and final responsibility.

2. Account for employees, guests, contractors, active transactions, and conditions that prevent secure closure or access control.
3. Use the approved route and sequence; do not enter or remain in an area that appears unsafe or unlawfully accessed.
4. Confirm the building check is complete and account for employees, guests, contractors, and authorized vehicles.
5. Lock interior controlled areas and exterior doors in the approved sequence while maintaining a safe final exit.
6. Arm the alarm with individual authorization and verify acceptance, zone status, and error messages.
7. Confirm final doors, record departure, and contact the alarm company or manager for unresolved faults.
8. Stop and contact management, alarm company, security, or emergency services when a condition cannot be resolved.
9. Verify locks, alarms, keys, utilities, access, and final custody through physical or system confirmation.
10. Record time, employee, credential, result, and exception before departure or transfer. CUSTOMIZATION

• Beginning alarm and lock-up without authorization, accountability, required contacts, and the current security checklist.

• Ignoring an alarm fault, lost credential, unsafe entry condition, or incomplete custody transfer.

sops.title: Delivery Receiving SOP
sops.frequency: During each delivery, storage transfer, inventory count, or product-control review covered by this SOP.
sops.role: The receiver performs and records checks. The manager authorizes rejection, correction, storage exceptions, and vendor follow-up.
sops.purpose: To accept, reject, document, and route incoming product only after the required source, condition, quantity, temperature, allergen, and invoice controls for delivery receiving are verified.
steps: Review the approved order, vendor, schedule, limits, storage plan, and prior manager notes.
Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
Confirm responsibility and keep delivery product separated from food preparation and guest traffic.
Match the delivery to the approved vendor, schedule, purchase record, and receiving location.
Inspect the vehicle, seals, packaging, dates, cleanliness, and evidence of contamination or pests.
Separate accepted, held, and rejected items and obtain vendor acknowledgment of exceptions.
Sign only after quantities, condition, temperatures, and disposition are accurately recorded.
Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
Record rejected, held, substituted, damaged, short, or credited product and obtain required signatures.
Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management.
