□ Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
□ Match the delivery to the approved vendor, schedule, purchase record, and receiving location.
□ Separate accepted, held, and rejected items and obtain vendor acknowledgment of exceptions.
□ Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
□ Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management.

• Starting delivery receiving before the approved source, order, product, tools, and receiving area are confirmed.
• Accepting or storing product before quantity, condition, temperature, date, and label checks are complete.
• Allowing questionable or rejected product to mix with accepted inventory.
• Recording exceptions after the driver leaves instead of at the point of receiving.
• Failing to obtain manager disposition and preserve the invoice, credit, and traceability record.

sops.title: Delivery Temperature Verification SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To verify delivery temperatures with a clean, calibrated thermometer and reject, hold, or escalate product that does not meet approved limits.
steps: Notify the manager or designated food-safety leader before proceeding with an uncertain high-risk condition.
Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
Isolate affected food and prevent sale, use, movement, or disposal until authorized.
Select representative products and sanitize the calibrated probe between products.
Measure in the approved location without damaging packaging or contaminating food.
Compare results to the current approved receiving limits for each food type.
Reject or hold product outside limits and record product, lot, temperature, time, and manager decision.
Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
Record all measurements, time, product, quantity, disposition, decision, and responsible people.
Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service.
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the product, approved source, required limit, record, and rejection or escalation authority for delivery temperature verification.
□ Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
□ Select representative products and sanitize the calibrated probe between products.
□ Compare results to the current approved receiving limits for each food type.
□ Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
□ Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service.
sops.correction:
• Checking delivery temperature verification with an unclean, uncalibrated, or inappropriate thermometer.
• Measuring only the equipment display, container surface, or an unrepresentative location.
• Delaying the reading or recording a rounded, estimated, or backfilled result.
• Keeping product in service when the required limit or time history is uncertain.
• Failing to document corrective action, product disposition, and manager verification.

• Current regulatory and restaurant standard
• Calibrated thermometer, timer, or approved test device
• Protected containers, labels, PPE, and sanitizer
• Corrective-action and food-disposition record
• Manager and regulatory contact information

sops.frequency: During each delivery, storage transfer, inventory count, or product-control review covered by this SOP.

sops.purpose: To accept, reject, document, and route incoming product only after the required source, condition, quantity, temperature, allergen, and invoice controls for allergen-sensitive product receiving are verified.
steps: Review the approved order, vendor, schedule, limits, storage plan, and prior manager notes.
Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
Confirm responsibility and keep delivery product separated from food preparation and guest traffic.
Identify allergen-sensitive items and compare labels, ingredients, seals, and substitutions to the approved order.
Reject unapproved substitutions or damaged packaging that makes ingredient identity uncertain.
Keep packages closed and separated from leaking or dusty products during receiving.
Label and transfer the item directly to its designated protected storage location.
Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
Record rejected, held, substituted, damaged, short, or credited product and obtain required signatures.
Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management.

□ Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
□ Identify allergen-sensitive items and compare labels, ingredients, seals, and substitutions to the approved order.
□ Keep packages closed and separated from leaking or dusty products during receiving.
□ Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
□ Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management.
sops.correction:
• Accepting product with missing, damaged, changed, or unreadable ingredient and allergen labels.
• Assuming a substitute or new formulation matches the previously approved product.
• Storing allergen-sensitive product where leaking or open ingredients can contact it.
• Removing manufacturer packaging before traceability information is retained.
• Failing to notify managers and recipe owners about ingredient or supplier changes.

sops.title: Food Storage Hierarchy SOP
sops.frequency: During each delivery, storage transfer, inventory count, or product-control review covered by this SOP.
sops.role: The receiver performs and records checks. The manager authorizes rejection, correction, storage exceptions, and vendor follow-up.
sops.purpose: To store food in the approved hierarchy so raw products cannot contaminate ready-to-eat food and every item remains identifiable and accessible.
steps: Review the approved order, vendor, schedule, limits, storage plan, and prior manager notes.
Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
Confirm responsibility and keep delivery product separated from food preparation and guest traffic.
Place ready-to-eat food above raw animal products and separate products by required cooking risk.
Keep chemicals, personal items, damaged product, and returned items outside food-storage zones.
Use shelves, pans, and containers that prevent leakage and cross-contamination.
Correct misplaced product immediately and document repeated or high-risk findings.
Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
Record rejected, held, substituted, damaged, short, or credited product and obtain required signatures.
Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management.
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the product, approved source, required limit, record, and rejection or escalation authority for food storage hierarchy.
□ Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
□ Place ready-to-eat food above raw animal products and separate products by required cooking risk.
□ Use shelves, pans, and containers that prevent leakage and cross-contamination.
□ Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
□ Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management.
sops.correction:
• Placing product into food storage hierarchy without verifying identity, label, date, condition, and approved location.
• Storing raw, ready-to-eat, allergen, chemical, or guest-use items in an unsafe relationship.
• Blocking airflow, drains, sprinklers, access, cleaning, or temperature monitoring.
• Leaving open, leaking, damaged, or unprotected containers in service.
• Failing to correct and document repeated organization, temperature, pest, or rotation problems.

sops.title: FIFO Rotation SOP
sops.frequency: During each delivery, storage transfer, inventory count, or product-control review covered by this SOP.
sops.role: The receiver performs and records checks. The manager authorizes rejection, correction, storage exceptions, and vendor follow-up.
sops.purpose: To rotate inventory using FIFO so older usable product is selected first and expired, damaged, or questionable product is controlled.
steps: Review the approved order, vendor, schedule, limits, storage plan, and prior manager notes.
Prepare a clean receiving area and gather calibrated tools, records, labels, and required PPE.
Confirm responsibility and keep delivery product separated from food preparation and guest traffic.
Locate the oldest acceptable product by approved date, lot, or receiving sequence.
Move older product to the first-use position without hiding newer product or damaging packages.
Check quality and expiration before combining or using product.
Record and escalate excessive age, repeated rotation failures, or product that cannot be used safely.
Move accepted food promptly to approved storage and maintain cold, frozen, dry, and allergen controls.
Record rejected, held, substituted, damaged, short, or credited product and obtain required signatures.
Clean the receiving area and submit records, photos, and unresolved issues to management. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Inventory Count SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled count, shift cutoff, delivery review, variance investigation, or controlled-product check.
sops.role: Counters record actual quantities without adjustment. Management verifies variances, custody, and follow-up.
sops.purpose: To complete accurate inventory counts using approved units, locations, cutoff rules, product movement controls, and variance review.
steps: Review the approved count list, locations, units, cutoff time, and access controls.
Freeze or record product movement according to the count plan and assign independent sections.
Gather clean counting tools and verify scales, labels, and system access.
Freeze movement during the count and use the approved location sequence.
Count sealed, open, prepared, and in-use product in the approved unit of measure.
Record actual quantities immediately and mark items that require weighing or conversion.
Recount material differences and submit the count without undocumented adjustment.
Recheck material differences and secure controlled products after the count.
Submit actual quantities, conversion notes, movement records, and unresolved variances.
Management signs the count and assigns investigation or corrective action. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the product, approved source, required limit, record, and rejection or escalation authority for inventory count.
□ Freeze or record product movement according to the count plan and assign independent sections.
□ Freeze movement during the count and use the approved location sequence.
□ Record actual quantities immediately and mark items that require weighing or conversion.
□ Recheck material differences and secure controlled products after the count.
□ Management signs the count and assigns investigation or corrective action.
sops.correction:
• Counting inventory count with inconsistent units, unorganized storage, or active product movement.
• Estimating open containers without the approved method.
• Changing counts to match expectations instead of recounting and documenting variance.
• Allowing unauthorized access or failing to preserve custody during the count.
• Ending without manager review of material variance, waste, transfer, and purchase records.

sops.title: High-Cost Item Control SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled count, shift cutoff, delivery review, variance investigation, or controlled-product check.
sops.role: Counters record actual quantities without adjustment. Management verifies variances, custody, and follow-up.
sops.purpose: To protect high-cost products through restricted access, accurate counts, documented movement, variance review, and manager accountability.
steps: Review the approved count list, locations, units, cutoff time, and access controls.
Freeze or record product movement according to the count plan and assign independent sections.
Gather clean counting tools and verify scales, labels, and system access.
Restrict access and record issue, return, waste, transfer, comp, and count activity for controlled items.
Use approved portions, scales, locks, cameras, or dual verification where assigned.
Compare usage and sales to beginning, received, transferred, and ending quantities.
Investigate and document unexplained variance without accusing employees or altering records.
Recheck material differences and secure controlled products after the count.
Submit actual quantities, conversion notes, movement records, and unresolved variances.
Management signs the count and assigns investigation or corrective action. CUSTOMIZATION

• Ending without manager review of material variance, waste, transfer, and purchase records.

sops.title: Product Recall Response SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To control product recall response consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Notify the manager or designated food-safety leader before proceeding with an uncertain high-risk condition.
Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
Isolate affected food and prevent sale, use, movement, or disposal until authorized.
Identify the affected item, brand, lot, date, supplier, and recall instructions.
Stop sale and use, search every storage and service location, and isolate affected product.
Mark the hold clearly and prevent return to inventory except through authorized disposition.
Document quantity, location, guest or sales traceability, vendor contact, disposal or return, and final verification.
Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
Record all measurements, time, product, quantity, disposition, decision, and responsible people.
Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Prep Area Opening SOP
sops.frequency: Before prep work begins, before product is pulled, or before the prep cook starts the assigned prep list.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows the approved recipe and production plan. A lead or manager verifies quality, yield, labeling, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To make sure the prep station is clean, organized, stocked, and ready before prep work begins.
steps: Wash hands before beginning prep setup.
Check that the prep table and work area are clean.
Remove trash, dirty towels, old labels, food debris, and clutter.
Set up sanitizer and clean towels according to restaurant policy.
Gather required cutting boards, knives, containers, portion tools, labels, and markers.
Review the prep list for the shift.
Review recipe cards or prep specifications if needed.
Check par levels and expected volume.
Pull product according to prep needs.
Check product quality, labels, dates, freshness, and storage capacity; obtain manager release before prep begins. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Prep List Completion SOP
sops.frequency: Before and during each assigned preparation or production cycle and whenever product is transferred or stored.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows the approved recipe and production plan. A lead or manager verifies quality, yield, labeling, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To complete the prep list with accurate priorities, quantities, assignments, deadlines, and status updates based on the approved production plan.
steps: Review the production forecast, reservations, events, current sales trend, weather, and manager priorities.
Count usable carryover and on-hand product; confirm labels, shelf life, quality, and available storage space.
Compare projected need with on-hand quantity using the restaurant's approved par, yield, and batch standards.
List each item, required quantity, batch size, priority, station, and completion time.
Sequence work by food-safety risk, cook/cool time, shelf life, service urgency, and shared-equipment demand.
Assign each item to a trained employee and confirm recipe, tools, ingredients, and allergen controls.
Record start, completion, actual yield, waste, shortage, substitution, and unfinished work as production occurs.
Recalculate remaining needs when sales, staffing, product, or reservations change; obtain approval before overproducing.
Label, date, cool, store, stage, or transfer completed product according to the approved process.
Review the completed list with the manager and hand off shortages, variances, and next-shift needs. CUSTOMIZATION

steps: Review the seafood species, source information, shellfish tags when applicable, recipe, portion, thaw status, and batch need.

Cut and portion according to recipe, verify weight and appearance, and record yield, waste, and product concerns.
Return prepared seafood to covered labeled refrigeration immediately; do not allow prolonged room-temperature staging.
Clean and sanitize boards, knives, sinks, equipment, and handles and control shell, bone, and packaging waste.
Wash hands and obtain manager review for off odor, damaged packaging, traceability gaps, parasites, or uncertain quality. CUSTOMIZATION

Record shortage, excess, waste, substitution, quality issue, and manager-approved correction.

sops.title: Cooling Prepared Food for Storage SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To cool prepared food for storage within approved time and temperature limits, document results, and take immediate corrective action when limits are missed.
steps: Notify the manager or designated food-safety leader before proceeding with an uncertain high-risk condition.
Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
Isolate affected food and prevent sale, use, movement, or disposal until authorized.
Divide food into shallow approved containers or smaller portions and begin cooling without delay.
Use approved rapid-cooling methods while protecting food from contamination.
Measure and record temperatures at required intervals using a sanitized calibrated probe.
If the approved cooling limit is missed, reheat, recool, or discard only under manager direction.
Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
Record all measurements, time, product, quantity, disposition, decision, and responsible people.
Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can identify the recipe or plan, batch or yield, required controls, storage result, and manager escalation point for cooling prepared food for storage.
□ Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
□ Divide food into shallow approved containers or smaller portions and begin cooling without delay.
□ Measure and record temperatures at required intervals using a sanitized calibrated probe.
□ Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
□ Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service.
sops.correction:
• Beginning cooling prepared food for storage without the approved time-temperature method, container depth, label, and storage space.
• Using room temperature, deep covered containers, standing water, or another unapproved method.
• Combining warm and cold product or overloading refrigeration and airflow.
• Failing to monitor and record required times and temperatures.
• Keeping product when the control history or limit is uncertain instead of escalating.

sops.title: Cross-Contamination Prevention During Prep SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To prevent cross-contamination during prep by separating raw and ready-to-eat food, tools, surfaces, storage, employee movement, and cleaning tasks.
steps: Notify the manager or designated food-safety leader before proceeding with an uncertain high-risk condition.
Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
Isolate affected food and prevent sale, use, movement, or disposal until authorized.
Separate raw and ready-to-eat work by time, space, tools, containers, and employee practices.
Wash hands and clean and sanitize the area before changing products or tasks.
Use designated boards, knives, pans, gloves, and storage locations.
Stop work and evaluate all affected food and surfaces after any suspected cross-contamination.
Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
Record all measurements, time, product, quantity, disposition, decision, and responsible people.
Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service. - VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:

□ Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
□ Separate raw and ready-to-eat work by time, space, tools, containers, and employee practices.
□ Use designated boards, knives, pans, gloves, and storage locations.
□ Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
□ Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service.
sops.correction:
• Starting cross-contamination prevention during prep without clean hands, protected ingredients, sanitized tools, and a controlled work area.
• Using shared towels, gloves, utensils, containers, fryers, or surfaces without approved controls.
• Relying on visible removal instead of remaking product after possible contact.
• Failing to verify ingredient labels and communicate directly with the designated leader.
• Continuing when product identity, cleaning, or cross-contact history is uncertain.

sops.frequency: Any time product is discarded, spoiled, trimmed excessively, overproduced, incorrectly prepared, damaged, expired, or unusable.
sops.role: The assigned employee follows the approved recipe and production plan. A lead or manager verifies quality, yield, labeling, and exceptions.
sops.purpose: To record and reduce waste connected to prep work, spoilage, overproduction, trimming, mistakes, and unusable product.
steps: Identify the waste issue.
Stop and confirm whether manager review is required before discarding.
Record the product name.
Record the amount wasted if required.
Record the reason for waste.
Record the employee or station if applicable.
Discard product according to policy.
Clean and sanitize area if needed.
Notify manager of repeated waste, large waste, or unusual waste.
Review waste patterns during manager follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

• Allowing contamination, allergen contact, temperature loss, or unapproved substitutions.
• Producing or restocking without checking on-hand product, shelf life, par, and expected demand.
• Failing to label, date, cool, store, and record the completed product.

sops.title: Cook Line Opening SOP
sops.frequency: During line setup, active cooking, ticket execution, holding, restocking, cleaning, or closing as applicable.
sops.role: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To open the cook line with clean and safe equipment, correctly held product, calibrated tools, stocked stations, clear assignments, and manager release.
steps: Review the opening checklist, manager notes, menu changes, outages, reservations, expected volume, and staffing plan.
Inspect the line for cleanliness, pests, leaks, damage, grease, blocked exits, and unresolved closing issues.
Verify ventilation, fire-suppression status, gas/electrical condition, refrigeration, hot equipment, lighting, and hand sinks.
Confirm each station has approved recipes, utensils, thermometers, timers, labels, towels, sanitizer, and PPE.
Check product identity, date marks, quality, storage order, thaw status, pars, and allergy-order supplies.
Preheat or start equipment only according to manufacturer instructions and the approved startup sequence.
Verify required holding and equipment temperatures before loading food or beginning production.
Assign stations, backups, communication calls, allergy-order leadership, restocking, and break coverage.
Correct shortages or hazards and document equipment, product, or staffing limits before service.
Complete a manager line walk and authorize the cook line to open only when critical standards are met. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.purpose: To set up each cook-line station according to the menu, recipe, equipment, product, sanitation, safety, and expected-volume requirements.
steps: Review the station assignment, menu, recipes, projected volume, specials, and known product or equipment limits.
Clean and sanitize the work area, food-contact surfaces, handles, utensils, and required smallwares.
Inspect assigned equipment, guards, cords, gas connections, controls, refrigeration, and ventilation before use.
Gather only approved ingredients and verify labels, dates, quality, thaw status, and storage hierarchy.
Stock the station to the approved opening par without blocking airflow, access, handwashing, or safe movement.
Arrange ingredients, tools, pans, towels, sanitizer, thermometers, timers, and waste containers in the approved layout.
Preheat equipment and verify operating or holding temperatures before placing food into service.
Separate raw, ready-to-eat, and allergen-sensitive work and establish the approved clean-tool process.
Test communication with expo and identify backups, substitutions, and restocking responsibility.
Ask the lead or manager to verify the station setup before accepting the first ticket. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Cooking Temperature Verification SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To verify cooking temperatures at the correct product location with a clean, calibrated thermometer and take immediate corrective action when limits are missed.
steps: Notify the manager or designated food-safety leader before proceeding with an uncertain high-risk condition.
Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
Isolate affected food and prevent sale, use, movement, or disposal until authorized.
Use a sanitized calibrated thermometer in the thickest or slowest-heating portion.
Check each required product or batch without relying on color, time, or appearance alone.
Compare the result to the current approved cooking requirement and record when required.
Continue cooking, hold for manager evaluation, or discard product that does not meet the standard.
Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
Record all measurements, time, product, quantity, disposition, decision, and responsible people.
Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the station, ticket or recipe standard, safety limit, quality result, and escalation point for cooking temperature verification.
□ Identify the product, lot, time, temperature, exposure, and applicable approved limit.
□ Use a sanitized calibrated thermometer in the thickest or slowest-heating portion.
□ Compare the result to the current approved cooking requirement and record when required.
□ Management determines approved correction, discard, closure, or authority notification.
□ Verify the affected process is safe before resuming production or service.
sops.correction:
• Checking cooking temperature verification with an unclean, uncalibrated, or inappropriate thermometer.
• Measuring only the equipment display, container surface, or an unrepresentative location.
• Delaying the reading or recording a rounded, estimated, or backfilled result.
• Keeping product in service when the required limit or time history is uncertain.
• Failing to document corrective action, product disposition, and manager verification.

sops.title: Portion Control on the Line SOP
sops.frequency: During line setup, active cooking, ticket execution, holding, restocking, cleaning, or closing as applicable.
sops.role: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To maintain approved portions on the cook line using specified tools, weights, counts, recipes, and manager-verified corrections.
steps: Review the recipe card, approved portion, yield, plate standard, modifier, and ticket before plating.
Use only the assigned scoop, ladle, scale, count, slice, cup, or measuring tool for the item.
Verify the tool is clean, intact, and matched to the correct product and portion size.
Portion from a mixed or evenly distributed batch so the serving represents the recipe.
Level, drain, weigh, count, or finish the portion according to the standard rather than estimating.
Keep raw, ready-to-eat, and allergen-sensitive tools and containers separated.
Compare the plated portion with the recipe photo, weight, count, side, garnish, and container standard.
Correct over- or under-portioning before the plate leaves the station and record repeated variance.
Restock portion tools and product without combining batches or losing label and date control.
Verify high-cost and high-variance items during manager line checks and coaching. & CUSTOMIZATION

• Clean utensils, portion tools, and equipment
• Calibrated thermometer and timers
• Allergy and special-request communication tools
• Expo and manager communication
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Tickets, recipes, modifiers, portions, temperatures, and plate standards are followed exactly.
• Allergy and special-request orders receive direct communication and controlled handling.
• Unsafe, undercooked, overcooked, contaminated, or poor-quality food is not served.
• Delays, shortages, equipment problems, and remakes are communicated immediately.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Read the entire special request and identify exactly what is added, removed, substituted, cooked differently, or separated.
2. Confirm the request is available, safe, and within restaurant authority before promising it to the guest.
3. Clarify unclear wording through expo or the server and distinguish preference from allergy or medical concern.
4. Mark the ticket and communicate the request directly to every affected station.
5. Verify ingredients, recipe changes, portion, price, cook time, and equipment limitations.
6. Use clean tools and controlled handling when the request changes cross-contact or food-safety risk.
7. Call out the order at firing and at completion so it does not merge with the standard item.
8. Expo verifies the modification, plate, side, garnish, and seat/table before release.
9. Stop and remake the item when the request was missed or cannot be verified.
10. Record repeated unavailable requests, pricing issues, menu confusion, and training needs. CUSTOMIZATION
sourceSections.managerVerification:
□ The employee can identify the station, ticket or recipe standard, safety limit, quality result, and escalation point for special request order.
□ Confirm the request is available, safe, and within restaurant authority before promising it to the guest.
□ Mark the ticket and communicate the request directly to every affected station.
□ Use clean tools and controlled handling when the request changes cross-contact or food-safety risk.
□ Expo verifies the modification, plate, side, garnish, and seat/table before release.
□ Record repeated unavailable requests, pricing issues, menu confusion, and training needs.
sourceSections.commonMistakes:
• Beginning special request order without direct confirmation of the request, recipe, ingredients, and designated leader.
• Allowing shared tools, surfaces, gloves, towels, fryers, or garnishes to compromise the order.
• Guessing about an ingredient or removing visible pieces instead of remaking.
• Losing the order's identity or direct handoff during a rush.
• Serving before designated verification of ingredients, preparation, plate, and destination.

sops.role: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To make sure kitchen employees communicate clearly during busy periods.
steps: Call back important ticket information according to kitchen standard.
Communicate low product before running out.
Communicate delays early.

Tell expo or manager when ticket times are at risk.

Communicate equipment problems immediately.

sops.title: Expo Communication SOP
sops.frequency: During line setup, active cooking, ticket execution, holding, restocking, cleaning, or closing as applicable.
sops.role: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To keep expo and cook-line employees aligned on ticket sequence, missing items, timing, allergens, remakes, quality, and table completion.
steps: Establish the approved expo call language, ticket queue, station names, and response expectations before service.
Read each ticket for table, server, course, seat, modifiers, allergy markers, and special requests.
Call or display the order once through the approved system and require clear station acknowledgement.
Track fired, working, delayed, completed, remade, and held items without creating duplicate calls.
Communicate changes immediately, including added items, cancellations, shortages, and revised timing.
Escalate allergy orders, severe delays, equipment failure, product shortages, and cross-station conflicts.
Coordinate course completion so hot and cold items reach the pass together at the correct quality.
Keep the pass organized by ticket and prevent employees from removing unverified plates.
Give the runner a complete handoff with table, seat, allergy, missing item, and timing information.
Record recurring communication failures and review them with the kitchen and floor managers. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Cook Line Restocking SOP
sops.frequency: Before service, during service, before rush periods, after rush periods, during low product alerts, and before shift handoff.
sops.role: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To make sure cook line stations stay stocked with the right amount of product during service without over-pulling or creating waste.
steps: Check current product level at the station.
Compare product level to expected volume and par standard.
Communicate low product before running out.
Pull backup product only as needed.
Check label, date, and quality before using product.
Follow FIFO when selecting product.
Keep product at safe temperature during restocking.
Place product in correct station location.
Do not overfill pans or containers beyond restaurant standard.
Label newly prepared or transferred product when required and return safe unused backups to the correct storage location. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Hot Holding SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To control hot holding consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Verify the product was fully cooked or reheated using the approved process before it enters hot holding.
Preheat the holding unit and confirm it is clean, operating, and capable of maintaining the required limit.
Transfer food in clean covered containers using shallow batches, correct utensils, and protected handling.
Label the product with identity, start time, discard or review time, and any batch or allergen information.
Place containers to allow heat circulation; do not overload, combine old and new batches, or use holding to finish cooking.
Measure food temperature at the required frequency with a clean, calibrated thermometer.
Stir, rotate, cover, or adjust the unit only according to the recipe, equipment instructions, and approved corrective action.
Hold, rapidly reheat, discard, or escalate any product outside the approved limit based on documented time and temperature.
Record temperatures, times, employee initials, corrective actions, and manager verification.
Discard or properly cool remaining food at the approved end point; clean and reset the holding unit. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the station, ticket or recipe standard, safety limit, quality result, and escalation point for hot holding.
□ Preheat the holding unit and confirm it is clean, operating, and capable of maintaining the required limit.
□ Label the product with identity, start time, discard or review time, and any batch or allergen information.
□ Measure food temperature at the required frequency with a clean, calibrated thermometer.
□ Hold, rapidly reheat, discard, or escalate any product outside the approved limit based on documented time and temperature.
□ Discard or properly cool remaining food at the approved end point; clean and reset the holding unit.
sops.correction:
• Starting hot holding without the station, ticket, recipe, equipment, tools, product, and communication plan ready.
• Losing ticket sequence, modifiers, allergy information, portion, temperature, or plate standards.
• Continuing when equipment, product, staffing, or timing cannot support safe execution.
• Failing to communicate delays, remakes, shortages, and completed items.
• Ending without restocking, cleaning, product disposition, and manager verification.

• Protected containers, labels, PPE, and sanitizer
• Corrective-action and food-disposition record
• Manager and regulatory contact information

sops.role: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sops.purpose: To control cold holding consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Verify the product was cooled, received, or prepared within the approved process before it enters cold holding.
Confirm the cold unit is clean, organized, and operating within the restaurant's approved limit.
Use clean covered containers, labels, date marks, and storage placement that prevent contamination and allergen cross- contact.
Keep product in refrigeration until needed and return working containers promptly between uses.
Do not overfill pans, block airflow, place hot food into overloaded units, or store product above raw-item hierarchy limits.
Measure food temperature at the required frequency with a clean, calibrated thermometer.
Use ice, smaller pans, alternate refrigeration, or another approved control only when the process is authorized and monitored.
Hold, rapidly cool, transfer, discard, or escalate any product outside the approved limit based on documented history.
Record temperatures, times, employee initials, corrective actions, and manager verification.
At closing, evaluate remaining product, protect labels and dates, and clean the unit and surrounding area. CUSTOMIZATION

sourceSections.purpose: To control cold holding consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
sourceSections.appliesTo: Trained food employees, kitchen leads, managers, and designated food-safety leaders.
sourceSections.responsibility: The employee follows the approved high-risk control. Management verifies limits, disposition, records, and required regulatory contact.
sourceSections.whenUsed: Whenever the named high-risk process is performed or a required limit, control, or record is uncertain or missed.
sourceSections.materials:
• Current regulatory and restaurant standard
• Calibrated thermometer, timer, or approved test device
• Protected containers, labels, PPE, and sanitizer
• Corrective-action and food-disposition record
• Manager and regulatory contact information
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• The current approved regulatory and restaurant limit controls the process.
• Questionable food is isolated and not served until management determines disposition.
• Corrective action and disposition are recorded at the time of the event.
• Management contacts the proper authority when required by law, permit, policy, or incident severity.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Verify the product was cooled, received, or prepared within the approved process before it enters cold holding.
2. Confirm the cold unit is clean, organized, and operating within the restaurant's approved limit.
3. Use clean covered containers, labels, date marks, and storage placement that prevent contamination and allergen cross- contact.
4. Keep product in refrigeration until needed and return working containers promptly between uses.
5. Do not overfill pans, block airflow, place hot food into overloaded units, or store product above raw-item hierarchy limits.
6. Measure food temperature at the required frequency with a clean, calibrated thermometer.
7. Use ice, smaller pans, alternate refrigeration, or another approved control only when the process is authorized and monitored.
8. Hold, rapidly cool, transfer, discard, or escalate any product outside the approved limit based on documented history.
9. Record temperatures, times, employee initials, corrective actions, and manager verification.
10. At closing, evaluate remaining product, protect labels and dates, and clean the unit and surrounding area. CUSTOMIZATION

• Failing to communicate delays, remakes, shortages, and completed items.
• Ending without restocking, cleaning, product disposition, and manager verification.

sops.title: Fryer Operation SOP
sops.frequency: During line setup, active cooking, ticket execution, holding, restocking, cleaning, or closing as applicable.
sops.role: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sops.purpose: To operate the fryer station safely and consistently according to equipment instructions, recipes, temperatures, ticket priorities, and cleaning controls.
steps: Review fryer assignments, oil type, product compatibility, cook settings, filtration status, and known maintenance issues.
Inspect the fryer, baskets, handles, guards, thermostat, drain valve, oil level, floor, and fire-suppression area.
Confirm the unit is dry and free of water, ice buildup, packaging, loose debris, and nearby trip hazards.
Heat oil only through the approved startup sequence and verify operating temperature before cooking.
Load dry product within basket capacity and lower it slowly to prevent boil-over and splash.
Use the approved timer and temperature and keep allergen or product-separation rules active.
Skim crumbs, monitor oil quality and level, and stop for smoke, foaming, leak, control failure, or abnormal odor.
Lift and drain baskets safely and transfer food to the approved holding or plating area.
Record waste, oil addition, filter need, temperature failure, spill, burn, or equipment concern.
Follow the approved idle, filtration, shutdown, and cleaning process at the end of use. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.purpose: To operate the grill station safely and consistently according to equipment instructions, recipes, temperatures, ticket priorities, and cleaning controls.
steps: Review grill assignments, recipes, doneness standards, zone layout, volume, and known equipment conditions.
Inspect grates, burners, ignition, flame, guards, grease tray, tools, ventilation, and surrounding floor.
Preheat the grill and establish approved heat zones before loading food.
Use separate clean tools and designated areas for raw, cooked, ready-to-eat, and allergen-sensitive items.
Place product according to zone and ticket sequence without overcrowding or creating unsafe flare-ups.
Turn, move, and finish product using recipe timing and a calibrated thermometer when required.
Prevent cross-contact by controlling brushes, towels, seasonings, pans, and shared surfaces.
Stop and report gas odor, failed ignition, uneven flame, excessive smoke, grease fire, or damaged grates.
Verify doneness, rest time, portion, quality, and correct ticket before transfer.
Scrape and reset the grill between products as required and complete approved shutdown and cleaning. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.purpose: To operate the saute station safely and consistently according to equipment instructions, recipes, temperatures, ticket priorities, and cleaning controls.
steps: Review saute assignments, recipes, pan sizes, burner zones, ingredients, sauces, garnishes, and expected volume.
Inspect burners, ignition, pan handles, utensils, hood operation, refrigeration, and surrounding work area.
Stage measured ingredients in the approved sequence while protecting cold holding and allergen separation.
Select the correct clean pan and preheat only to the recipe requirement; never leave an empty pan unattended.
Add oil, ingredients, and liquids carefully to control flame, steam, splash, and boil-over.
Cook in ticket order using approved timing, agitation, reduction, and temperature checks.
Use dedicated or freshly sanitized tools and pans for allergy orders and verified special requests.
Stop for flare-up, gas odor, failed burner, damaged handle, excessive smoke, or uncontrolled spill.
Verify sauce consistency, doneness, portion, garnish, and ticket before plating.
Remove pans safely, control hot handles, clean the station continuously, and complete shutdown and handoff. CUSTOMIZATION

Clean spills and trays as safe, record issues, and complete the approved shutdown and cleaning sequence. CUSTOMIZATION

sourceSections.purpose: To close cook line through a verified sequence that protects food, equipment, chemicals, records, and next-shift readiness.
sourceSections.appliesTo: Line cooks, expo employees, kitchen leads, trainers, and managers.
sourceSections.responsibility: The cook executes the ticket and recipe. Expo or management verifies timing, quality, safety, and corrections.
sourceSections.whenUsed: During line setup, active cooking, ticket execution, holding, restocking, cleaning, or closing as applicable.
sourceSections.materials:
• Current tickets, recipes, and station assignment
• Clean utensils, portion tools, and equipment
• Calibrated thermometer and timers
• Allergy and special-request communication tools
• Expo and manager communication
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Tickets, recipes, modifiers, portions, temperatures, and plate standards are followed exactly.
• Allergy and special-request orders receive direct communication and controlled handling.
• Unsafe, undercooked, overcooked, contaminated, or poor-quality food is not served.
• Delays, shortages, equipment problems, and remakes are communicated immediately.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Review the station assignment, tickets, recipes, portions, allergens, shortages, and expected volume.
2. Wash hands and prepare clean tools, thermometers, timers, sanitation controls, and safe equipment.
3. Inspect and organize dated product by safe storage, cook sequence, and service priority.
4. Stop production only after active tickets and transfer needs are confirmed.
5. Cool, label, rotate, store, or discard product and account for waste.
6. Shut down and clean equipment according to manufacturer and restaurant instructions.
7. Complete station cleaning, restocking, maintenance notes, and manager sign-off.
8. Verify the complete item or station result against the ticket and quality standard.
9. Communicate and document remakes, delays, waste, shortages, equipment, and allergy exceptions.
10. Reset tools, product, sanitation, and station readiness for the next ticket or shift. CUSTOMIZATION
sourceSections.managerVerification:
□ The employee can identify the station, ticket or recipe standard, safety limit, quality result, and escalation point for cook line closing.
□ Wash hands and prepare clean tools, thermometers, timers, sanitation controls, and safe equipment.
□ Stop production only after active tickets and transfer needs are confirmed.
□ Shut down and clean equipment according to manufacturer and restaurant instructions.
□ Verify the complete item or station result against the ticket and quality standard.
□ Reset tools, product, sanitation, and station readiness for the next ticket or shift.
sourceSections.commonMistakes:
• Starting cook line closing without the station, ticket, recipe, equipment, tools, product, and communication plan ready.
• Losing ticket sequence, modifiers, allergy information, portion, temperature, or plate standards.
• Continuing when equipment, product, staffing, or timing cannot support safe execution.
• Failing to communicate delays, remakes, shortages, and completed items.
• Ending without restocking, cleaning, product disposition, and manager verification.

sops.title: Handwashing SOP
sops.frequency: Before food work, whenever contamination may occur, and whenever an employee health or hygiene concern is reported.
sops.role: Each employee follows the personal-health and hygiene standard. Management removes unsafe work and follows required reporting or exclusion procedures.
sops.purpose: To control handwashing consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Stop food handling when the hygiene or health requirement cannot be met.
Review the current employee-health or hygiene standard and notify management when required.
Prepare approved handwashing, glove, utensil, clothing, or reporting controls.
Wet hands and exposed forearms with approved running water.
Apply soap and scrub all surfaces, including fingertips, thumbs, nails, and between fingers, for the approved time.
Rinse thoroughly and dry with a single-use towel or approved dryer.
Use the towel to avoid recontaminating hands when required and repeat whenever contamination occurs.
Discard contaminated barriers or food and clean and sanitize affected surfaces as required.
Report the condition and follow manager direction on restriction, retraining, or corrective action.
Document only required facts and protect employee privacy. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can state the approved food-safety limit, monitoring method, corrective action, documentation, and person-in-charge role for handwashing.
□ Review the current employee-health or hygiene standard and notify management when required.
□ Wet hands and exposed forearms with approved running water.
□ Rinse thoroughly and dry with a single-use towel or approved dryer.
□ Discard contaminated barriers or food and clean and sanitize affected surfaces as required.
□ Document only required facts and protect employee privacy.
sops.correction:
• Treating handwashing as optional during busy periods or after contamination events.
• Using gloves as a substitute for handwashing or touching unclean surfaces and returning to food.
• Allowing an ill employee to work or return without required manager evaluation and clearance.
• Handling ready-to-eat food with unapproved bare-hand contact.
• Failing to document reporting, exclusion/restriction, corrective action, and retraining.
sops.records:
• Current employee-health and hygiene policy
• Hand sink, soap, warm water, and single-use towels
• Approved gloves or utensils when required
• Manager reporting and exclusion information
• Training and corrective-action record

sops.title: Glove Use SOP
sops.frequency: When handling ready-to-eat food if required by policy
sops.role: Each employee follows the personal-health and hygiene standard. Management removes unsafe work and follows required reporting or exclusion procedures.
sops.purpose: To make sure gloves are used correctly when handling food or performing tasks that require gloves.
steps: Wash hands before putting on gloves.
Dry hands properly.
Select the correct glove size if available.
Put gloves on without contaminating the glove surface.
Use gloves only for the assigned task.
Change gloves when switching tasks.
Change gloves after touching raw food, trash, face, hair, phone, clothing, chemicals, money, or contaminated surfaces.
Change gloves if torn, dirty, or damaged.
Remove gloves properly.
Throw gloves away after use. Wash hands before putting on new gloves. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Bare-Hand Contact Prevention SOP
sops.frequency: Before food work, whenever contamination may occur, and whenever an employee health or hygiene concern is reported.
sops.role: Each employee follows the personal-health and hygiene standard. Management removes unsafe work and follows required reporting or exclusion procedures.
sops.purpose: To prevent bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food by using approved utensils, gloves, deli tissue, and immediate corrective action.
steps: Stop food handling when the hygiene or health requirement cannot be met.
Review the current employee-health or hygiene standard and notify management when required.
Prepare approved handwashing, glove, utensil, clothing, or reporting controls.
Identify ready-to-eat food and use approved gloves, deli tissue, tongs, spatulas, or other utensils.
Keep utensil handles and dispensing points from contacting food or contaminated surfaces.
Change the barrier whenever it is contaminated, damaged, or used for another product.
Stop and discard affected food after unapproved bare-hand contact unless management confirms an allowed corrective action.
Discard contaminated barriers or food and clean and sanitize affected surfaces as required.
Report the condition and follow manager direction on restriction, retraining, or corrective action.
Document only required facts and protect employee privacy. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Discard contaminated barriers or food and clean and sanitize affected surfaces as required.
□ Document only required facts and protect employee privacy.

sops.title: Sanitizer Bucket SOP
sops.frequency: At each required monitoring point and whenever a limit, complaint, contamination concern, or inspection issue occurs.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To control sanitizer bucket consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Identify the product, employee, location, required limit, and monitoring frequency.
Use a clean calibrated thermometer, timer, test strip, or other approved device.
Protect or isolate food and work when the condition, history, or control is uncertain.
Prepare sanitizer only in a clean labeled container using the approved chemical and dilution system.
Test concentration with the correct test strip and record or correct the result.
Store wiping cloths fully submerged and keep the bucket away from food and guest access.
Replace solution when dirty, weak, strong, contaminated, or at the required interval.
Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
Clean and sanitize tools and affected surfaces and prevent recurrence.
Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up.

• Failing to verify product disposition, sanitation, equipment condition, and manager review.

sops.frequency: At each required monitoring point and whenever a limit, complaint, contamination concern, or inspection issue occurs.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To control food temperature check consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Identify the product, employee, location, required limit, and monitoring frequency.
Use a clean calibrated thermometer, timer, test strip, or other approved device.
Protect or isolate food and work when the condition, history, or control is uncertain.
Sanitize the calibrated probe and select the correct measurement location.
Measure the thickest, coldest, hottest, or most representative portion as required.
Wait for a stable reading and record product, time, temperature, employee, and corrective action.
Sanitize the probe and hold, reheat, chill, cook, or discard product under the approved rule.
Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
Clean and sanitize tools and affected surfaces and prevent recurrence.
Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can state the approved food-safety limit, monitoring method, corrective action, documentation, and person-in-charge role for food temperature check.
□ Use a clean calibrated thermometer, timer, test strip, or other approved device.
□ Sanitize the calibrated probe and select the correct measurement location.
□ Wait for a stable reading and record product, time, temperature, employee, and corrective action.
□ Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
□ Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Checking food temperature check with an unclean, uncalibrated, or inappropriate thermometer.
• Measuring only the equipment display, container surface, or an unrepresentative location.
• Delaying the reading or recording a rounded, estimated, or backfilled result.
• Keeping product in service when the required limit or time history is uncertain.
• Failing to document corrective action, product disposition, and manager verification.

• Current food-safety standard and monitoring log
• Calibrated thermometer or approved test device
• Sanitizer, test strips, and cleaning supplies
• Labels, timers, discard controls, and PPE
• Manager and regulatory contact information

sops.title: Thermometer Calibration SOP
sops.frequency: At each required monitoring point and whenever a limit, complaint, contamination concern, or inspection issue occurs.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To control thermometer calibration consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Identify the product, employee, location, required limit, and monitoring frequency.
Use a clean calibrated thermometer, timer, test strip, or other approved device.
Protect or isolate food and work when the condition, history, or control is uncertain.
Use the approved ice-point, boiling-point, or manufacturer calibration method.
Prepare the test medium correctly and keep the sensing area from touching the container.
Compare the stable reading to the expected reference and adjust when the device permits.
Tag and replace a thermometer that cannot be calibrated, then record the check.
Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
Clean and sanitize tools and affected surfaces and prevent recurrence.
Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Compare the stable reading to the expected reference and adjust when the device permits.
□ Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
□ Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Performing thermometer calibration without the current approved limit, clean tools, test method, timer, and record.
• Guessing temperature, concentration, contact time, or elapsed time instead of measuring.
• Continuing with an out-of-limit result without approved corrective action.
• Backfilling, altering, or omitting monitoring records.
• Failing to verify product disposition, sanitation, equipment condition, and manager review.

sops.title: Cooling Food SOP
sops.frequency: Any time cooked or heated food is cooled for later storage or use.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To make sure food is cooled safely according to restaurant policy and food safety requirements.
steps: Identify food that requires cooling.
Use the approved cooling method.
Portion food into shallow containers if required.
Use ice bath, stirring, venting, or other approved method as required.
Check starting temperature if required.
Record time and temperature if required.
Monitor cooling progress.
Recheck temperature according to policy.
Label and date food when ready for storage.
Store food properly after cooling standard is met. Notify manager if food does not cool properly. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can state the approved food-safety limit, monitoring method, corrective action, documentation, and person-in-charge role for cooling food.

□ Record time and temperature if required.
□ Recheck temperature according to policy.
□ Store food properly after cooling standard is met. Notify manager if food does not cool properly.
sops.correction:
• Beginning cooling food without the approved time-temperature method, container depth, label, and storage space.
• Using room temperature, deep covered containers, standing water, or another unapproved method.
• Combining warm and cold product or overloading refrigeration and airflow.
• Failing to monitor and record required times and temperatures.
• Keeping product when the control history or limit is uncertain instead of escalating.

• Labels

sops.title: Reheating Food SOP
sops.frequency: Any time previously cooked or cooled food is reheated for hot holding or service.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To make sure food is reheated safely and correctly before service.
steps: Confirm the food is labeled, dated, and safe to reheat.
Use approved reheating equipment.
Reheat food according to restaurant standard.
Stir or rotate product if required for even heating.
Check internal temperature with clean thermometer.
Record temperature if required.
Continue reheating if temperature standard is not met.
Do not serve until standard is reached.
Move food to hot holding or service area only after approved temperature is reached.
Notify manager of any safety, quality, or temperature concern. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Do not serve until standard is reached.

• Keeping food in service when identity, time, temperature, contamination, or control history is uncertain.
• Failing to stop work, isolate product, notify the person in charge, and complete required correction.
• Closing the record without product disposition, sanitation, documentation, and follow-up.

sops.title: Hot Holding Monitoring SOP
sops.frequency: At each required monitoring point and whenever a limit, complaint, contamination concern, or inspection issue occurs.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To control hot holding monitoring consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Identify every hot-held product, container, station, start time, required limit, and monitoring frequency.
Confirm the thermometer is clean, calibrated, and appropriate for the product and container depth.
Measure the product in a representative location without contacting the pan or contaminating the food.
Record the actual temperature, time, employee initials, and product identity immediately.
Check unit setting, water level, lids, batch depth, stirring, and product turnover when a reading trends downward.
Recheck after any adjustment within the approved corrective-action window.
Rapidly reheat, transfer, discard, or hold for manager evaluation according to approved time-temperature history.
Do not average readings, backfill logs, or change a recorded result after the fact.
Notify the manager about repeated loss of control, equipment weakness, or uncertain product history.
Verify the final disposition and retain the completed monitoring record. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Allergen Communication SOP
sops.frequency: Any time a guest mentions an allergy, food sensitivity, ingredient concern, or cross-contact concern.
sops.role: The receiving employee communicates the allergy exactly. The designated leader controls preparation, verification, and delivery.
sops.purpose: To make sure allergy concerns are communicated clearly between guests, servers, kitchen, bar, and management.
steps: Listen carefully when a guest mentions an allergy.
Confirm the allergy concern clearly.
Thank the guest for telling the restaurant.
Do not guess about ingredients or safety.
Notify a manager according to policy.
Enter allergy information clearly in the POS or written order.
Communicate allergy concern directly to kitchen or expo according to policy.
Kitchen confirms whether the item can be prepared according to policy.
Use required cross-contact prevention steps.
Verify the item before it leaves the kitchen. Deliver the item only after verification. Document allergy concern if required. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can state the approved food-safety limit, monitoring method, corrective action, documentation, and person-in-charge role for allergen communication.
□ Confirm the allergy concern clearly.
□ Do not guess about ingredients or safety.
□ Enter allergy information clearly in the POS or written order.
□ Kitchen confirms whether the item can be prepared according to policy.
□ Verify the item before it leaves the kitchen. Deliver the item only after verification. Document allergy concern if required.
sops.correction:
• Starting allergen communication without exact allergen information, current labels, and direct manager or kitchen confirmation.
• Assuming a menu item or substitute is safe without checking all ingredients and shared equipment.
• Allowing shared tools, gloves, towels, surfaces, fryers, or garnishes to contact the order.
• Removing visible ingredients instead of remaking after possible cross-contact.
• Serving without designated verification and direct handoff.
sops.records:
• POS allergy notes
• Manager communication
• Recipe / ingredient information
• Kitchen ticket system
• Allergy verification form if used

sops.title: Allergen Order Preparation SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest reports an allergy or an order, ingredient, surface, utensil, or handoff may involve allergen risk.
sops.role: The receiving employee communicates the allergy exactly. The designated leader controls preparation, verification, and delivery.
sops.purpose: To control allergen order preparation consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Stop and obtain the exact guest-reported allergen and the designated manager or allergy-order leader.
Review the current recipe, ingredient labels, manufacturer information, and restaurant capability.
Wash hands and establish a protected cleaned and sanitized work area with separate tools and ingredients.
Assign a designated leader and review the allergy ticket, recipe, ingredients, and station capability.
Wash hands and prepare clean and sanitized tools, surfaces, gloves, and protected ingredients.
Control shared equipment, fryers, grills, steam, garnishes, storage, and handoffs according to policy.
The designated leader verifies the complete plate and delivers or hands off directly.
The designated leader verifies ingredients, preparation, plate, markings, and direct handoff.
Stop and remake whenever cross-contact or ingredient identity is uncertain.
Document exceptions and update the guest only through the approved manager communication. & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Cross-Contact Prevention SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest reports an allergy or an order, ingredient, surface, utensil, or handoff may involve allergen risk.
sops.role: The receiving employee communicates the allergy exactly. The designated leader controls preparation, verification, and delivery.
sops.purpose: To control cross-contact prevention consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Stop and obtain the exact guest-reported allergen and the designated manager or allergy-order leader.
Review the current recipe, ingredient labels, manufacturer information, and restaurant capability.
Wash hands and establish a protected cleaned and sanitized work area with separate tools and ingredients.
Identify the allergen and every possible shared ingredient, tool, surface, glove, towel, container, and piece of equipment.
Schedule or locate the work to prevent contact and clean and sanitize before preparation.
Use protected ingredients and dedicated or freshly sanitized tools and containers.
Stop and remake the order whenever cross-contact may have occurred; do not remove visible pieces and serve it.
The designated leader verifies ingredients, preparation, plate, markings, and direct handoff.
Stop and remake whenever cross-contact or ingredient identity is uncertain.
Document exceptions and update the guest only through the approved manager communication. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Foodborne Illness Complaint SOP
sops.frequency: Any time a guest claims they became sick from restaurant food or reports illness symptoms connected to a visit.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To receive and document a possible foodborne-illness complaint accurately, protect relevant food and records, complete required notifications, and assign authorized follow-up.
steps: Listen calmly and record the guest's report without arguing, diagnosing, admitting fault, or assigning blame.
Obtain the guest's name and contact information if voluntarily provided, plus visit date, time, party size, and check details.
Record each food or beverage consumed, symptoms reported, symptom onset, other affected people, and any medical or authority contact.
Notify the person in charge and ownership or designated food-safety leader immediately.
Preserve relevant guest checks, recipes, ingredient labels, lot information, delivery records, temperature logs, and employee schedules.
Hold related food only under authorized direction; do not discard, sample, relabel, or move evidence unnecessarily.
Review required health-department, insurer, legal, or company notifications and complete them through authorized management.
Protect private medical and employee information and keep witness statements separate and objective.
Complete immediate corrective actions for any verified food-safety control failure without concealing the original condition.
Assign guest follow-up, regulatory follow-up, product disposition, SOP review, and record retention. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Notify the person in charge and ownership or designated food-safety leader immediately.
□ Hold related food only under authorized direction; do not discard, sample, relabel, or move evidence unnecessarily.
□ Protect private medical and employee information and keep witness statements separate and objective.
□ Assign guest follow-up, regulatory follow-up, product disposition, SOP review, and record retention.

• Arguing, diagnosing, admitting fault, or promising a result before authorized review.
• Failing to collect visit, food, symptom, timing, party, and contact information.
• Discarding or altering food, labels, logs, checks, video, or other relevant records.
• Sharing private medical or employee information with uninvolved people.
• Closing the complaint without required notification, corrective action, and assigned follow-up.

sops.title: Contaminated Food Disposal SOP
sops.frequency: At each required monitoring point and whenever a limit, complaint, contamination concern, or inspection issue occurs.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To control contaminated food disposal consistently so food remains safe, required limits are verified, and exceptions receive immediate corrective action.
steps: Identify the product, employee, location, required limit, and monitoring frequency.
Use a clean calibrated thermometer, timer, test strip, or other approved device.
Protect or isolate food and work when the condition, history, or control is uncertain.
Stop use and isolate the exact food, container, lot, station, and related product.
Mark it clearly so it cannot be returned to service or mixed with usable food.
Determine disposition through approved food-safety and management authority; never donate or repurpose unsafe food.
Record identity, quantity, reason, method, witness or approval, and corrective action.
Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
Clean and sanitize tools and affected surfaces and prevent recurrence.
Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ The employee can state the approved food-safety limit, monitoring method, corrective action, documentation, and person-in-charge role for contaminated food disposal.
□ Use a clean calibrated thermometer, timer, test strip, or other approved device.
□ Stop use and isolate the exact food, container, lot, station, and related product.
□ Determine disposition through approved food-safety and management authority; never donate or repurpose unsafe food.
□ Complete the approved corrective action and record product, time, result, disposition, and manager.
□ Management reviews trends and assigns retraining, maintenance, vendor, or regulatory follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Beginning contaminated food disposal without the approved food-safety limit, calibrated tool, monitoring frequency, and corrective action.
• Guessing, averaging, backfilling, or altering results.
• Keeping food in service when identity, time, temperature, contamination, or control history is uncertain.
• Failing to stop work, isolate product, notify the person in charge, and complete required correction.
• Closing the record without product disposition, sanitation, documentation, and follow-up.

sops.title: Boil Water Notice SOP
sops.frequency: Any time a boil water notice, advisory, or unsafe water alert affects the restaurant.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To protect food, water-contact systems, employees, and guests during a boil-water notice or advisory and restore operations only after approved clearance and sanitation.
steps: Confirm the official notice, affected area, start time, restrictions, and issuing authority.
Notify ownership, the person in charge, and the local regulatory authority when required.
Stop using affected water for drinking, ice, beverages, food preparation, produce washing, handwashing, warewashing, and sanitation unless an approved alternative exists.
Isolate or discard affected ice, beverages, food, filters, and water-contact product according to authority direction.
Evaluate whether approved bottled, hauled, boiled, or otherwise treated water can support restricted operations.
Provide approved handwashing and restroom controls or close when required hygiene and sanitation cannot be maintained.
Suspend dishwashing, beverage, ice, produce, and food processes that lack an approved safe-water method.
Communicate restrictions to employees, guests, delivery partners, and vendors without making unsupported reopening promises.
After official clearance, flush lines, clean and sanitize equipment, replace filters, discard initial ice, and restore systems as directed.
Document the notice, decisions, product disposition, authority contacts, restoration actions, and manager approval. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can state the approved food-safety limit, monitoring method, corrective action, documentation, and person-in-charge role for boil water notice.
□ Notify ownership, the person in charge, and the local regulatory authority when required.
□ Isolate or discard affected ice, beverages, food, filters, and water-contact product according to authority direction.
□ Provide approved handwashing and restroom controls or close when required hygiene and sanitation cannot be maintained.
□ Communicate restrictions to employees, guests, delivery partners, and vendors without making unsupported reopening promises.
□ Document the notice, decisions, product disposition, authority contacts, restoration actions, and manager approval.
sops.correction:
• Continuing normal ice, beverage, food, handwashing, or warewashing processes during the notice.
• Using an alternate water source or boiling method that has not been approved for the specific use.
• Forgetting affected filters, beverage lines, ice bins, produce, and water-contact equipment.
• Promising reopening before official clearance and restoration steps are complete.
• Failing to document product disposition, authority contacts, flushing, sanitation, and approval.
sops.records:
• Health department guidance
• Company policy
• Emergency contact list
• Approved safe water source if available
• Signage if required
