sourceSections.purpose: To protect food, water-contact systems, employees, and guests during a boil-water notice or advisory and restore operations only after approved clearance and sanitation.
sourceSections.appliesTo: Manager on duty leads the response with ownership or health department guidance.
sourceSections.responsibility: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sourceSections.whenUsed: Any time a boil water notice, advisory, or unsafe water alert affects the restaurant.
sourceSections.materials:
• Health department guidance
• Company policy
• Emergency contact list
• Approved safe water source if available
• Signage if required
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Affected water is not used for food, ice, beverages, handwashing, warewashing, or sanitation unless an approved alternative is in place.
• The restaurant follows the issuing authority and local regulatory authority for restrictions, restoration, flushing, cleaning, and reopening.
• Affected ice, food, beverages, filters, and water-contact equipment are identified and controlled.
• Operations close or remain restricted whenever required hygiene, sanitation, or safe-water controls cannot be maintained.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Confirm the official notice, affected area, start time, restrictions, and issuing authority.
2. Notify ownership, the person in charge, and the local regulatory authority when required.
3. Stop using affected water for drinking, ice, beverages, food preparation, produce washing, handwashing, warewashing, and sanitation unless an approved alternative exists.
4. Isolate or discard affected ice, beverages, food, filters, and water-contact product according to authority direction.
5. Evaluate whether approved bottled, hauled, boiled, or otherwise treated water can support restricted operations.
6. Provide approved handwashing and restroom controls or close when required hygiene and sanitation cannot be maintained.
7. Suspend dishwashing, beverage, ice, produce, and food processes that lack an approved safe-water method.
8. Communicate restrictions to employees, guests, delivery partners, and vendors without making unsupported reopening promises.
9. After official clearance, flush lines, clean and sanitize equipment, replace filters, discard initial ice, and restore systems as directed.
10. Document the notice, decisions, product disposition, authority contacts, restoration actions, and manager approval. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.frequency: At each required monitoring point and whenever a limit, complaint, contamination concern, or inspection issue occurs.
sops.role: Employees complete required controls and records. Management stops unsafe work, evaluates affected food, and completes corrective action.
sops.purpose: To cooperate professionally with a health-department inspection, preserve truthful records, correct immediate hazards, and complete every required follow-up action.
steps: Greet the inspector professionally, verify identification when appropriate, and notify the person in charge without delaying lawful access.
Assign one authorized manager to accompany the inspection and one employee to coordinate immediate corrections.

Obtain and review the written report before the inspector leaves when available.
Notify ownership and required company contacts and determine whether service restriction, closure, or specialized support is necessary.
Complete corrective actions, repairs, retraining, and required written responses by the stated deadline.
Verify sustained compliance through follow-up inspections and retain the report and supporting records. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Dish Pit Opening SOP
sops.frequency: Before service begins, before dish volume starts, or before the dishwasher begins the assigned shift.
sops.role: Dish employees follow the approved sequence. Management verifies chemicals, temperatures, air-drying, storage, and corrective action.
sops.purpose: To make sure the dish area is clean, safe, stocked, and ready before dishes, pans, glassware, and utensils begin arriving.
steps: Arrive at the dish area before dish volume begins.
Check that the dish area is clean and free of old food, trash, broken glass, and clutter.
Check that the dish machine is assembled and ready according to restaurant procedure.
Check chemical levels if required.
Check water temperature or machine readiness according to restaurant policy.
Set up dish racks, glass racks, silverware baskets, and pot/pan areas.
Check the dirty dish drop area.
Check the clean dish landing area.
Make sure clean and dirty areas are clearly separated.
Prepare trash, floors, drains, racks, and clean-storage areas and obtain manager release before the dish pit opens. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Check chemical levels if required.
□ Set up dish racks, glass racks, silverware baskets, and pot/pan areas.

□ Prepare trash, floors, drains, racks, and clean-storage areas and obtain manager release before the dish pit opens.

• Continuing after chemical, temperature, pressure, drainage, machine, or breakage failure.
• Ending without cleaning the area, documenting checks, and manager verification.

sops.title: Dirty Dish Sorting SOP
sops.frequency: During opening, active warewashing, chemical or temperature checks, storage, cleaning, and closing.
sops.role: Dish employees follow the approved sequence. Management verifies chemicals, temperatures, air-drying, storage, and corrective action.
sops.purpose: To sort dirty dishes, utensils, glassware, and cookware by type and hazard while preserving a clear dirty-to-clean warewashing flow.
steps: Establish separate landing zones for plates, glassware, silverware, cups, pans, trash, and sharps.
Receive dirty wares without allowing them to cross into the clean side or block the machine path.
Remove knives and sharp tools immediately into the approved clearly marked container.
Separate broken or chipped items and handle glass through the approved breakage process.
Empty liquids and food waste into the correct containers without splashing or clogging drains.
Stack like items only to the safe approved height and keep heavy wares below fragile items.
Route soak items, pots, glassware, silverware, and machine-ready racks to the correct next step.
Keep chemicals, towels, personal items, and trash out of ware-sorting zones.
Clear backups before they block exits, hand sinks, floor drains, or employee movement.
Clean and reset the sorting area and report recurring breakage, sharps, or flow problems. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Pre-Scraping and Soaking SOP
sops.frequency: During opening, active warewashing, chemical or temperature checks, storage, cleaning, and closing.
sops.role: Dish employees follow the approved sequence. Management verifies chemicals, temperatures, air-drying, storage, and corrective action.
sops.purpose: To remove food debris and soak approved wares safely before washing without creating chemical, sharps, lifting, or cross-contamination hazards.
steps: Move sorted wares to the scraping area while preserving dirty-to-clean separation.
Scrape food into the approved waste container using the designated tool rather than hands or spray pressure.
Empty cups, pans, and hollow items before placing them into soak or racks.
Use only approved soaking solution, container, dilution, and maximum soak time.
Keep knives, blades, glass, aluminum, wood, and chemical-sensitive items out of incompatible soak solutions.
Change soak water when cold, greasy, overloaded, contaminated, or outside the approved chemical range.
Loosen heavy soil without nesting items or creating hidden sharp hazards.
Rinse or transfer items according to the next warewashing step and do not treat soaking as washing or sanitizing.
Clean the scrape table, waste opening, soak sink, tools, floor, and splash zone as buildup occurs.
Report clogged drains, chemical problems, sharp objects, broken glass, or persistent soil. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Three-Compartment Sink Warewashing SOP
sops.frequency: During opening, active warewashing, chemical or temperature checks, storage, cleaning, and closing.
sops.role: Dish employees follow the approved sequence. Management verifies chemicals, temperatures, air-drying, storage, and corrective action.
sops.purpose: To apply and document the approved food-safety limits, measuring tools, monitoring frequency, corrective actions, and manager verification for three-compartment sink warewashing.
steps: Clean and set the wash, rinse, and sanitize compartments in the approved left-to-right or posted sequence.
Fill each compartment to the required level and verify wash temperature and sanitizer concentration.
Scrape and pre-rinse wares before placing them in the wash solution.
Wash each item completely with approved detergent and clean tools, changing water when soiled or ineffective.
Rinse away detergent and loosened soil in clean rinse water.
Fully immerse or expose each item to the approved sanitizer for the required contact time.
Test and record sanitizer concentration at opening, required intervals, and after solution changes.
Place sanitized wares on the clean drainboard or rack and allow complete air-drying.
Never towel-dry, stack wet items, mix dirty and clean wares, or use the sink for food preparation during warewashing.
Drain, clean, sanitize, and reset the sink and record corrective action or manager verification. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Fully immerse or expose each item to the approved sanitizer for the required contact time.
□ Place sanitized wares on the clean drainboard or rack and allow complete air-drying.
□ Drain, clean, sanitize, and reset the sink and record corrective action or manager verification.

• Performing three-compartment sink warewashing without the current approved limit, clean tools, test method, timer, and record.

• Continuing with an out-of-limit result without approved corrective action.
• Backfilling, altering, or omitting monitoring records.
• Failing to verify product disposition, sanitation, equipment condition, and manager review.

sops.title: Dish Machine Chemical Check SOP
sops.frequency: During opening, active warewashing, chemical or temperature checks, storage, cleaning, and closing.
sops.role: Dish employees follow the approved sequence. Management verifies chemicals, temperatures, air-drying, storage, and corrective action.
sops.purpose: To verify dish-machine chemicals, concentration, supply, feed lines, and test results before and during use and stop operation when control is lost.
steps: Review the machine chemical requirements, product labels, SDS, test method, and approved operating range.
Confirm detergent, rinse aid, and sanitizer containers are correct, connected, labeled, upright, and not empty.
Inspect pickup tubes, caps, lines, pumps, alarms, and injection points for leaks, air gaps, kinks, or damage.
Run the approved priming or test cycle according to manufacturer instructions.
Test the final rinse or sanitizer using the approved strip, device, location, and timing.
Record the actual result and do not estimate from smell, color, or machine display alone.
Stop warewashing when chemical delivery or required results are outside the approved limit.
Notify the manager and use the approved three-compartment-sink fallback only when it can be controlled safely.
Replace chemicals or request service only through trained and authorized employees.
Retest, document corrective action, and obtain manager release before returning the machine to service. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:

sops.title: Master Cleaning Schedule SOP

steps: Review the current master cleaning schedule by area, surface, equipment, frequency, method, and responsible position.

Assign daily, weekly, monthly, seasonal, and shutdown tasks around service and food-production risk.
Coordinate tasks that require equipment shutdown, vendor access, ladders, ventilation, or restricted areas.
Check completed work through direct inspection rather than accepting initials alone.
Reassign missed or failed tasks with an owner, deadline, and reinspection time.
Record chemical, equipment, pest, damage, drainage, and access issues discovered during cleaning.
Compare repeated failures with staffing, training, tools, schedule timing, and maintenance needs.
Update the schedule when menus, equipment, layout, regulations, or operating hours change.
Retain completion records and review overdue and recurring items at the manager checkpoint. & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Restroom Deep Cleaning SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled frequency, after contamination or spills, and before the area is released for normal use.
sops.role: The assigned employee cleans and sanitizes safely. Management verifies the area, chemical use, records, and unresolved hazards.
sops.purpose: To complete restroom deep cleaning safely using the approved chemical, concentration, contact time, PPE, area control, food protection, and manager verification.
steps: Close or control the restroom and post approved signs before beginning deep cleaning.
Put on required PPE and remove trash, liners, consumables, personal items, and removable debris.
Apply approved cleaner to toilets, urinals, partitions, sinks, fixtures, dispensers, doors, and high-touch points.
Allow required dwell time and use dedicated color-coded tools that never enter food areas.
Scrub bowls, undersides, grout, corners, vents, walls, bases, and hard-to-reach buildup.
Rinse or remove residue as required and disinfect approved surfaces at the labeled concentration and contact time.
Clean mirrors, stainless surfaces, dispensers, baby-changing equipment, and accessibility fixtures.
Clean and dry floors from the farthest point toward the exit and keep warning signs in place.
Restock supplies and report leaks, damage, pests, odors, lighting, ventilation, or accessibility problems.
Manager-inspect cleanliness, odor, dryness, supplies, and function before reopening. CUSTOMIZATION

steps: Move or protect food in sections so required temperature control is maintained during cleaning.
Remove expired, leaking, spoiled, unlabeled, or manager-held product according to the disposition process.
Clean shelves, racks, walls, doors, gaskets, handles, fan guards, floors, drains, and condensate areas.
Use only approved chemicals and keep them away from exposed food and absorbent packaging.
Work from cleanest/highest areas downward and prevent dirty water from splashing product or containers.
Clean spills beneath containers and remove cardboard, broken packaging, standing water, and blocked airflow.
Rinse or remove residue as required and sanitize food-contact or high-touch surfaces.
Dry surfaces, return food to approved hierarchy, and restore labels, dates, spacing, and airflow.
Verify unit temperature and report leaks, ice, mold, pests, gasket, fan, drain, or door problems.
Record discarded product, corrections, maintenance needs, and manager verification. CUSTOMIZATION

steps: Identify high-touch surfaces, required frequency, approved product, compatible material, and area-control needs.

Use separate cloths or tools by zone and replace contaminated solution or materials promptly.
Include handles, switches, railings, devices, payment surfaces, doors, dispensers, and shared equipment as assigned.

Use approved tools to clean up glass.
Check surrounding area carefully for small pieces.
Dispose of glass according to restaurant policy.

Clean the area after glass is removed.
Report injury immediately if anyone is cut or hurt.
Complete incident documentation if required. CUSTOMIZATION

9. Report injury immediately if anyone is cut or hurt.
10. Complete incident documentation if required. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Bodily Fluid Cleanup SOP
sops.frequency: At the scheduled frequency, after contamination or spills, and before the area is released for normal use.
sops.role: The assigned employee cleans and sanitizes safely. Management verifies the area, chemical use, records, and unresolved hazards.
sops.purpose: To complete bodily fluid cleanup safely using the approved chemical, concentration, contact time, PPE, area control, food protection, and manager verification.
steps: Review the current schedule, area standard, chemical label, SDS, PPE, and required contact time.
Place signs or barriers and protect guests, food, clean utensils, equipment, and unaffected areas.
Remove loose soil and waste using tools assigned to the correct sanitation zone.
Block access and put on approved PPE before approaching bodily fluids.
Use the designated kit and follow the approved cleanup and disinfectant contact-time procedure.
Bag contaminated materials and dispose of them according to policy without compressing or sorting.
Remove PPE safely, wash hands, secure the kit, and document exposure or follow-up.
Inspect for soil, residue, moisture, odor, damage, pests, and missed high-touch points.
Remove tools, waste, PPE, signs, and barriers only when the area is safe and dry.
Complete the schedule or issue log and obtain manager verification. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Chemical Safety SOP
sops.frequency: Whenever a chemical is handled, stored, spilled, misused, released, or associated with possible exposure.
sops.role: Employees isolate the area and avoid unapproved cleanup. Management directs response using the label, SDS, PPE, and required reporting.
sops.purpose: To store, label, dilute, use, and dispose of chemicals safely according to the product label, SDS, PPE, food-protection, and access requirements.
steps: Keep people away and notify management before approaching the release or exposure.
Identify the product from the label or records without touching or smelling unknown material.
Review the SDS and emergency instructions and obtain only the required PPE and spill materials.
Restrict access and identify the chemical, label, hazard, quantity, and exposure from a safe position.
Notify management and use the SDS and emergency instructions to select PPE and response limits.
Contain and clean only within training; protect food, drains, ventilation, and occupied areas.
Dispose of material properly and document exposure, cleanup, notification, and follow-up.
Arrange approved disposal, ventilation, decontamination, medical evaluation, or outside response.
Restock and secure chemicals and keep the area closed until management confirms it is safe.
Document product, quantity, exposure, response, contacts, disposal, and corrective action. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Document product, quantity, exposure, response, contacts, disposal, and corrective action.

• Cleaning beyond training instead of evacuating and contacting emergency or hazardous-material support.

sops.title: Equipment Opening Inspection SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To inspect equipment before opening for cleanliness, guards, utilities, damage, operating condition, food-safety impact, and required service restrictions.
steps: Review the equipment opening checklist, overnight notes, maintenance holds, service tags, and manufacturer instructions.
Inspect cords, plugs, gas connections, hoses, guards, doors, seals, blades, controls, vents, casters, and mounting points.
Confirm the area is clean, dry, unobstructed, ventilated, and free of leaks, grease buildup, pests, or stored items.
Verify utilities, suppression systems, drains, filters, water, and required clearances before startup.
Check that safety devices, shields, interlocks, thermostats, alarms, and emergency shutoffs are present and functional.
Start equipment only in the approved sequence and observe sound, odor, heat, pressure, vibration, flame, and display behavior.
Verify operating temperature or performance before loading food or assigning production.
Stop, disconnect when authorized, tag out, and notify management when any unsafe or abnormal condition is found.
Record the inspection result, defect, temporary restriction, service request, and person responsible.
Obtain manager release before employees use equipment that was previously out of service or repaired. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The employee can identify the manufacturer instruction, shutdown control, performance limit, authorized service role, and release requirement for equipment opening inspection.
□ Inspect cords, plugs, gas connections, hoses, guards, doors, seals, blades, controls, vents, casters, and mounting points.
□ Verify utilities, suppression systems, drains, filters, water, and required clearances before startup.
□ Start equipment only in the approved sequence and observe sound, odor, heat, pressure, vibration, flame, and display behavior.

sops.title: Fryer Filtering and Cleaning SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To filter and clean fryers safely while controlling hot oil, burns, ignition, product quality, waste oil, equipment condition, and documentation.
steps: Follow the fryer manufacturer instructions and confirm the unit is cool enough and safe for filtering.
Put on required PPE, secure the area, remove nearby water, and verify the correct filter equipment and oil container.
Turn off or place the fryer in the approved filter mode; never drain hot oil into an unapproved container.
Remove baskets and skim loose debris without splashing or contacting hot surfaces.
Drain oil through the approved filter system while monitoring hoses, valves, seals, and container capacity.
Clean crumbs and sediment from the fry pot using approved tools; do not use water on hot oil or energized components.
Inspect oil quality, level, odor, color, and service life and obtain approval before topping off or discarding.
Return filtered oil, close valves, verify correct level, and restart only according to manufacturer instructions.
Wipe exterior surfaces, clean the floor, store filter tools, and move used oil through the approved route.
Record filtering, oil change, defect, spill, burn, or service need and obtain manager verification. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Flat-Top Cleaning SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To clean the flat-top safely after controlled cooldown using approved tools and chemicals without damaging the surface or contaminating food areas.
steps: Follow manufacturer instructions and allow the flat-top to reach the approved cleaning temperature or cool-down state.
Put on required PPE, post the area, remove food, and protect nearby clean surfaces and ingredients.
Scrape food residue and grease toward the trough using an approved scraper held away from the body.
Empty and clean the grease drawer or trough without overfilling, spilling, or mixing water with hot grease.
Apply only the approved cleaner or method; never use chemicals or abrasives prohibited by the manufacturer.
Scrub the cooking surface, corners, splash guards, front edge, knobs, and surrounding nonfood-contact areas.
Remove residue and rinse or wipe as required so no chemical or debris remains on the cooking surface.
Dry, season, or protect the surface according to the approved process and reinstall clean components.
Clean the floor and nearby wall surfaces and report warping, cracks, hot spots, loose controls, or gas concerns.
Record completion and obtain manager verification before the unit is returned to service. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Ice Machine Cleaning SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To clean and sanitize the ice machine on the approved schedule while protecting ice, water-contact surfaces, filters, chemicals, and restart verification.
steps: Follow the manufacturer cleaning and sanitation procedure and place the ice machine out of service.
Protect or discard ice as required; never clean over usable ice or place tools inside the bin.
Wash hands, put on required PPE, and gather the approved cleaner, sanitizer, brushes, and test materials.
Turn off water or power only as instructed and remove approved parts without damaging sensors, tubes, or seals.
Remove scale, slime, soil, and mineral buildup from food-contact and water-contact components.
Rinse completely and sanitize the machine, bin, scoop holder, chute, and removable parts at the approved concentration and contact time.
Allow surfaces to air-dry when required and reassemble all parts correctly.
Restart the machine, discard the required initial ice, and verify water flow, drainage, temperature, and ice quality.
Store the scoop correctly and report leaks, mold, recurring buildup, damaged parts, or treatment-system problems.
Record the cleaning date, chemical, concentration, employee, and manager verification. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Refrigeration Temperature Review SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To review refrigeration temperatures, product conditions, alarms, doors, airflow, records, and corrective actions before food safety is lost.
steps: Identify every refrigeration unit, assigned temperature limit, product type, and required review time.
Inspect doors, gaskets, airflow, fan operation, displays, alarms, condensation, ice, and unit loading.
Read the unit display and measure representative food temperatures with a clean calibrated thermometer.
Record actual unit and product temperatures, time, employee, and any recent door, delivery, or defrost activity.
Recheck unexpected readings and verify the thermometer before concluding that the unit failed.
Move or protect food only through the approved alternate refrigeration or ice-control process.
Evaluate affected product using documented time, temperature, and product history under manager authority.
Adjust loading or door use only when safe; do not alter controls or repair equipment without authorization.
Contact service for repeated or material failure and record food disposition and corrective action.
Verify recovery and sustained control before returning the unit to normal use. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Preventive Maintenance Log SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To maintain a preventive-maintenance log that identifies equipment, required work, frequency, completion, service provider, cost, and follow-up status.
steps: Review manufacturer intervals, service history, inspections, warranty requirements, and recurring equipment failures.
List each equipment asset, location, model, identifier, responsible manager, and authorized service provider.
Schedule cleaning, lubrication, filter, calibration, inspection, replacement, and professional-service tasks.
Coordinate shutdown, product relocation, access, permits, and service timing to protect operations and safety.
Record work performed, parts used, readings, technician, cost, findings, and recommended follow-up.
Verify that guards, panels, utilities, controls, alarms, and safety devices are restored after service.
Test equipment under the approved operating condition before releasing it to employees.
Tag unresolved defects and define operating restrictions, repair deadline, and alternate process.
Review overdue work and repeated failures with ownership, purchasing, and department leaders.
Retain service records and update the next-due date and SOP when equipment or instructions change. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Smallwares Inspection SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To inspect smallwares for cleanliness, damage, correct quantity, safe storage, and removal or replacement of unsafe items.
steps: Gather knives, utensils, pans, boards, containers, scoops, racks, and other assigned smallwares for inspection.
Separate clean items from dirty, damaged, unapproved, or employee-owned items.
Inspect for cracks, chips, sharp edges, rust, loose handles, worn coatings, warping, missing parts, and difficult-to-clean surfaces.
Verify food-contact items are clean, dry, odor-free, and made of approved material.
Check that measuring, portioning, and temperature tools are accurate and matched to the intended use.
Remove damaged items from service immediately and place them in the approved hold or disposal area.
Record the item, quantity, defect, station, and replacement or repair need.
Restock each station to the approved par without mixing damaged or unverified items back into service.
Escalate repeated breakage, shortage, unsafe substitutions, or purchasing concerns to management.
Complete the smallwares count and manager verification before opening or shift release. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Knife Safety and Storage SOP
sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.
sops.role: The operator uses and cleans equipment as approved. Management removes unsafe equipment from service and controls repair and return.
sops.purpose: To use, transport, clean, and store knives safely with approved cutting surfaces, handling methods, racks or sheaths, and damage controls.
steps: Use only approved knives matched to the task and inspect the blade, tip, handle, rivets, and guard before use.
Select a stable approved cutting board and place a damp towel or nonslip base underneath when required.
Keep the cutting area clear, use required cut-resistant PPE, and maintain a controlled body position.
Cut away from the body with the guiding hand protected and fingers curled out of the blade path.
Do not catch a falling knife, carry it hidden, leave it in a sink, or place it under towels or food.
Carry a knife point down at the side and announce movement through crowded or blind areas.
Clean one knife at a time using the approved method and never reach into cloudy or filled sinks.
Sharpen or hone only with training and approved equipment and remove damaged knives from service.
Store clean dry knives in the approved rack, sheath, or secured location with blades protected.
Report cuts, near misses, damage, loss, and unauthorized knives and obtain manager follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.frequency: Before use, during operation, at shutdown or cleaning, and whenever damage, failure, or unsafe performance is observed.

steps: Review manufacturer instructions, the current SOP, service history, and authorized task.

Stop use, disconnect or isolate energy when trained and safe, and keep others away.

PART 8 FACILITY, WASTE & PEST CONTROL 15 ready-to-customize SOPs These SOPs control exterior and entry safety, patios, lighting, ventilation, plumbing, waste, oil, dumpsters, pests, and vendor access.

sops.title: Building Exterior Walkthrough SOP
sops.frequency: During opening and closing inspections and whenever a building, utility, access, or environmental condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned employee inspects and reports conditions. Management assigns correction, restricts unsafe areas, and verifies completion.
sops.purpose: To inspect the building exterior for lighting, access, damage, drainage, waste, pest evidence, security, and conditions requiring correction or vendor support.
steps: Walk the full building perimeter before opening, at the scheduled review, and before final lock-up.
Inspect doors, windows, walls, roofline, utility entries, vents, locks, cameras, and signs of forced access.
Check sidewalks, curbs, ramps, stairs, handrails, drainage, mats, and accessible routes for hazards.
Look for broken glass, needles, waste, standing water, ice, grease, pests, graffiti, and unauthorized storage.
Verify exterior lighting, address numbers, exits, fire lanes, utility areas, and emergency access remain clear.
Inspect grease, dumpster, delivery, propane, gas, electrical, and employee-entry zones for leaks or damage.
Do not enter or disturb an area that suggests crime, fire, gas, electrical, structural, or hazardous-material danger.
Correct minor housekeeping issues and isolate larger hazards with barriers or restricted access.
Contact management, property, vendor, utility, security, police, or emergency services as appropriate.
Record findings, photos, owner, deadline, temporary control, and reinspection. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

□ Inspect doors, windows, walls, roofline, utility entries, vents, locks, cameras, and signs of forced access.
□ Look for broken glass, needles, waste, standing water, ice, grease, pests, graffiti, and unauthorized storage.
□ Inspect grease, dumpster, delivery, propane, gas, electrical, and employee-entry zones for leaks or damage.
□ Correct minor housekeeping issues and isolate larger hazards with barriers or restricted access.
□ Record findings, photos, owner, deadline, temporary control, and reinspection.
sops.correction:
• Completing building exterior walkthrough from a desk or checklist without inspecting the actual area and surrounding conditions.
• Leaving a hazard, leak, pest source, waste problem, access issue, or vendor action without an owner and deadline.
• Allowing contractors or waste movement to contaminate food areas or bypass access controls.
• Failing to protect guests, employees, traffic, drainage, lighting, and emergency access.
• Closing the record without reinspection, documentation, and manager verification.

sops.title: Parking Lot and Entry Safety SOP
sops.frequency: During opening and closing inspections and whenever a building, utility, access, or environmental condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned employee inspects and reports conditions. Management assigns correction, restricts unsafe areas, and verifies completion.
sops.purpose: To keep parking and entry areas safe, lighted, accessible, unobstructed, and free of hazards that could injure guests or employees.
steps: Inspect the parking lot and entry routes for traffic, pedestrian, lighting, surface, weather, and security conditions.
Check potholes, curbs, wheel stops, ramps, stairs, crosswalks, drains, ice, water, grease, and loose debris.
Verify accessible spaces, access aisles, curb ramps, and entry paths are clear and not used for storage or delivery.
Confirm signs, lane markings, speed controls, exterior lights, cameras, and emergency access are visible and working.
Remove or isolate broken glass, trip hazards, abandoned items, and spills without entering vehicle danger.
Coordinate deliveries, employee parking, rideshare, curbside, and guest pickup so routes do not conflict.
Do not direct employees into active traffic, severe weather, criminal activity, or unsafe cleanup conditions.
Notify property management, vendors, towing, utility, security, or emergency services when needed.
Communicate temporary closures or alternate routes to hosts, curbside staff, employees, and guests.
Document the hazard, location, temporary control, responsible party, and reinspection. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Patio Opening and Closing SOP
sops.frequency: During opening and closing inspections and whenever a building, utility, access, or environmental condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned employee inspects and reports conditions. Management assigns correction, restricts unsafe areas, and verifies completion.
sops.purpose: To open and close the patio through verified furniture, cleanliness, weather, lighting, access, service, safety, and security checks.
steps: Review weather, temperature, wind, lighting, staffing, reservations, occupancy, and local patio restrictions.
Inspect the surface, railings, gates, umbrellas, heaters, furniture, planters, exits, and accessible route.
Secure or remove unstable, wet, damaged, hot, sharp, or wind-sensitive items before seating guests.
Verify tables and chairs are clean, level, spaced, and arranged within approved capacity and egress.
Test approved lighting, fans, heaters, music, POS, communication, and service-station equipment.
Establish weather-monitoring, closing authority, guest-relocation, and employee communication responsibilities.
Stop seating and clear the patio for lightning, dangerous wind, extreme temperature, smoke, flooding, or another unsafe condition.
During closing, account for guests and checks and move food, alcohol, cash, devices, and supplies indoors.
Shut off and secure heaters, umbrellas, gates, furniture, lighting, and equipment according to policy.
Document damage, weather closure, guest relocation, maintenance, and manager verification. & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.frequency: During opening and closing inspections and whenever a building, utility, access, or environmental condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned employee inspects and reports conditions. Management assigns correction, restricts unsafe areas, and verifies completion.
sops.purpose: To keep restrooms supplied with soap, hand-drying materials, tissue, liners, and other required items and escalate any condition that prevents safe use.
steps: Review the restroom supply par, approved products, dispenser types, storage location, and check frequency.
Inspect toilet tissue, towels or dryers, soap, sanitizer when provided, liners, seat covers, and baby-changing supplies.

sops.title: HVAC Comfort and Ventilation Check SOP
sops.frequency: During opening and closing inspections and whenever a building, utility, access, or environmental condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned employee inspects and reports conditions. Management assigns correction, restricts unsafe areas, and verifies completion.
sops.purpose: To maintain safe and comfortable HVAC and ventilation conditions by checking temperatures, airflow, odors, hoods, exhaust, complaints, and dangerous-atmosphere triggers.
steps: Review indoor temperature, humidity, odor, smoke, condensation, hood, makeup-air, and guest or employee complaints.
Check thermostats, vents, returns, filters, doors, fans, kitchen hoods, restroom exhaust, and known problem areas.
Verify kitchen ventilation operates before heat-, smoke-, steam-, or gas-producing equipment is used.
Keep vents and returns clear and do not alter controls, filters, dampers, or equipment without authorization.
Separate comfort concerns from smoke, gas, carbon monoxide, refrigerant, electrical, or fire hazards.
Stop affected equipment and evacuate or contact emergency services when a dangerous atmosphere is suspected.
Adjust approved settings or service zones only within manager authority and monitor the result.
Communicate realistic limitations and seating or work-area changes to employees and guests.
Contact the landlord or qualified HVAC service provider for repeated or material failure.
Record readings, complaints, equipment status, actions, service contact, and recheck. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Plumbing Leak Response SOP
sops.frequency: During opening and closing inspections and whenever a building, utility, access, or environmental condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned employee inspects and reports conditions. Management assigns correction, restricts unsafe areas, and verifies completion.
sops.purpose: To control plumbing leaks quickly by identifying the source, protecting people and food, restricting affected areas, stopping water when authorized, and arranging repair.
steps: Identify the source, location, flow, water condition, electrical exposure, food impact, and whether the leak is controlled.
Stop nearby work and protect guests and employees with barriers and wet-floor controls.
Shut off the local fixture or water supply only when trained and authorized.
Move or protect food, packaging, utensils, chemicals, records, and electrical equipment from water exposure.
Do not use contaminated water, ceiling water, sewage, or unknown leakage for any cleaning or food process.
Contact management, property, plumber, utility, or emergency services based on severity.
Collect water only with approved containers and prevent flow into food areas, electrical systems, and public routes.
Discard or hold affected food and single-use items and clean and sanitize exposed areas after repair.
Verify plumbing, water quality, floors, walls, ceilings, equipment, and slip hazards before reopening.
Document the leak, cause, damage, product disposition, repair, sanitation, and follow-up. & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Cardboard Breakdown and Recycling SOP
sops.frequency: During collection, separation, transport, storage, vendor pickup, spill response, and closing verification.
sops.role: Employees separate and move waste safely. Management verifies containment, vendor requirements, records, and site condition.
sops.purpose: To break down and store cardboard safely without blocking exits, contaminating food areas, attracting pests, or exceeding recycling capacity.
steps: Remove food, grease, plastic liners, waxed material, and other nonaccepted contents from cardboard.
Keep boxes away from food preparation, clean storage, exits, electrical panels, and ignition sources.
Break boxes down using the approved safe method and cutting tool away from the body.
Flatten cardboard fully and remove or control staples, bands, and sharp edges.
Stack or bale within the approved height, weight, capacity, and equipment rules.
Keep the storage area dry and inspect for pests, moisture, product residue, and hidden trash.
Do not climb, jump on, or hand-compress cardboard in compactors or balers.
Operate balers or compactors only with training, guards, interlocks, and lockout procedures.
Move cardboard at the scheduled time and secure exterior containers against wind and unauthorized access.
Record equipment, vendor, pest, injury, overflow, or contamination problems and manager follow-up. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Used Oil Handling SOP
sops.frequency: During collection, separation, transport, storage, vendor pickup, spill response, and closing verification.
sops.role: Employees separate and move waste safely. Management verifies containment, vendor requirements, records, and site condition.
sops.purpose: To transfer used cooking oil safely into approved containers while preventing burns, spills, drain contamination, unauthorized access, and unrecorded loss.
steps: Confirm the approved used-oil container, capacity, lid, transfer route, pickup schedule, and spill supplies.
Allow oil to reach the approved handling condition and wear required heat-, slip-, and splash-resistant PPE.
Use only approved closed containers, carts, hoses, and fittings; never use open buckets through guest or crowded routes.
Keep water, ice, chemicals, food debris, and incompatible materials out of used oil.
Move oil slowly through the designated route and stop if the floor, container, valve, or path is unsafe.
Transfer oil without overfilling, splashing, or leaving lids and valves unsecured.
Clean drips immediately using the approved grease-spill method and keep drains protected.
Record quantity, date, employee, pickup, spill, loss, or vendor issue when required.
Report leaks, damage, overflow, theft, pests, or unsafe vendor equipment.
Secure the area, wash hands, and obtain manager verification of containment and documentation. CUSTOMIZATION

Contact the approved waste vendor or property manager and assign temporary controls when service fails.

sops.title: Pest Prevention SOP
sops.frequency: During routine prevention checks and immediately when evidence, entry points, damage, or a sighting is found.
sops.role: Employees prevent access and report evidence. Management protects food, documents findings, and coordinates licensed treatment.
sops.purpose: To prevent pests by controlling food, water, shelter, entry points, waste, deliveries, cleaning, and timely licensed-vendor follow-up.
steps: Review pest-control reports, prior sightings, service recommendations, and unresolved structural or sanitation issues.
Inspect exterior doors, sweeps, windows, drains, pipes, roof or wall openings, receiving points, and waste areas.
Keep food, packaging, and utensils off the floor, covered, dated, rotated, and protected from contamination.
Remove standing water, crumbs, grease, clutter, cardboard, and inaccessible buildup that provide food or shelter.
Maintain tight waste lids, clean dumpsters, dry mop areas, screened openings, and working door closures.
Inspect traps and monitoring devices only as authorized; do not move or apply pesticides without approval.
Correct or assign sanitation, storage, building, vendor, and maintenance actions with deadlines.
Train employees to report evidence immediately and never conceal, sweep away, or discard evidence before documentation.

sops.title: Employee Injury SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Any time an employee is cut, burned, falls, slips, strains, becomes ill, is exposed to chemicals, or is otherwise injured at work.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To protect an injured employee, obtain appropriate emergency or medical help, secure the hazard, complete required reporting, and prevent recurrence.
steps: Stop work, protect the injured employee from additional harm, and notify the manager immediately.
Call 911 for serious, life-threatening, or uncertain conditions and follow dispatcher instructions.
Provide first aid only within current training, available equipment, and company policy.
Do not move the employee unless remaining creates immediate danger or trained responders direct movement.
Isolate equipment, chemicals, food, broken glass, blood, spills, or other hazards that could cause another injury.
Arrange authorized medical evaluation or transportation and do not require the employee to drive when unsafe.
Preserve the scene, equipment, video, photos, witness information, and work records when appropriate.
Complete required injury, workers' compensation, OSHA, insurer, or company notifications through authorized management.
Protect private medical information and prohibit retaliation for good-faith reporting.
Assign corrective action, return-to-work routing, equipment release, sanitation, retraining, and follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Arrange authorized medical evaluation or transportation and do not require the employee to drive when unsafe.
□ Complete required injury, workers' compensation, OSHA, insurer, or company notifications through authorized management.
□ Assign corrective action, return-to-work routing, equipment release, sanitation, retraining, and follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Moving the employee, providing care, or transporting them beyond training and policy.
• Leaving the original hazard exposed or allowing equipment back into service.
• Delaying emergency help, medical evaluation, or required reporting.
• Recording blame, diagnosis, or unnecessary medical details instead of objective facts.
• Failing to assign corrective action, return-to-work routing, and follow-up.

sops.title: Guest Injury SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest is injured, reports an injury, or alleges that an injury occurred in or near the restaurant.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To assist an injured guest promptly, secure and preserve the scene, protect private information, and complete authorized incident follow-up without admitting fault.
steps: Notify the manager and approach the guest calmly without admitting fault or debating responsibility.
Call 911 for serious, life-threatening, or uncertain conditions and follow dispatcher instructions.
Offer only assistance within training and policy; do not move the guest unless immediate danger requires it.
Secure the area and isolate the spill, object, furniture, equipment, food, chemical, or other suspected hazard.
Obtain the guest's name and contact information if voluntarily provided and record the exact reported location and time.
Identify witnesses separately and preserve video, photos, receipts, product, equipment, and scene information.
Do not ask the guest to sign a release, minimize symptoms, or promise payment or a specific outcome.
Notify ownership, insurer, security, property management, or authorities according to policy.
Complete objective incident documentation and protect medical, payment, and personal information.
Correct the hazard, verify the area before reopening, and assign guest and management follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Correct the hazard, verify the area before reopening, and assign guest and management follow-up.

• Arguing, admitting fault, minimizing symptoms, or promising payment or a specific outcome.

• Combining witness statements or failing to preserve video, receipts, product, or equipment.
• Exposing private guest information or discussing the incident publicly.
• Closing the record without hazard correction, required notification, and guest follow-up.

5. Obtain the guest's name and contact information if voluntarily provided and record the exact reported location and time.
6. Identify witnesses separately and preserve video, photos, receipts, product, equipment, and scene information.
7. Do not ask the guest to sign a release, minimize symptoms, or promise payment or a specific outcome.
8. Notify ownership, insurer, security, property management, or authorities according to policy.
9. Complete objective incident documentation and protect medical, payment, and personal information.
10. Correct the hazard, verify the area before reopening, and assign guest and management follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.frequency: Immediately when the emergency or safety condition is observed or reported.

Complete incident documentation, replace used emergency supplies, and assign manager follow-up. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Fire SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Immediately when the emergency or safety condition is observed or reported.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To protect guests and employees during a fire through immediate alarm, emergency notification, evacuation, accountability, responder support, and controlled recovery.
steps: Activate the fire alarm, call 911, and state the restaurant name, exact address, and known fire location.
Direct guests and employees to approved exits and assembly points without delaying for cash, product, or personal property.
Shut off equipment or utilities only when trained, authorized, and able to do so without delaying evacuation.
Use an extinguisher only if trained, the fire is small and controllable, the correct extinguisher is available, and a clear exit remains behind the user.
Do not enter smoke, open hot doors, fight a spreading fire, use elevators, or block responder access.
Assist people with mobility, sensory, or communication needs using the approved evacuation plan.
Managers account for employees, guests, contractors, and known missing people at the assembly point.
Remain outside, prevent reentry, and follow fire-department instructions.
Tell responders about gas, fryers, suppression systems, chemicals, utilities, and anyone unaccounted for.
Notify ownership, preserve records, document the incident, and reopen only after official and management authorization.

• Reentering before fire officials authorize it.

sops.title: Gas Leak SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Any time gas odor, suspected gas leak, hissing gas sound, gas equipment issue, or carbon monoxide concern is reported.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To protect life during a suspected gas leak by preventing ignition, evacuating, contacting emergency and utility responders, and prohibiting reentry until clearance.
steps: Treat any gas odor, hissing, alarm, failed ignition, or suspected leak as an immediate hazard.
Do not create sparks or flames, operate electrical switches, start vehicles nearby, or use a phone in the suspected area.
Warn nearby people and begin evacuation using the approved route without attempting to locate the leak.
Shut off gas only if trained, authorized, and able to do so without entering danger or delaying evacuation.
Call 911 and the gas utility from a safe location and provide the exact address and known conditions.
Account for employees, guests, contractors, and anyone believed to remain inside.
Keep people away from the building, meters, tanks, vents, and ignition sources.
Do not reenter, restart equipment, or restore gas until the fire department, utility, or qualified authority clears the site.
Notify ownership, landlord, insurer, and service vendors according to the emergency plan.
Document the timeline, observations, actions, repairs, clearance, testing, and reopening approval. CUSTOMIZATION

□ Document the timeline, observations, actions, repairs, clearance, testing, and reopening approval.

• Using switches, phones, flames, vehicles, or equipment in the suspected area.
• Searching for the leak or shutting gas off without training and safe access.
• Allowing people to remain near the building, meter, tank, vent, or ignition source.
• Reentering or restarting equipment before qualified clearance.
• Failing to document repair, testing, authority clearance, and reopening approval.

sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Immediately when the emergency or safety condition is observed or reported.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To control a power outage so the restaurant protects life safety, food, refrigeration, ventilation, payments, security, and an orderly closure or recovery.
steps: Confirm the outage scope and start time and identify any injury, fire, gas, electrical, elevator, or security hazard.
Notify management and contact the utility, landlord, electrician, or approved service provider from a safe location.
Stop unsafe cooking, ventilation-dependent equipment, powered doors, elevators, and other affected operations.
Use only approved emergency lighting; do not use candles, open flames, unsafe wiring, or unapproved generators.
Keep refrigeration doors closed and begin documented time-temperature monitoring for affected food.
Shift to approved manual order, payment, communication, and guest-accounting procedures only when safe.
Restrict or close operations when lighting, egress, ventilation, handwashing, refrigeration, payment, or security cannot be maintained.
Communicate clearly with employees and guests and account for people during closure or evacuation.
After restoration, verify equipment, refrigeration, alarms, POS, ventilation, utilities, and food disposition before reopening.
Record the outage, temperatures, transactions, losses, service contacts, decisions, and manager approval. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Active Threat or Violent Guest SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Whenever a guest, employee, or outside person threatens violence, becomes physically aggressive, displays a weapon, or creates a reasonable fear of immediate harm.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To protect guests and employees during an active threat or violent incident through immediate escape or secure shelter, emergency notification, accountability, and law-enforcement cooperation.
steps: Recognize the threat and prioritize immediate escape from danger when a safe route is available.
Call 911 when safe and provide the exact location, description, direction, weapon information, and known injuries.
Warn others without drawing attention to yourself and follow current law-enforcement or dispatcher instructions.
If escape is not possible, move to a secure location, lock or block access when appropriate, silence devices, and stay out of view.
Do not confront, pursue, negotiate, film, or attempt physical intervention unless necessary to protect life and consistent with training.
Keep guests and employees away from the threat and do not direct people toward an uncertain route.
When police arrive, keep hands visible, follow commands, and do not run toward officers.
Provide first aid only when the area is safe and within current training.
Preserve the scene and do not share unverified information publicly or on social media.
Account for people, notify ownership, complete objective records, and arrange employee and guest support. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Robbery SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Any time robbery, attempted robbery, theft with threat, or forced cash demand occurs.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To protect people first during a robbery or attempted robbery and preserve accurate evidence and reporting after the immediate danger ends.
steps: Stay calm, prioritize life safety, and do not resist, argue, chase, or make sudden movements.
Follow demands when directly threatened without volunteering additional access or information.
Activate an alarm only if it can be done without increasing danger and according to training.
Observe only details that can be noticed safely, such as appearance, voice, direction, vehicle, and weapon.
Do not block exits, attempt to detain the person, or follow outside.
When safe, lock access as directed, call 911, and provide the exact address and known facts.
Protect injured people and provide first aid only within training and when the area is safe.
Preserve the scene, notes, video, transaction records, touched objects, and separate witness accounts.
Notify ownership, security, bank, insurer, and other required contacts through authorized management.
Complete objective documentation and follow law-enforcement direction before reopening or discussing the event. CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Missing Child or Lost Child SOP
sops.station: Part 9 — Employee & Guest Safety / Emergency Response
sops.frequency: Any time a parent reports a missing child, a child is found alone, or employees suspect a child is separated from a guardian.
sops.role: Employees protect life, notify management, and follow trained emergency actions. Management contacts responders, controls accountability, and documents.
sops.purpose: To coordinate a rapid, controlled response when a child is missing, separated from a guardian, or found without a verified guardian.
steps: Notify the manager immediately and obtain the child's name, age, clothing, description, last known location, and guardian information.
Assign specific employees to search approved zones while maintaining supervision of their current safety responsibilities.
Check restrooms, dining areas, patio, lobby, entrance, pickup zones, and other safe areas without creating additional risk.
Observe exits and parking areas only as allowed by policy and safety conditions; do not physically detain people.
Call 911 promptly when the child is not found within the approved immediate-search period, danger is suspected, or the guardian requests emergency help.
If a separated child is found, keep the child with the manager and a second employee in a visible safe area.
Release the child only after the manager and authorities, when involved, confirm the guardian according to policy.
Preserve video, witness, timing, and communication records and avoid broadcasting unnecessary personal information.
Do not post the child's information publicly or allow employees to conduct uncoordinated searches off property.
Complete the incident record, guardian communication, authority contact, and post-incident review. & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Water Outage SOP
sops.frequency: Any time water service stops, water pressure is lost, water is unsafe, or water use is restricted.
sops.role: Management activates the approved continuity plan, protects people and food, assigns communication, and authorizes reopening or recovery.
sops.purpose: To protect food safety, sanitation, hygiene, restrooms, and guest service during a water outage and restore operations only after approved clearance.
steps: Confirm the outage or unsafe-water condition, affected fixtures, start time, cause, and estimated restoration.
Notify ownership, the utility, landlord, and local regulatory authority when required.
Stop food preparation, handwashing, warewashing, beverage, ice, restroom, and cleaning processes that lack safe water.
Evaluate whether approved alternate water, handwashing, restroom, and warewashing methods can support restricted operations.
Protect food, ice, beverages, equipment, and clean utensils from contamination or unapproved water use.
Restrict service or close when employee hygiene, sanitation, plumbing, restrooms, or food-safety requirements cannot be maintained.
Communicate the operating decision and limitations to employees, guests, vendors, and delivery partners.
Track affected food, temperatures, transactions, labor, and closure time while awaiting restoration.
After restoration, flush lines, clean and sanitize equipment, replace filters, discard affected ice or product, and verify plumbing.
Obtain required clearance and manager approval before reopening and retain the outage record. CUSTOMIZATION
sops.checks:
□ The manager can state the backup or closure trigger, operating authority, communication plan, required records, and recovery approval for water outage.
□ Notify ownership, the utility, landlord, and local regulatory authority when required.
□ Evaluate whether approved alternate water, handwashing, restroom, and warewashing methods can support restricted operations.
□ Restrict service or close when employee hygiene, sanitation, plumbing, restrooms, or food-safety requirements cannot be maintained.
□ Track affected food, temperatures, transactions, labor, and closure time while awaiting restoration.
□ Obtain required clearance and manager approval before reopening and retain the outage record.

• Continuing normal service without safe handwashing, restrooms, warewashing, or sanitation.
• Using unapproved water or failing to control affected ice, beverages, filters, and utensils.
• Failing to notify the utility, ownership, or regulatory authority when required.
• Reopening before flushing, sanitation, plumbing, ice, filters, and product disposition are complete.
• Losing the outage timeline, temperature, transaction, closure, and approval record.

sops.title: Kitchen Display System Down SOP
sops.frequency: Any time POS system, terminals, printers, handhelds, kitchen display, or payment system stops working.
sops.role: Management activates the approved continuity plan, protects people and food, assigns communication, and authorizes reopening or recovery.
sops.purpose: To maintain one accurate kitchen order queue when the kitchen display system fails and reconcile all orders before normal processing resumes.
steps: Confirm whether the failure affects one display, one station, printers, the POS interface, or the entire kitchen system.
Notify the manager, expo, cooks, servers, bar, to-go team, and approved technical support.
Activate the approved paper-ticket or verbal backup process with one designated control point.
Number and time every order and record table, server, course, modifiers, allergies, and special requests clearly.
Require direct confirmation for allergy and high-risk special-request orders before cooking.
Maintain one master order queue and mark fired, working, completed, delivered, cancelled, and remade items.
Prevent duplicate production by controlling reprints, verbal calls, and ticket handoffs.
Communicate realistic delays and menu restrictions to the floor and stop orders the kitchen cannot track safely.
After restoration, reconcile open checks and system orders before reentering or closing tickets.
Document the failure, backup period, missed or duplicate items, support contact, and corrective action. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.title: Emergency Closure and Reopening SOP
sops.frequency: When a utility, system, facility, or crisis condition interrupts normal operations or requires closure or recovery.
sops.role: Management activates the approved continuity plan, protects people and food, assigns communication, and authorizes reopening or recovery.

steps: Assess life safety, utilities, food safety, sanitation, staffing, access, systems, weather, and official direction.
The authorized manager decides whether to restrict service, stop new orders, evacuate, shelter, or close.
Notify employees, guests, delivery partners, vendors, ownership, landlords, and authorities using approved messages.
Resolve or document active orders, payments, refunds, reservations, employee time, deliveries, and guest property.
Protect or dispose of food based on documented time, temperature, contamination, water, and utility conditions.
Shut down or secure equipment, chemicals, cash, records, keys, alarms, doors, utilities, and the building.
Maintain the incident timeline, responsible people, pending repair, inspection, and communication assignments.
Before reopening, verify utilities, water, ventilation, refrigeration, sanitation, pest control, equipment, and safe access.
Verify staffing, product, systems, cash, records, permits, authority clearance, and employee briefing.
The authorized manager signs the reopening checklist and communicates the approved reopening time. VERIFICATION & CUSTOMIZATION

sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for catering inquiry intake and qualification so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the current approved scope for catering inquiry intake and qualification, including date/time, location, guest count or demand assumption, responsible leader, and special commitments.
Review staffing, production, equipment, transport/site, payment, guest-access, safety, and food-safety requirements; assign an owner to each critical control.
Inspect the required area, equipment, supplies, communication method, and backup resources before product or guests arrive.
Stage and label materials in the sequence they will be used; separate guest-specific, event-specific, allergen, payment, and high-risk items as applicable.
Execute catering inquiry intake and qualification using the current event/service plan and verify critical handoffs before proceeding to the next phase.
Monitor volume, staffing, timing, food condition, guest flow, and safety; record exceptions and adjust before control is lost.
Escalate shortages, unsafe conditions, late changes, quality failures, or guest commitments the team cannot meet to the event manager immediately.
Complete the guest/client or internal handoff, confirm unresolved items, and document any approved change to the original plan.
Reconcile product, equipment, payments, damage, waste, incidents, and outstanding follow-up; clean and restore the work/site area.
The accountable manager reviews the record, closes open issues, and captures lessons that should change the next comparable event.
sops.checks:

□ Unsafe, out-of-standard, unidentified, or undocumented conditions were held, stopped, or escalated instead of informally accepted.
□ Corrective actions and product/equipment/guest/employee disposition were completed and documented when required.
□ The accountable manager or program owner completed final verification and assigned unresolved follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Using an old, generic, or remembered procedure instead of the current approved specialty-operation standard.
• Starting before required permits, approvals, trained people, utilities, equipment, labels, or records are ready.
• Failing to document actual conditions, readings, identities, handoffs, or deviations at the time they occur.
• Continuing service or releasing product/equipment when a required control cannot be verified.
• Treating a vendor, platform, event organizer, sister unit, or outside agency as responsible for controls that still belong to the restaurant.
• Closing the activity without manager verification, record completion, cleanup/restoration, and follow-up ownership.

sops.title: Mobile Unit Pre-Departure Readiness SOP
sops.station: Part — Food Trucks, Mobile Units & Temporary Events
sops.frequency: Before the applicable operation, service period, event, route, batch, opening, or equipment use, and again after any material condition changes.
sops.role: The mobile-unit or event manager owns readiness. The person in charge verifies permits, utilities, food-safety controls, equipment, records, and safe return/closeout.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for mobile unit pre-departure readiness so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm that mobile unit pre-departure readiness is authorized under the current mobile/temporary operating plan, permit, event rules, and commissary relationship.
Verify the assigned person in charge, route/site, service window, emergency contacts, and required records for the operating period.
Inspect the unit/booth and all relevant utilities—potable water, wastewater, handwashing, warewashing, refrigeration/hot holding, fuel/power, ventilation, lighting, and waste control.
Load or stage only protected, labeled, approved product and supplies; maintain separation of food, chemicals, waste, personal items, and fuel/equipment hazards.
Perform mobile unit pre-departure readiness using the approved sequence and monitor any food temperature, water, power, sanitation, fuel, or structural condition that can make operation unsafe.
Record required readings, fills, disposals, transfers, checks, or corrective actions at the restaurant-approved frequency.
Stop the affected activity when a critical utility, food-safety control, fuel system, sanitation control, or permit condition cannot be maintained.
Notify the manager/commissary/event authority of any deviation that affects service scope, product disposition, utilities, or safe operation.
At close or return, remove food/waste safely, clean and sanitize the unit/booth, secure fuel/power and equipment, and reconcile product and records.
The person in charge verifies the unit/site is safe, required records are complete, and unresolved defects are tagged for correction before next use.

sops.title: Drive-Thru Lane Opening SOP
sops.frequency: Before the applicable operation, service period, event, route, batch, opening, or equipment use, and again after any material condition changes.
sops.role: The shift leader owns lane, staging, accuracy, and recovery controls. Assigned employees execute the station process and escalate safety, payment, timing, or accuracy failures.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for drive-thru lane opening so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the station, lane, staging zone, menu availability, staffing, devices, and safety controls needed for drive-thru lane opening.
Test communications, order display/payment tools, labels, staging identifiers, and backup methods before volume builds.
Define who owns order acceptance, production, accuracy, payment, staging, handoff, guest updates, and recovery during the shift.
Keep guest/order identity attached to the order through every handoff and separate orders so bags, drinks, condiments, and special requests cannot be mixed.
Execute drive-thru lane opening while monitoring queue length, order age, food quality, traffic/employee safety, and production capacity.
Verify order identity, required packaging, product condition, payment status, and final accuracy before release.
Use the approved throttle, hold, menu-reduction, recovery, remake, or manager-escalation method before delays create uncontrolled errors.
Communicate realistic updates to guests/drivers and document significant delays, complaints, unsafe conditions, or recurring accuracy failures.
Reset the staging/traffic area, clear abandoned or unresolved orders through the approved disposition process, and reconcile exceptions.
The shift leader reviews speed, accuracy, recovery, and safety evidence and assigns follow-up for recurring bottlenecks.

steps: Confirm the station, lane, staging zone, menu availability, staffing, devices, and safety controls needed for drive-thru payment handoff.
Test communications, order display/payment tools, labels, staging identifiers, and backup methods before volume builds.
Define who owns order acceptance, production, accuracy, payment, staging, handoff, guest updates, and recovery during the shift.
Keep guest/order identity attached to the order through every handoff and separate orders so bags, drinks, condiments, and special requests cannot be mixed.
Execute drive-thru payment handoff while monitoring queue length, order age, food quality, traffic/employee safety, and production capacity.
Verify order identity, required packaging, product condition, payment status, and final accuracy before release.
Use the approved throttle, hold, menu-reduction, recovery, remake, or manager-escalation method before delays create uncontrolled errors.
Communicate realistic updates to guests/drivers and document significant delays, complaints, unsafe conditions, or recurring accuracy failures.
Reset the staging/traffic area, clear abandoned or unresolved orders through the approved disposition process, and reconcile exceptions.
The shift leader reviews speed, accuracy, recovery, and safety evidence and assigns follow-up for recurring bottlenecks.

sops.title: Commissary Production Scheduling SOP
sops.station: Part — Commissary, Central Production & Multi-Unit Transfers
sops.frequency: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.
sops.role: The sending location owns production, labeling, and release. The receiving location verifies condition, identity, quantity, traceability, and acceptance before use.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for commissary production scheduling so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the approved production or transfer request for commissary production scheduling, including item identity, quantity, destination, required condition, and accountable sender/receiver.
Verify source product, batch/lot/date information, packaging, labels, transport containers, and calibrated monitoring tools before release.
Prepare product using the approved recipe/process and maintain traceability through cooling, packaging, staging, and loading as applicable.
Label each unit/container with the identifiers required by the company and applicable food-safety/traceability program.
Execute commissary production scheduling using equipment and transport conditions that protect time/temperature control, package integrity, and product identity.
Record departure/release condition, quantities, times, temperatures or other required verification before custody changes.
The receiving employee inspects identity, quantity, packaging, traceability, and product condition before acceptance and records any variance.
Hold and escalate any product with missing identity, damaged packaging, questionable condition, temperature deviation, or unexplained quantity variance.
Reconcile accepted, rejected, returned, wasted, and missing quantities and restore/clean reusable transport equipment.
Sending and receiving managers close the transfer record and investigate recurring yield, loss, timing, or cold-chain problems.

3. Prepare product using the approved recipe/process and maintain traceability through cooling, packaging, staging, and loading as applicable.
4. Label each unit/container with the identifiers required by the company and applicable food-safety/traceability program.
5. Execute commissary packaging and labeling for transfer using equipment and transport conditions that protect time/temperature control, package integrity, and product identity.
6. Record departure/release condition, quantities, times, temperatures or other required verification before custody changes.
7. The receiving employee inspects identity, quantity, packaging, traceability, and product condition before acceptance and records any variance.
8. Hold and escalate any product with missing identity, damaged packaging, questionable condition, temperature deviation, or unexplained quantity variance.
9. Reconcile accepted, rejected, returned, wasted, and missing quantities and restore/clean reusable transport equipment.
10. Sending and receiving managers close the transfer record and investigate recurring yield, loss, timing, or cold-chain problems.
