sourceSections.responsibility: The sending location owns production, labeling, and release. The receiving location verifies condition, identity, quantity, traceability, and acceptance before use.
sourceSections.whenUsed: For every applicable receipt, transfer, pickup, release, or custody handoff, before the product/order is accepted or released.
sourceSections.materials:
• Approved production/transfer order
• Batch, lot, date, label, and traceability materials
• Calibrated thermometers and approved transport equipment
• Transfer manifests, receiving records, and variance forms
• Clean food-grade totes, racks, or containers appropriate to the product
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Every transferred product is identifiable from production through receipt and use.
• Time/temperature-controlled food remains within the restaurant’s approved food-safety controls during production, cooling, transport, and receipt.
• Sending and receiving quantities are reconciled and variances are documented.
• Products with compromised identity, packaging, temperature control, or traceability are held from use pending manager disposition.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Confirm the approved production or transfer request for receiving product from a sister location, including item identity, quantity, destination, required condition, and accountable sender/receiver.
2. Verify source product, batch/lot/date information, packaging, labels, transport containers, and calibrated monitoring tools before release.
3. Prepare product using the approved recipe/process and maintain traceability through cooling, packaging, staging, and loading as applicable.
4. Label each unit/container with the identifiers required by the company and applicable food-safety/traceability program.
5. Execute receiving product from a sister location using equipment and transport conditions that protect time/temperature control, package integrity, and product identity.
6. Record departure/release condition, quantities, times, temperatures or other required verification before custody changes.
7. The receiving employee inspects identity, quantity, packaging, traceability, and product condition before acceptance and records any variance.
8. Hold and escalate any product with missing identity, damaged packaging, questionable condition, temperature deviation, or unexplained quantity variance.
9. Reconcile accepted, rejected, returned, wasted, and missing quantities and restore/clean reusable transport equipment.
10. Sending and receiving managers close the transfer record and investigate recurring yield, loss, timing, or cold-chain problems.

sops.title: Buffet Opening and Line Setup SOP
sops.station: Part — Buffet, Self-Service & Specialty Service Formats
sops.frequency: Before the applicable operation, service period, event, route, batch, opening, or equipment use, and again after any material condition changes.
sops.role: The assigned station employee maintains the control during service. The shift manager verifies setup, monitoring frequency, guest protection, replenishment, and closing disposition.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for buffet opening and line setup so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the approved product/service specification and assigned employee for buffet opening and line setup.
Review required labels, ingredients, equipment, monitoring tools, service/display limits, rotation method, and corrective-action rules.
Inspect and clean the station/equipment; verify barriers, utensils, containers, monitoring devices, and guest-protection controls are ready.
Stage product in controlled quantities, maintain required segregation, and attach identity/date/allergen or handling information before display/use.
Perform buffet opening and line setup using the approved operating sequence; do not mix uncontrolled old and new product or bypass required monitoring.
Check product condition, time/temperature, labels, equipment, guest-contact risk, and sanitation at the restaurant-approved frequency and record results.
Remove, hold, discard, or replace product immediately when a required control is missed, contamination is suspected, or identity cannot be verified.
Replenish only from approved protected stock and keep the station orderly so employees can see age, condition, and ownership of product.
At close/changeover, dispose or store product only under the approved rule, clean and sanitize the station/equipment, and complete records.
The manager reviews the monitoring record and recurring deviations before the next service period.

sops.role: The assigned station employee maintains the control during service. The shift manager verifies setup, monitoring frequency, guest protection, replenishment, and closing disposition.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for buffet closing and leftover disposition so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the approved product/service specification and assigned employee for buffet closing and leftover disposition.
Review required labels, ingredients, equipment, monitoring tools, service/display limits, rotation method, and corrective-action rules.
Inspect and clean the station/equipment; verify barriers, utensils, containers, monitoring devices, and guest-protection controls are ready.
Stage product in controlled quantities, maintain required segregation, and attach identity/date/allergen or handling information before display/use.
Perform buffet closing and leftover disposition using the approved operating sequence; do not mix uncontrolled old and new product or bypass required monitoring.
Check product condition, time/temperature, labels, equipment, guest-contact risk, and sanitation at the restaurant-approved frequency and record results.
Remove, hold, discard, or replace product immediately when a required control is missed, contamination is suspected, or identity cannot be verified.
Replenish only from approved protected stock and keep the station orderly so employees can see age, condition, and ownership of product.
At close/changeover, dispose or store product only under the approved rule, clean and sanitize the station/equipment, and complete records.
The manager reviews the monitoring record and recurring deviations before the next service period.

□ The accountable manager or program owner completed final verification and assigned unresolved follow-up.

• Closing the activity without manager verification, record completion, cleanup/restoration, and follow-up ownership.

Monitor each required critical limit or acceptance point at the specified frequency and record the actual result, employee, date/time, and lot/batch identity as applicable.

Notify the person in charge and follow the approved corrective-action/disposition process; obtain regulatory, program, or technical direction when required.
Complete labeling, storage, service/consumer communication, traceability, and record-retention controls before affected product is released.
The accountable program owner reviews the complete record and authorizes release/continued use only when the documented process meets the approved standard.

steps: Confirm current platform/brand status, menu availability, hours, prices, modifiers, access, equipment, and owner for third-party delivery platform opening check.

Monitor order age, platform status, driver arrival, packaging integrity, product condition, and unresolved exceptions.
Escalate outage, duplicate/missing orders, delayed pickup, suspected fraud, driver identity concerns, or cross-brand mix-ups before release.
Use the approved guest/marketplace recovery path for refunds, remakes, cancellations, and delay communication and document material losses.
Reconcile unresolved orders and reset availability, devices, staging, and access controls at shift end or after recovery.
The manager reviews recurring platform failures, delays, refunds, and handoff exceptions and assigns system/vendor follow-up.

sops.title: Draft Beer Line Cleaning Verification SOP

sops.frequency: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.

steps: Identify the exact equipment/system involved in draft beer line cleaning verification and review current manufacturer instructions, service history, hazards, and employee authorization limits.
Inspect the surrounding area for food, guest, electrical, gas, fire, chemical, pressure, slip/fall, or contamination hazards and control access as needed.
Remove affected equipment from service, isolate energy/product, post signage, or activate the approved emergency control when the condition requires it.
Gather the approved tools/PPE and contact an authorized service provider whenever the work exceeds normal trained-operator duties.
Perform or coordinate draft beer line cleaning verification according to the controlled maintenance/service procedure; never bypass guards, interlocks, alarms, ventilation, or safety devices.
Record findings, measurements, service performed, parts/replenishment, vendor identity, and any condition that can recur.
Clean/sanitize any food-contact or exposed area affected by the work and remove tools, debris, chemicals, and temporary barriers appropriately.
Test normal operation and all relevant safety, alarm, drainage, ventilation, temperature, pressure, or utility functions before return to service.
If the system cannot be verified safe and functional, keep it out of service and implement the approved operational workaround or closure decision.
The manager signs the service record, updates preventive-maintenance needs, and communicates any operating restriction to affected employees.

sourceSections.whenUsed: At the end of the applicable service, event, route, shift, equipment cycle, or temporary operation, before the responsible employee is released.
sourceSections.materials:
• Manufacturer/service documentation
• Preventive-maintenance and inspection records
• Lockout/signage or area-control materials as applicable
• Authorized vendor and emergency contact list
• Verification checklist and post-service record
• Current fire-system service documentation and authorized service contact
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Only trained employees or authorized service providers perform technical maintenance beyond normal operator tasks.
• Equipment or utilities with a suspected safety, sanitation, fire, electrical, gas, or contamination hazard are removed from service or isolated until cleared.
• Required inspections and service records are retained according to company and local requirements.
• Restart occurs only after the affected area is clean, safe, functional, and verified by the accountable manager.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Identify the exact equipment/system involved in hood and exhaust deep-cleaning shutdown and restart and review current manufacturer instructions, service history, hazards, and employee authorization limits.
2. Inspect the surrounding area for food, guest, electrical, gas, fire, chemical, pressure, slip/fall, or contamination hazards and control access as needed.
3. Remove affected equipment from service, isolate energy/product, post signage, or activate the approved emergency control when the condition requires it.
4. Gather the approved tools/PPE and contact an authorized service provider whenever the work exceeds normal trained-operator duties.
5. Perform or coordinate hood and exhaust deep-cleaning shutdown and restart according to the controlled maintenance/service procedure; never bypass guards, interlocks, alarms, ventilation, or safety devices.
6. Record findings, measurements, service performed, parts/replenishment, vendor identity, and any condition that can recur.
7. Clean/sanitize any food-contact or exposed area affected by the work and remove tools, debris, chemicals, and temporary barriers appropriately.
8. Test normal operation and all relevant safety, alarm, drainage, ventilation, temperature, pressure, or utility functions before return to service.
9. If the system cannot be verified safe and functional, keep it out of service and implement the approved operational workaround or closure decision.
10. The manager signs the service record, updates preventive-maintenance needs, and communicates any operating restriction to affected employees.

sops.title: Floodwater Intrusion Assessment and Sanitization SOP
sops.frequency: Immediately when the condition is suspected or confirmed, and continuously until the manager documents safe stabilization, recovery, or closure.
sops.role: The senior manager present activates the response, protects people first, coordinates authorities/vendors, controls product and building decisions, and documents reopening authorization.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for floodwater intrusion assessment and sanitization so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Treat floodwater intrusion assessment and sanitization as an abnormal condition and immediately determine whether people, food, water, utilities, air quality, access, or the building are in immediate danger.
Call emergency services, utilities, property management, health/fire authorities, or other official resources when the event requires external direction.
Stop or restrict affected operations, keep employees/guests away from the hazard, and establish an accountable incident leader and communication method.
Identify potentially affected food, water, equipment, documents, cash/data, and building areas; label/hold or secure them from use until evaluated.

Execute the approved response for floodwater intrusion assessment and sanitization and follow official instructions even when that requires closure, evacuation, sheltering, menu reduction, or disposal.
Account for employees and communicate schedule/access instructions; document important decisions, times, conditions, photos, readings, and authority/vendor contacts.
Do not reopen or restore affected food/equipment merely because the visible hazard has passed; verify sanitation, utilities, structure, food safety, and equipment function.
Complete required cleaning, disinfection, disposal, repair, flushing, pest control, testing, or professional remediation before recommissioning.
Obtain manager/authority approval required by the applicable event and communicate any temporary restriction or reduced operating scope to the team.
Conduct a post-incident review, close employee/guest/vendor follow-up, preserve records, and update continuity controls based on what failed or worked.

sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Life safety and official emergency instructions override normal operations.

sourceSections.procedure:
1. Treat disaster employee accountability and welfare check as an abnormal condition and immediately determine whether people, food, water, utilities, air quality, access, or the building are in immediate danger.
2. Call emergency services, utilities, property management, health/fire authorities, or other official resources when the event requires external direction.
3. Stop or restrict affected operations, keep employees/guests away from the hazard, and establish an accountable incident leader and communication method.
4. Identify potentially affected food, water, equipment, documents, cash/data, and building areas; label/hold or secure them from use until evaluated.
5. Execute the approved response for disaster employee accountability and welfare check and follow official instructions even when that requires closure, evacuation, sheltering, menu reduction, or disposal.
6. Account for employees and communicate schedule/access instructions; document important decisions, times, conditions, photos, readings, and authority/vendor contacts.
7. Do not reopen or restore affected food/equipment merely because the visible hazard has passed; verify sanitation, utilities, structure, food safety, and equipment function.
8. Complete required cleaning, disinfection, disposal, repair, flushing, pest control, testing, or professional remediation before recommissioning.
9. Obtain manager/authority approval required by the applicable event and communicate any temporary restriction or reduced operating scope to the team.
10. Conduct a post-incident review, close employee/guest/vendor follow-up, preserve records, and update continuity controls based on what failed or worked.

sops.title: Food Donation Eligibility and Segregation SOP
sops.station: Part — Food Donation, Sustainability & Reusable Programs
sops.frequency: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.
sops.role: The assigned program owner verifies eligibility, segregation, sanitation, vendor/agency handoff, and records. The manager resolves any food-safety, contamination, vendor, or documentation concern.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for food donation eligibility and segregation so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the approved program criteria, participating vendor/agency, eligible material/product, responsible employee, and required record for food donation eligibility and segregation.
Verify that food-safety, sanitation, chemical, waste, oil, packaging, and cross-contamination controls take priority over diversion or sustainability goals.
Inspect dedicated containers/storage and labels; remove anything damaged, contaminated, leaking, unidentified, or outside program criteria.
Segregate eligible items at the point of generation so they do not become mixed with trash, chemicals, allergens, unsafe food, or non-approved material.
Perform food donation eligibility and segregation using the approved storage, temperature, sanitation, handling, pickup, or return method.
Record quantities/weights, condition, temperatures where applicable, date/time, responsible employee, and receiving vendor/agency or disposition.
Stop the handoff or reuse when eligibility, food safety, sanitation, container condition, vendor authorization, or documentation cannot be verified.
Clean and restore the collection/storage area after each handoff and control pests, spills, odor, leaks, and employee/guest access.
Reconcile missed pickups, rejected material, waste, contamination, or program exceptions and document corrective action.
The program owner reviews results and vendor/agency performance and adjusts pars, pickup frequency, training, or approved materials as needed.

Verify that food-safety, sanitation, chemical, waste, oil, packaging, and cross-contamination controls take priority over diversion or sustainability goals.
Inspect dedicated containers/storage and labels; remove anything damaged, contaminated, leaking, unidentified, or outside program criteria.
Segregate eligible items at the point of generation so they do not become mixed with trash, chemicals, allergens, unsafe food, or non-approved material.
Perform donation agency pickup verification using the approved storage, temperature, sanitation, handling, pickup, or return method.
Record quantities/weights, condition, temperatures where applicable, date/time, responsible employee, and receiving vendor/agency or disposition.
Stop the handoff or reuse when eligibility, food safety, sanitation, container condition, vendor authorization, or documentation cannot be verified.
Clean and restore the collection/storage area after each handoff and control pests, spills, odor, leaks, and employee/guest access.
Reconcile missed pickups, rejected material, waste, contamination, or program exceptions and document corrective action.
The program owner reviews results and vendor/agency performance and adjusts pars, pickup frequency, training, or approved materials as needed.
sops.checks:
□ Donation Agency Pickup Verification was performed under the current approved restaurant procedure.
□ Required people, equipment, utilities, product, approvals, and records were verified before release or continued operation.
□ Critical readings, identities, handoffs, exceptions, or other evidence required by this procedure were recorded.
□ Unsafe, out-of-standard, unidentified, or undocumented conditions were held, stopped, or escalated instead of informally accepted.
□ Corrective actions and product/equipment/guest/employee disposition were completed and documented when required.
□ The accountable manager or program owner completed final verification and assigned unresolved follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Using an old, generic, or remembered procedure instead of the current approved specialty-operation standard.
• Starting before required permits, approvals, trained people, utilities, equipment, labels, or records are ready.
• Failing to document actual conditions, readings, identities, handoffs, or deviations at the time they occur.
• Continuing service or releasing product/equipment when a required control cannot be verified.
• Treating a vendor, platform, event organizer, sister unit, or outside agency as responsible for controls that still belong to the restaurant.
• Closing the activity without manager verification, record completion, cleanup/restoration, and follow-up ownership.

• Dedicated labeled containers or storage area
• Temperature/condition records when food safety applies
• Pickup/weight/diversion or transfer log
• Cleaning and sanitation supplies for reusable-program equipment
• Approved recipient-agency criteria and transfer documentation

Reconcile missed pickups, rejected material, waste, contamination, or program exceptions and document corrective action.

sourceSections.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for surplus food tracking and diversion reporting so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
sourceSections.appliesTo: Kitchen, food-safety, inventory, receiving, dish, sustainability, and manager teams responsible for donation, waste diversion, recycling, oil, or reusable-container programs.
sourceSections.responsibility: The assigned program owner verifies eligibility, segregation, sanitation, vendor/agency handoff, and records. The manager resolves any food-safety, contamination, vendor, or documentation concern.
sourceSections.whenUsed: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.
sourceSections.materials:
• Approved program criteria and vendor/agency agreement
• Dedicated labeled containers or storage area
• Temperature/condition records when food safety applies
• Pickup/weight/diversion or transfer log
• Cleaning and sanitation supplies for reusable-program equipment
sourceSections.criticalStandards:
• Donation and reuse programs never override food-safety requirements or approved disposition rules.
• Materials are clearly segregated so food, chemicals, waste, oil, recyclables, and reusable containers cannot cross-contaminate.
• Third-party handoffs are documented to the level required by the restaurant’s program and applicable rules.
• Unclear eligibility, contamination, damaged reusable items, or missed controls require hold/disposal rather than informal release.
sourceSections.procedure:
1. Confirm the approved program criteria, participating vendor/agency, eligible material/product, responsible employee, and required record for surplus food tracking and diversion reporting.
2. Verify that food-safety, sanitation, chemical, waste, oil, packaging, and cross-contamination controls take priority over diversion or sustainability goals.
3. Inspect dedicated containers/storage and labels; remove anything damaged, contaminated, leaking, unidentified, or outside program criteria.
4. Segregate eligible items at the point of generation so they do not become mixed with trash, chemicals, allergens, unsafe food, or non-approved material.
5. Perform surplus food tracking and diversion reporting using the approved storage, temperature, sanitation, handling, pickup, or return method.
6. Record quantities/weights, condition, temperatures where applicable, date/time, responsible employee, and receiving vendor/agency or disposition.
7. Stop the handoff or reuse when eligibility, food safety, sanitation, container condition, vendor authorization, or documentation cannot be verified.
8. Clean and restore the collection/storage area after each handoff and control pests, spills, odor, leaks, and employee/guest access.
9. Reconcile missed pickups, rejected material, waste, contamination, or program exceptions and document corrective action.
10. The program owner reviews results and vendor/agency performance and adjusts pars, pickup frequency, training, or approved materials as needed.

sops.title: VIP or Media Visit Service Control SOP
sops.station: Part — Large Events, Seasonal Operations & Crowd Management
sops.frequency: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.
sops.role: The manager on duty owns the event/surge plan, staffing, capacity, safety, and service adjustments. Department leaders execute assigned controls and report deviations immediately.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for vip or media visit service control so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the current approved scope for vip or media visit service control, including date/time, location, guest count or demand assumption, responsible leader, and special commitments.
Review staffing, production, equipment, transport/site, payment, guest-access, safety, and food-safety requirements; assign an owner to each critical control.
Inspect the required area, equipment, supplies, communication method, and backup resources before product or guests arrive.
Stage and label materials in the sequence they will be used; separate guest-specific, event-specific, allergen, payment, and high-risk items as applicable.
Execute vip or media visit service control using the current event/service plan and verify critical handoffs before proceeding to the next phase.
Monitor volume, staffing, timing, food condition, guest flow, and safety; record exceptions and adjust before control is lost.
Escalate shortages, unsafe conditions, late changes, quality failures, or guest commitments the team cannot meet to the event manager immediately.
Complete the guest/client or internal handoff, confirm unresolved items, and document any approved change to the original plan.
Reconcile product, equipment, payments, damage, waste, incidents, and outstanding follow-up; clean and restore the work/site area.
The accountable manager reviews the record, closes open issues, and captures lessons that should change the next comparable event.

• Closing the activity without manager verification, record completion, cleanup/restoration, and follow-up ownership.

sops.title: New Unit Pre-Opening Operational Readiness SOP
sops.station: Part — Multi-Unit Governance, Openings & Temporary Leadership
sops.frequency: Before the applicable operation, service period, event, route, batch, opening, or equipment use, and again after any material condition changes.
sops.role: The designated regional or ownership authority defines decision rights and approves exceptions. Unit managers execute the current controlled standard and document deviations or temporary authority.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for new unit pre-opening operational readiness so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Define the scope, effective date, accountable leader, participating units, and decision authority for new unit pre-opening operational readiness.
Verify the current controlled standard, version, required forms, training evidence, system dependencies, and any legal/permit constraints before implementation.
Document temporary or permanent authority, exceptions, transition risks, unresolved liabilities, and escalation paths in writing.
Brief affected managers and employees on what changes, what does not change, who owns decisions, and what evidence proves adoption.
Execute new unit pre-opening operational readiness according to the approved deployment/transition plan and prevent local workarounds from silently replacing the controlled standard.
Verify implementation through records, observation, audit evidence, training sign-off, and manager acknowledgment—not verbal assurance alone.
Log exceptions and require the authorized owner to approve, time-limit, and review any deviation from the system standard.
Calibrate findings across units/leaders so identical conditions are scored and corrected consistently.
Close transition/opening/coverage actions with evidence and transfer unresolved items to the named owner and due date.
The regional/ownership authority records the final decision and updates controlled standards or support resources when the transition reveals a systemic gap.

sops.frequency: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.
sops.role: The designated system owner controls access, approved configuration, backups, incident escalation, and restoration. Employees use only authorized accounts/devices and immediately report suspicious activity or failure.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for online ordering menu sync verification so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Identify the system/device/data involved in online ordering menu sync verification, its business owner, authorized users, vendor/support contact, and approved fallback method.
Confirm current access rights, device inventory, network/payment boundaries, backup status, support credentials, and required incident records before making changes.
Inspect devices/connections for unexpected changes, tampering, unsupported software, alarms, failed synchronization, or other signs of compromise or loss of control.
Execute online ordering menu sync verification using only approved accounts, devices, settings, networks, storage locations, and vendor/company procedures.
Protect credentials and payment/guest/employee data; do not share passwords, disable security controls, or move protected data into unapproved personal tools.
Record outage/change/inspection time, affected systems, observed condition, actions taken, vendor/ticket information, and any data or operational impact.
On suspected tampering, breach, unauthorized access, or unexplained data loss, stop the affected activity as appropriate and preserve evidence for the authorized incident owner.
Activate the approved offline/manual backup process so critical operations and records continue without bypassing required cash, food-safety, or authorization controls.
Restore or reconnect only after the system owner verifies configuration, security, data integrity/synchronization, and required tests.
Close the incident/change record, rotate or revoke access if required, verify backups, and document prevention actions for recurring failures.

sops.frequency: Whenever this specialty operation is performed and at each required monitoring, handoff, verification, or closeout point defined by the restaurant.
sops.role: The designated system owner controls access, approved configuration, backups, incident escalation, and restoration. Employees use only authorized accounts/devices and immediately report suspicious activity or failure.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for guest wi-fi and operations network separation so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Identify the system/device/data involved in guest wi-fi and operations network separation, its business owner, authorized users, vendor/support contact, and approved fallback method.
Confirm current access rights, device inventory, network/payment boundaries, backup status, support credentials, and required incident records before making changes.
Inspect devices/connections for unexpected changes, tampering, unsupported software, alarms, failed synchronization, or other signs of compromise or loss of control.
Execute guest wi-fi and operations network separation using only approved accounts, devices, settings, networks, storage locations, and vendor/company procedures.
Protect credentials and payment/guest/employee data; do not share passwords, disable security controls, or move protected data into unapproved personal tools.
Record outage/change/inspection time, affected systems, observed condition, actions taken, vendor/ticket information, and any data or operational impact.
On suspected tampering, breach, unauthorized access, or unexplained data loss, stop the affected activity as appropriate and preserve evidence for the authorized incident owner.
Activate the approved offline/manual backup process so critical operations and records continue without bypassing required cash, food-safety, or authorization controls.
Restore or reconnect only after the system owner verifies configuration, security, data integrity/synchronization, and required tests.
Close the incident/change record, rotate or revoke access if required, verify backups, and document prevention actions for recurring failures.
sops.checks:
□ Guest Wi-Fi and Operations Network Separation was performed under the current approved restaurant procedure.
□ Required people, equipment, utilities, product, approvals, and records were verified before release or continued operation.
□ Critical readings, identities, handoffs, exceptions, or other evidence required by this procedure were recorded.
□ Unsafe, out-of-standard, unidentified, or undocumented conditions were held, stopped, or escalated instead of informally accepted.
□ Corrective actions and product/equipment/guest/employee disposition were completed and documented when required.
□ The accountable manager or program owner completed final verification and assigned unresolved follow-up.
sops.correction:
• Using an old, generic, or remembered procedure instead of the current approved specialty-operation standard.
• Starting before required permits, approvals, trained people, utilities, equipment, labels, or records are ready.
• Failing to document actual conditions, readings, identities, handoffs, or deviations at the time they occur.
• Continuing service or releasing product/equipment when a required control cannot be verified.
• Treating a vendor, platform, event organizer, sister unit, or outside agency as responsible for controls that still belong to the restaurant.
• Closing the activity without manager verification, record completion, cleanup/restoration, and follow-up ownership.

Review required labels, ingredients, equipment, monitoring tools, service/display limits, rotation method, and corrective-action rules.

Stage product in controlled quantities, maintain required segregation, and attach identity/date/allergen or handling information before display/use.

The manager reviews the monitoring record and recurring deviations before the next service period.

sourceSections.procedure:

8. Replenish only from approved protected stock and keep the station orderly so employees can see age, condition, and ownership of product.

10. The manager reviews the monitoring record and recurring deviations before the next service period.

sops.title: Shared Commercial Kitchen Opening and Space Handoff SOP
sops.station: Part — Shared Kitchens, Pop-Ups & Remote Service Venues
sops.frequency: Before the applicable operation, service period, event, route, batch, opening, or equipment use, and again after any material condition changes.
sops.role: The designated operation lead owns the space handoff, segregation, temporary setup, service controls, and restoration. The manager escalates facility, co-tenant, contamination, access, or authority issues.
sops.purpose: To establish a controlled, repeatable, and verifiable process for shared commercial kitchen opening and space handoff so specialty operations do not depend on improvisation, undocumented exceptions, or unassigned responsibility.
steps: Confirm the written scope for shared commercial kitchen opening and space handoff, including site owner, available space/equipment/utilities, operating times, access rules, permits, and restoration obligations.
Walk the site before setup and document cleanliness, damage, pest evidence, utilities, storage, handwashing, warewashing, refrigeration/hot holding, waste, lighting, and safe access.
Assign and label the restaurant’s food, chemicals, smallwares, equipment, cold/dry storage, and personal items so ownership remains clear in the shared/temporary environment.
Establish handwashing, sanitation, allergen, food-protection, waste, security, and employee/guest-flow controls before food preparation or service begins.

Perform shared commercial kitchen opening and space handoff within the approved footprint and prevent co-tenant or venue activity from contaminating, displacing, or compromising the restaurant’s operation.
Monitor utilities, storage, product condition, access, co-tenant activity, and sanitation throughout service and document any shared-space incident.
Stop or relocate the affected activity if safe food handling, sanitation, utilities, segregation, or site security cannot be maintained.
At handoff/closeout, reconcile food/equipment, remove waste and chemicals, clean/sanitize assigned areas, and restore the site as required.
Document damage, contamination, missing property, shared-storage disputes, or facility defects and notify the site owner/manager promptly.
The operation lead completes the space-handoff record and blocks the next use until unresolved critical defects are corrected.

• Continuing service or releasing product/equipment when a required control cannot be verified.
• Treating a vendor, platform, event organizer, sister unit, or outside agency as responsible for controls that still belong to the restaurant.
• Closing the activity without manager verification, record completion, cleanup/restoration, and follow-up ownership.
